The events route never filters by cin, and live /v1/company/X/events returns the same list as the sample CIN. GET /v1/instruments/880(E)/affected gives obligations ['CA13-S2-85-SMALL'] only. checker/feeds/ibbi.py and ofac_sdn.py are feed modules with no route (PLAN_17:470 'scheduled watchers', unbuilt). operations.py:361 notes that Gazette listings don't name the instrument. Main.dc.html watchRaw[0].path; Sentence and Guided watch rows.
findings.recommendation: Watch v1 should show only /v1/company/{cin}/events items, with the output_class badge (VERIFIED_FACT / DETERMINISTIC_CONSEQUENCE / SIGNAL), both dates ('at' and 'known_at'), and the _V0_SCOPE sentence shown verbatim. The impact chain should come only from /affected. Show counterparty and sanctions checks as not yet available until M5/M8 ship.

findings.issue: The Drafts screen has no route, and its behaviour does not match drafting.py. The engine implements one template, the AGM notice; the mockups draft a board-meeting notice. approve() requires a named reviewer, while the mockups approve anonymously. The slot legend invents a 'company record' source, although no registry feed exists (it would be USER_FACT). The notice states 'sent at least seven days ahead' with no send date on record. As far as I found, no engine code computes the s.173 120-day next-meeting date (14 Oct 2026).
findings.evidence: checker/drafting.py docstring 'Only ONE template is implemented -- the AGM notice'; Draft.approve raises 'approval requires a named reviewer'. provenance_slots slot types: SOURCE_QUOTE, USER_FACT, DERIVED_FACT, TEMPLATE_TEXT, MODEL_SUGGESTION, UNKNOWN. api.py's route list has no draft route. A grep of obligations.py for '120' or 'next due' found no gap-to-next-meeting calculation (I did not search the rest of the package exhaustively). Main.dc.html draft legend 'Solid line · from the company record'; approveHelp 'The record keeps who approved it' with no reviewer field.
findings.recommendation: Demo the AGM notice from drafting.py, and map the underline legend one-to-one to the six slot types (dashed = UNKNOWN, double = DERIVED_FACT with its working, gold = SOURCE_QUOTE verified against the text). Add a reviewer-name field to Approve, and add the backend draft route before the screen ships.

findings.issue: State names don't match the engine, or each other. The engine keeps APPLIES_UNDETERMINED (it applies, a fact is missing) separate from CANNOT_DETERMINE (applicability itself is unknown). The mockups file s.149(3), a missing-fact case, under '? Can't tell'. A and B say '! Not met yet / … Not known yet' while C says '! Needs action / … Comes later'. The website uses 'Undetermined / Cannot determine'. The legend defines NOT_SATISFIED as 'needs action' rather than a finding of breach. Document checks invent five labels over the engine's three buckets.
findings.evidence: obligations.ROW_STATES (5). Live s.149(3) with no days supplied is APPLIES_UNDETERMINED. placedon-claude-legal-3300/src/app/product/compliance-pack/page.tsx:28-30 labels. Main.dc.html L and DL maps; Guided.dc.html L and K maps; Sentence.dc.html L. contract.md:349 proposes 'Not held' for out_of_scope (the mockups' Ask labels are fine).
findings.recommendation: Freeze one label table keyed by ROW_STATES and use it on the site and in all mockups. Keep 'missing a fact' and 'missing a rule' visibly separate: show the missing_facts text for the first and the blocked_by rule name for the second. For document checks, use the engine's three buckets.

findings.issue: The engine returns things the UI never shows. Missing everywhere: the law_version statement ('current consolidation, not point-in-time'), figure evidence_state and source_url, what_this_is and what_it_is_not, coverage.sentence and the unchecked list, cited_spans sha256, the summary counts, the scope sentence ('1 of 9 in-scope bodies of law are held') and blocked_by rule ids. A shows '9 of 15' duties and hides exactly the six rows (s.185, 186, 188, 180, 184, 203) that are all UNDETERMINED or CANNOT_DETERMINE, which makes the sheet look greener than it is. No mockup has a screen for /v1/mca-strip, though its data is not wired yet.
findings.evidence: api.compliance_pack return keys (summary, rows[].cited_spans, unverified, law_currency_watch, what_it_is_not). /v1/ask keys observed: law_version, scope, evidence_pack, demand_signal, what_it_is_not. Main.dc.html line 205 'Showing 9 of the 15 duties'.
findings.recommendation: Show all 15 rows, sorted with NEEDS_ATTENTION first, with the summary counts in the header. Add a short provenance footer (law_version statement, scope sentence, what this is not). Show evidence_state on every figure.

strengths_worth_keeping: A's Company duties table with a detail panel (What we found / Still needed / The rule) maps almost one-to-one onto _row_json (basis, missing_facts, provision/cited_spans). It is the easiest surface to wire to POST /v1/compliance-pack.
All three model the Ask states as answered / partly answered / not held, with no confidence field anywhere, consistent with ask_contract STATES and FORBIDDEN_KEYS ('confidence', 'coverage').
The FEMA out_of_scope sample matches the live route: POST /v1/ask returns state=out_of_scope, body.key=FEMA1999, scope_status=DECLARED, with the register's reason.
Blanks locking approval matches drafting.py's rule that UNKNOWN or MODEL_SUGGESTION slots block approve(); worth keeping once the reviewer name and slot-type legend are fixed.

B's idea that the same question gives different figures on different dates is backed for thresholds: live as_of 2025-08-14 returns 700(E) ₹4 cr and today returns 880(E) ₹10 cr. It is the product's strongest demo, if limited to what the engine covers.
The document check's 'law it relied on, then vs now' framing matches document_check's governed_then / governs_now superseded output.
reviews.preferred_direction: A as the shell, with the samples regenerated from real compliance-pack, ask and document-check output, C's glossary panel, and a narrow B-style date control on figures only. A is the only layout whose screens match existing routes one-to-one; C's step list makes up engine stages, and B's free date travel breaks PLAN_13 §9.
open_questions: Will the backend expose checker/agm.py's AGM deadline, and a board-meeting next-due calculation, as a figure or row on a route? Without that, no mockup's headline deadline can be produced.

Is PLAN_13 §9 (as_of today only) to be amended for Phase C? If so, who owns the per-key coverage floors (e.g. s.2(85) before 15-Sep-2022 gives ThresholdUnavailable) and the rule that a figure's effective_from may not be later than as_of?

Should the copy call 880(E)'s CORROBORATED state (a named human attestation plus automated gazette-copy corroboration, per operator_note) 'checked against the Gazette', or does the product want a stricter word?
Are routes for drafts, Watch (IBBI/OFAC/deadlines) and file-based document forensics in scope for beta (PLAN_17 M8/M10), or should these screens ship labelled as not yet available?

Should document-check narrow its checks to the obligations a given document relies on? Today it flags s.2(85) as superseded for every document dated before Dec 2025, which will read as noise on an AGM notice.

My live runs used a scratch copy patched for Python 3.9 (from __future__ annotations, .git excluded), so /v1/health's provenance_error seen there is likely an artifact of the copy, not a real defect. It should be re-checked on the real checkout under the project's Python.

reviews.summary: None of the three mockups uses a banned word or a gradient, glass or blob trope. All three share one chip() palette that breaks two binding rules in AGENTS.md: gold-muted #9F743B, which is for citations only, marks the "Not met / Needs action" status, and Cool Grey #5B6472, which is for abstention only, is used on non-abstention elements. None of them uses the brand's own word "Abstained", and none has a "Request a pilot" path. B holds the brand best. It uses the site's dark ink shell with answers on cream paper (PLAN_13 §27), has exactly one Brass Gold element (the timeline "you are here" cursor), and its point-in-time idea is the brand promise ("the date that law took effect") made visible. A is a competent but generic SaaS dashboard, and it breaks the accent rule on several screens. C has no Brass Gold at all, so it is on-palette but carries no brand signature, and its copy is the most chatty and the least like a judgment ("the way you'd ask a colleague").

findings.issue: Gold-muted #9F743B, which is reserved for citations, is used as a status colour. The 'Not met yet / Needs action / Law has changed / Potential issue' chip uses it, so the citation signature is spent on warnings. Several of these chips on one screen also give that screen more than one gold-family accent.
findings.evidence: The same chip() in Main.dc.html:336, Sentence.dc.html chip() and Guided.dc.html chip() has notmet: 'background: #FBF3E2; color: #6E4A17; border: 1.5px solid #9F743B'. AGENTS.md:14 says '--gold-muted #9F743B for citations only'. A's Company duties screen shows the gold nav bar (Main.dc.html:357 'inset 3px 0 0 #C9A24B') plus a gold-muted chip on the s.96(1) row. C's Documents result has three gold-muted chips in one panel.
findings.recommendation: Re-token 'needs action' in ink only: a solid 2px ink border with a bold '!' glyph and a heavier word (for example 'Action required'). Keep #9F743B only for citation underlines, as the Draft screens already use it (Main.dc.html:297-298). Add a lint rule that bans #9F743B outside a .cite class.

findings.issue: Cool Grey #5B6472, which is reserved for abstained/unknown, is used on elements that are not abstention. This weakens the one colour that has to mean 'we abstain'.
findings.evidence: Main.dc.html:52 draws the 'Sample data · not a real company' badge with 'border: 1px dashed #5B6472'. Main.dc.html:274 wraps the Watch 'What to do:' box in a dashed #5B6472 border, including for the AGM deadline, which is a deterministic action rather than an unknown. Guided.dc.html uses a dashed #5B6472 card for the 'Other laws: FEMA, SEBI, IBC and more' roadmap tile, which is closer to marketing a roadmap than to an abstention. AGENTS.md:14-15 says 'reserved only for the abstained / unknown state — never decorative'. PLAN_13 §27 adds 'Dashed = abstention, as on the site'.
findings.recommendation: Use a neutral warm-grey solid border for the sample-data badge and the 'What to do' box. B and C already show the badge in cream on the dark header. Keep the dashed rule plus Cool Grey for '? Can't tell', '□ Not held' and blank draft slots only. Make the FEMA card a neutral note, or show it as the actual Not-held answer state.

findings.issue: The brand's abstention vocabulary is missing. The site and PLAN_13 say 'Abstained', and the mockups say 'Can't tell', 'Not held', 'Partly answered' and 'Can't confirm'. PLAN_13 §27 explicitly replaced 'Partly answered' with 'Abstained in part'. The four product answer classes that the site shows (Verified fact / Determined / Signal, not asserted / Abstained) do not appear at all.
findings.evidence: grep -ci 'abstain' returns 0 for all three files. Main.dc.html:393 and Sentence.dc.html SL = { partial: '◧ Partly answered' }. PLAN_13_ASSISTANT_UX.md §27 table: '"Partly answered" → "Abstained in part"'. AGENTS.md:28 lists 'abstains' under 'Words in'. placedon-claude-legal-3300/src/components/surfaces/surface-shell.tsx:77-92 defines the class labels.
findings.recommendation: Adopt one state lexicon across the site, the backend and the app. Suggested: Answered / Abstained in part / Abstained (Not held), with glyphs ■ ◧ □. Obligation rows keep the engine's own row states. Plain-language glosses such as 'we need more before we can say' can stay in the legend, but the badge word must be the brand word.

findings.issue: Mono is not applied to every section, instrument, figure and date. It is applied in labelled slots, but whenever a citation or date appears in running prose, headlines or titles it falls back to sans or Fraunces. That is exactly where the 'mono citations are the brand signature' rule matters most.
findings.evidence: Main.dc.html:396 has the headline 'By 30 Sep 2026.' in Fraunces, the body in sans containing '31 Mar 2026', and figBasis 'Worked out from s.96(1)' in sans. The Watch titles 'G.S.R. 880(E): small-company limits revised' are in sans. The tile reads 'Last allowed date 30 Sep 2026'. Sentence.dc.html timelineNote ('On 14 Aug 2025 ... G.S.R. 700(E) ... G.S.R. 880(E)') and the timeline sub-labels '2021 · limits revised' are in sans. Guided.dc.html row text 'Hold the AGM by 30 Sep 2026' and headline 'Your AGM is due by 30 Sep 2026' are in sans or serif. AGENTS.md:16-17 says 'IBM Plex Mono (every section reference..., figure..., instrument..., and date)'.
findings.recommendation: Stop hand-styling. Render all copy through a tokeniser that wraps s.NNN(n), G.S.R./S.O. numbers, ₹ figures, day counts that are statutory figures, and DD-Mon-YYYY dates in a <cite-mono> span. The mockups already keep these as strings in renderVals(), so this is a mechanical fix.

findings.issue: There is no Brass Gold #C9A24B anywhere in C, so it has no brand accent element. C is on-palette but anonymous, and it could be any cream-coloured SaaS product. It also spends the ink-fill emphasis on four competing things at once: the current step, the 'Check it' button, black '✓ Met/Done' chips and outlined glossary terms.
findings.evidence: The colour count for Guided.dc.html has #C9A24B = 0. The active step has 'background: #0C0C0D' and the Next button has 'background: #0C0C0D'. Met chips are black-filled, and in step 2 even process steps such as 'Looked up the 15 duties' get a black '✓ Done' chip. AGENTS.md:13 says 'Accent = Brass Gold ... ONE accent element per view'. DESIGN_SYSTEM.md §1 says 'if a screen has more than one accent-colored element, the design has failed'.
findings.recommendation: Give C one gold element per view, preferably the current-step marker (a 3px gold top rule on the active step), and make the step fill cream-on-ink outline instead of solid. Show process checklist items as plain ink tick text, not the same chip as a verified legal state.

findings.issue: The 'met/verified' chip is the heaviest mark on the page (solid ink), and it is reused for things that are not verified facts: a sanctions no-match, a completed process step, and a statute quote in the Ask result. This contradicts the honesty rule that answer classes must be distinguishable, and it makes a SIGNAL look like a VERIFIED_FACT.
findings.evidence: Main.dc.html watchRaw: OFAC no match → ck 'met' → '✓ Checked', styled the same as '✓ Met'. Sentence.dc.html watch does the same. Guided.dc.html task 04 has row('met','26 Sep 2026','No sanctions match...'), and task 02 has row('met','s.96(1)','“…within a period of six months...”'), which prints '✓ Met' next to a quote. The site's surface-shell.tsx:86 labels this class 'Signal, not asserted'. The backend's event_log output classes are VERIFIED_FACT / DETERMINISTIC_CONSEQUENCE / SIGNAL (per the task brief; I did not re-verify the enum names in checker/event_log.py for this review).
findings.recommendation: Map every chip to a backend output class plus a state. Watch items from IBBI or OFAC must carry 'Signal, not asserted'. Ask results carry the Ask state (■ Answered), not the obligation state '✓ Met'. Save the heaviest visual weight for 'needs action', not for 'met'.

findings.issue: Voice drifts into onboarding and sales register. Several lines would never appear in a judgment, and humility is repeated on every screen when the brand allows it once, in abstention.
findings.evidence: Main.dc.html:74 'New here? Here is everything Placedon does', :75 'Five tools, one rule', the 'Try it' buttons, :139 'Was this useful?', and :61 'What needs your attention'. The first-person 'we' humility ('We won’t guess this one.', 'We can’t tell yet, so we won’t mark this as met.') repeats across rows. AGENTS.md:24-29 says 'Claim, then evidence... would this appear in a judgment?... humility appears once — in abstention'.
findings.recommendation: Cut the feature-tour section, or reduce it to a one-line index. Write rows as a claim followed by a basis ('Abstained. Requires: days in India per director (s.149(3)).'). Remove 'Was this useful?' from the evidence card, or move it outside the answer artefact.

findings.issue: The copy in C is the least on-voice of the three. It is conversational and task-coach in register, and it says 'You decide' in one place and 'Your result' in another for the same step.
findings.evidence: Guided.dc.html: h1 'What do you need to do today?'. 'Type your question the way you’d ask a colleague.' 'Plain words are fine.' 'You tell us a little.' The home how-it-works card labels step 3 'You decide', while stepNames labels it 'Your result'. The Watch result is 'Four things happened that touch this company.'
findings.recommendation: Keep C's structure but rewrite it in the house register: 'Facts / Check / Result'. Use the headline 'Obligations for Sample Company Pvt Ltd as of 26-Sep-2026'. Use one name per step everywhere.

findings.issue: B's signature sentence is set in italic Fraunces 300. The business-plan design system bans italics because they 'read as uncertain'. Dotted underlines are also used both for 'editable slot' in the sentence and for 'you typed it' in the draft legend, so one mark means two things.
findings.evidence: Sentence.dc.html slotStyle(): 'font-style: italic; text-decoration-style: dotted'. DESIGN_SYSTEM.md §3 says 'Never italicize except input placeholders — italics read as uncertain'. The draft uses 'border-bottom: 2px dotted #0C0C0D' for user-typed text. PLAN_13 §27 says 'The same mark cannot mean two things across the product'.
findings.recommendation: Set the slots in roman Fraunces with a solid 1px cream underline plus a small caret glyph. Keep dotted for user-supplied facts only. AGENTS.md does not ban italics, so the brand owner must rule on whether the DESIGN_SYSTEM ban survives into the 3300 system.

findings.issue: There are sub-minimum type and low-contrast labels on dark: the timeline sub-labels are 11px at 60% cream opacity. The mockup also presents specific instrument numbers (G.S.R. 92(E) 2021, G.S.R. 700(E) 2022, G.S.R. 880(E) 2025) as history. If any of these is wrong, it breaks 'never invent an instrument'.
findings.evidence: Sentence.dc.html timeline: '<span style="font-size: 11px; color: rgba(244,239,230,0.6)">'. DESIGN_SYSTEM.md §3 says 'no font size below 12px'. I believe G.S.R. 92(E) (Feb 2021) and G.S.R. 700(E) (Sep 2022) did revise the small-company limits. I am not certain of G.S.R. 880(E) or its December 2025 date, and I have not checked any of them against corpus/.
findings.recommendation: Use at least 12px and at least 4.5:1 contrast, in mono. Before the design is shown externally, source every instrument on the timeline from the backend corpus index, or show '[instrument unverified]' in the abstain style.

findings.issue: The brand assets and tokens are not used. The mockups use a generic document-icon SVG (A) or a text-only wordmark (B, C) instead of brand-kit/logo, a 4-6px radius instead of the site's --radius: 3px, and Google-hosted fonts. There is no 'Request a pilot' path, which matters if these screens are used in a demo or at a pilot stage.
findings.evidence: Main.dc.html:26 uses an svg rect plus lines as the logo, but placedon-claude-legal-3300/brand-kit/logo/ contains gold, white and navy PNGs. globals.css:19 has '--radius: 3px'. The mockups use border-radius 6 (19× in A). PLAN_13 §27 says 'Kept stricter than the site: 3px radius'. grep for 'pilot' returns 0 in all three files. AGENTS.md:33 says 'Primary CTA: Request a pilot'.
findings.recommendation: Use the white-on-ink logo in the dark header or sidebar and a 3px radius token. In a pre-launch, sample-data app, add a quiet 'Request a pilot' link beside the Sample data badge, as a text link and not a second accent.

findings.issue: Mono is used on non-citation numbering, which dilutes the signature. Row numbers ('01'...'05') and ref-column words ('Type', 'Missing', 'Record', 'Blank', 'You') are set in IBM Plex Mono, so mono no longer reliably means 'this is a citation'.
findings.evidence: Main.dc.html:79 sets f.n ('01') in mono. Guided.dc.html sets t.n/t.tool ('01 · Company duties'), 'Not yet' and r.ref values 'Type' / 'Missing' / 'Blank' / 'You' in mono.
findings.recommendation: Keep mono for statutory references, instruments, figures and dates only, and set row labels in sans small caps. The ref column should hold a citation or stay empty.

strengths_worth_keeping: B's dark ink shell with answers on cream paper already matches PLAN_13 §27 and the live site (layout.tsx dark shell, .ddoc-paper); A's cream-page-plus-dark-sidebar and C's light page do not.
B's single Brass Gold element (the timeline 'you are here' cursor, a thin 2px line) is the textbook application of 'one accent, at most 10%'.

B's point-in-time timeline shows the brand promise ('the date that law took effect') directly, with a dashed marker for the unverified G.S.R. 880(E) that correctly means 'abstention'. It is the most distinctive brand device in any of the three.

The draft provenance legend in A and B (solid = company record, dotted = you typed it, double = worked out from the law, gold-muted = section of the Act, dashed grey = blank) is correct brand usage of gold-muted and abstain-grey, and it matches PLAN_13's double-rule decision.
Every status chip leads with a glyph and a word (✓ ! … – ?), so the states survive grayscale and meet the no-colour-only rule.
None of the three files uses a banned word, a gradient, glassmorphism or emoji, and radii stay at or below 6px.
reviews.preferred_direction: A hybrid with B as the frame: B's dark ink shell, one-gold-cursor and as-of timeline as the brand signature, carrying C's glossary and step clarity inside the paper sheet and A's duty table as the Duties view. Before any of it ships, re-token the shared chip() so it follows the gold-muted-for-citations-only and Cool-Grey-for-abstention-only rules, and use the Abstained lexicon.
open_questions: Which design system governs the product: placedon-claude-legal-3300 (dark ink, Brass Gold, Cool Grey abstain, 3px radius) or bp/docs/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md (Parchment, Slate accent #475569, Caution #8B4513, Playfair, JetBrains Mono, no italics, ≤200ms)? PLAN_13 §27 treats 3300 as the system of record, but its open decision 1 says the founder has not yet confirmed that.

Is 'needs action' a legitimate status that deserves colour? If it is, which token does it get, given that Slate/Caution are retired, gold-muted is for citations only and the palette allows no second accent?
Date convention: the mockups use '26 Sep 2026', PLAN_13 uses DD-Mon-YYYY ('26-Sep-2026') and the site uses formatIST ('11 Sept 2026'). Which one wins (PLAN_13 open decision 3)?
Should the logged-in app use the dark shell (site parity, as B does) or the light paper (Word pane, as A and C do)? Status hues fail contrast on ink, per PLAN_13 §27.
Does the ban on italics from DESIGN_SYSTEM.md §3 survive into the 3300 system? B's sentence depends on the answer.
Are OFAC and IBBI watch feeds in scope for the brand promise ('Companies Act, 2013' only)? If they are not, A, B and C all show out-of-scope sources as though they were live.

reviews.role: Legal accuracy and honesty auditor (Indian company law)
reviews.summary: All three mockups get the plain statutory numbers right: 6 months or 15 months for the AGM under s.96(1), 120 days, four meetings and 7 days' notice under s.173, 2 directors and 182 days under s.149, and the Rs 500 cr / 1000 cr / 5 cr CSR limits in s.135(1). They also match the s.96(1) quotes in the corpus word for word. The legal logic built on those numbers is wrong in places. Three problems stand out. (1) Every mockup marks s.173 'Met' after only three meetings. The backend would never return that for this company: it declines while small-company status is unknown (s.173(5)), and with 3 meetings its count floor fails. (2) Every mockup gives a false reason for not answering: it says G.S.R. 880(E) 'hasn't been checked against the Gazette' (and B says 700(E) is 'waiting for review'). The backend records both as VERIFIED_INSTRUMENT, with the eGazette copy byte-identical. (3) B's date-travel and the 'then/now' document checks in A and B claim the Act's text as it stood on a past date, which the backend explicitly cannot do (point_in_time_verified is false; the corpus is an 18-Aug-2026 consolidation). A is the most honest ('Showing 9 of the 15 duties'). C adds 'Checked each section is in force' and 'every duty we checked' claims the engine cannot back. B's central idea rests on something the engine does not have.

findings.issue: s.173(1) is marked '✓ Met' with only three board meetings, while small-company status is 'Can't tell'. This is legally wrong and contradicts the backend.
findings.evidence: Main.dc.html rowsRaw: {sec:'s.173(1)', st:'met', finding:'Three meetings held this year...next must be held by 14 Oct 2026'}. Sentence.dc.html dutiesToday has ['met','s.173(1)'...]. Guided.dc.html has row('met','s.173(1)','Board meetings on track'). By the corpus text (s.173(1)), four meetings are required 'every year', so with three held the count limb is at best undecided until the year ends. s.173(5) says a small company is deemed compliant with one meeting in each half-year and a gap of at least 90 days, so which regime applies depends on s.2(85). The mockups show s.2(85) as 'Can't tell' two rows lower. Backend checker/obligations.py _decide_board returns None ('the s.173(5) regime depends on small-company status, which cannot be determined'), and checker/s173_slice.py fails any count below MIN_MEETINGS_PER_YEAR=4. The legend defines 'Met' as 'Checked and satisfied'. The README also says the engine 'never claims an obligation was complied with unless every limb... has been decided'.
findings.recommendation: Change s.173 to '… Not known yet' or '? Can't tell'. Name both open limbs: the 4th meeting due by 31 Dec 2026, and whether the s.173(5) regime applies depending on s.2(85). Keep the 120-day date as a separate 'next meeting by' fact, not as a pass. Build a rule into the copy: no row may be 'Met' while a row it depends on is 'Can't tell'.

findings.issue: The reason given for abstaining on small-company status is false against the backend. The mockups say G.S.R. 880(E) is unchecked against the Gazette (and B says G.S.R. 700(E) awaits review), but the backend holds and attests both.
findings.evidence: A: 'G.S.R. 880(E). Its text hasn't yet been checked against the Gazette'; the Watch item says 'reported but not yet checked against the official Gazette'. B timelineNote: 'Its text is not yet checked against the Gazette, so the marker is dashed'; past mode: 'G.S.R. 700(E). Our copy of it is waiting for a person to review it'. C: 'Two rules we depend on are not yet confirmed: G.S.R. 880(E)...'. Backend corpus/sources/gsr880e_registration.json: classification 'VERIFIED_INSTRUMENT', status 'CORROBORATED', corroborating_copy egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2025/268124.pdf match 'identical', verbatim_clause_checked_by 'NS' 2026-09-10, operative clause Rs 10 cr / Rs 100 cr. research/TASKS.md S-002: 700(E) 'HELD and ATTESTED since 04-09-2026' and corroborated from the Gazette. checker/prescribed_thresholds.py serves 700(E) for 15-09-2022 to 30-11-2025 and 880(E) from 01-12-2025. Caveat: the Gazette match was automated ('not a human check'), and the founder's download provenance is null. The honest wording is therefore 'attested; Gazette copy matched automatically', not 'not checked'. The backend README line 41 ('refuses, naming G.S.R. 700(E)') is itself stale.
findings.recommendation: Rebuild the s.2(85) example from what the engine actually outputs today. Most likely it now resolves using 10 cr / 100 cr, provided the proviso facts (holding, subsidiary, s.8, special Act) are known. If a live abstention example is needed, use s.177/Rule 6 or s.203 (KMP Rules not held). An abstention that states a false reason is as dishonest as a wrong answer.

findings.issue: B's main interaction, 'the law as it stood on [date]', claims point-in-time statutory text that the engine explicitly cannot produce. A and B's document checks ('s.96 was in force in this form on 01 Jun 2024' ✓ Verified) make the same unsupported claim.
findings.evidence: Sentence.dc.html: date tray 'The law as it stood on which date?'; sources 'Companies Act, 2013 · as in force 14 Aug 2025'; doc check 'Same law, on the date you chose ✓ Verified: Unchanged on 14 Aug 2025'. Main.dc.html docs: 'Law it relies on, then ✓ Verified: s.96 was in force in this form on 01 Jun 2024' and summary '✓ Law still current'. Backend docs/PLAN_13_ASSISTANT_UX.md (around line 843): 'as_of is today, and only today, in v1. The engine has no point-in-time capability (law_version.point_in_time_verified is false; ...no statement here is a statement about the law as it stood on any past date)'. It also calls a past as_of a breach of the CLAUDE.md non-negotiable. The only dated history the engine has is the prescribed-threshold chain (700(E) to 880(E)) and amendment footnotes in the India Code consolidation (for s.96, only the 2018 amendment to s.96(2) at 13-6-2018).
findings.recommendation: Allow date travel only for figures the engine can date: the s.2(85) thresholds and s.137/s.92 deadline arithmetic. For section text, show the currency line the spec requires ('Text as ingested 18-Aug-2026. Current consolidation, not a point-in-time version.'). Replace 'was in force in this form on 01 Jun 2024 ✓ Verified' with something like 'No amendment to s.96(1) is recorded in our consolidation after 01 Jun 2024', using a neutral chip. If B is chosen, its date slot must refuse or grey out section text before coverage.

findings.issue: 'AGM due by 30 Sep 2026' is labelled '■ Answered' / 'Last allowed date' but ignores the 15-month limb, which may produce an earlier date. The mockups never ask for the previous AGM date.
findings.evidence: s.96(1) corpus text: 'not more than fifteen months shall elapse between the date of one annual general meeting... and that of the next' AND 'within a period of six months, from the date of closing of the financial year'. The binding date is whichever falls earlier. If the FY2024-25 AGM was held on 20 Jun 2025, the 15-month limit is 20 Sep 2026, so the company is already in default. A's own basis text quotes the 15-month rule, yet the figure is 'Worked out from s.96(1): six months after 31 Mar 2026'. Guided.dc.html Ask step 1 asks only for the question. The backend _decide_agm returns undetermined with 'only one AGM date is on record; the fifteen-month gap needs the previous one', and it does not decide the Registrar's 3-month extension limb (third proviso).
findings.recommendation: State the answer as 'By 30 Sep 2026 under the six-month limb, or earlier if your last AGM was before 30 Jun 2025', with the Ask state set to Partly answered and 'Date of last AGM' listed as missing. Or collect the last AGM date in onboarding. Mention the s.96(1) third proviso (ROC extension of up to 3 months) as not decided.

findings.issue: The s.137(1) and s.92(4) filing rows say the deadline 'counts from the date of the AGM, which isn't set yet'. That omits the statutory fallback that applies when no AGM is held, which is the exact situation shown on screen.
findings.evidence: A rowsRaw s.137(1)/s.92(4): 'The deadline counts from the date of the AGM, which isn't set yet.' B and C say the same. Corpus s.137(2): if no AGM is held, file 'within thirty days of the last date before which the annual general meeting should have been held' (here 30 Oct 2026). s.92(4): 'within sixty days from the date on which the annual general meeting should have been held' (29 Nov 2026). The backend _decide_annual_return implements this second limb and says in its docstring that it is 'the one a company in default most needs and most often misses'.
findings.recommendation: Show outer deadlines now: AOC-4 by 30 Oct 2026 at the latest and MGT-7 by 29 Nov 2026 at the latest, counted from 30 Sep 2026 if no AGM is held, and earlier if the AGM is held earlier. A lawyer would treat the current text as an omission of the most useful fact.

findings.issue: Scope overclaims: the copy says 'See every duty the Act gives it', but the engine covers 15 obligations. C's result says 'Below is every duty we checked' but lists 7 rows.
findings.evidence: Main.dc.html features: 'See every duty the Act gives it, and which ones are met.' (it does correctly say 'Showing 9 of the 15 duties Placedon checks today' on the duties screen). Guided.dc.html task 01 blurb has the same 'every duty the Act gives it', and its result sub says 'Below is every duty we checked' with 7 rows, after step 2 claims 'Looked up the 15 duties'. Sentence.dc.html hint: 'Every duty the Act gives a company'. checker/obligations.py registers 15 IDs, including s.185, s.186, s.188, s.180, s.184 and s.203, none of which appear in C.
findings.recommendation: Use 'the 15 duties Placedon checks today' everywhere and link to the full list. In C, render all 15, or say 'Showing 7 of 15. 8 more below.' Never imply the whole Act is covered.

findings.issue: Step 2 'We check' ticks '✓ Done' for verifications the engine does not perform, and says no instrument needs citing, which undercuts the product's own promise.
findings.evidence: Guided.dc.html task 01: chk('done','Checked each section is in force as of 26 Sep 2026'). Task 02: chk('done','Confirmed s.96(1) is in force as of today') and chk('skip','No notification has changed this rule since, so none is cited'). The engine holds an India Code consolidation fetched 2026-08-18 (corpus JSON fetched_at) and has no in-force verification (point_in_time_verified false). The product promise is to show 'the notification that set its wording, and the date it took effect'. For s.96(1) that is the commencement notification (1 Apr 2014, S.O. 902(E) of 26 Mar 2014, if my recollection is right; please verify against corpus/sources/commencement, since I did not confirm s.96's entry). C says nothing is cited instead.
findings.recommendation: Replace the ticks with what actually happened: 'Read s.96(1) from our copy of the Act (India Code, fetched 18 Aug 2026)'. Show the commencement instrument and date for the section, or say 'commencement instrument not held' as a visible gap.

findings.issue: The Watch/sanctions tile shows '✓ Checked: no match' against OFAC only. For an Indian company that is a misleading compliance signal, and the backend has no sanctions or IBBI module.
findings.evidence: A watchRaw: 'Sanctions list checked: no match for 3 counterparties' ✓ Checked, 'compared with the US Treasury's OFAC list'. B and C carry the same row with a met-style chip. A grep for 'ofac' in the backend returns nothing. The IBBI name match has no SIGNAL labelling, although the backend (event_log.py) and web contract classes separate VERIFIED_FACT, DETERMINISTIC_CONSEQUENCE and SIGNAL. An Indian lawyer would expect the UNSC consolidated list and MHA designations under UAPA s.51A and s.35 before OFAC. A clean OFAC result says nothing about Indian-law exposure.
findings.recommendation: Remove sanctions and IBBI from the pre-launch mockups, or show them explicitly as 'Not built'. If kept, name the lists in the chip ('OFAC SDN only: no match'), never use the 'Met/Checked' visual, and label the IBBI item as a Signal, not a finding.

findings.issue: Document checks use '✓ Verified' for things that are not verifications, and scanned-document reading contradicts the plan's decision to cut document parsing.
findings.evidence: Main.dc.html DL.ok = '✓ Verified'. It is applied to 'What it is: A notice calling an annual general meeting. It says so on its face.' A document's self-description is not verification. C does the same: row('met','Type','A board resolution. It says so on its face.'). bp/docs/UX_INTERACTION_SPEC.md line 213: 'Client manager / document upload: Cut. Document parsing was rejected on measured evidence'. C says the date is 'Read from the page'.
findings.recommendation: Keep 'Verified' for VERIFIED_FACT rows backed by a held source. Use 'Identified as' for document type. Do not show OCR or scanned-page reading until it exists.

findings.issue: The s.2(85) timeline is incomplete and mislabels how verified its steps are.
findings.evidence: Sentence.dc.html marks: 2014 's.2(85) in force', 'G.S.R. 92(E) 2021 · limits revised' (solid, i.e. presented as held), 700(E), and 880(E) (dashed). The backend holds no G.S.R. 92(E): prescribed_thresholds.py covers only 700(E) from 15-09-2022 and 880(E) from 01-12-2025, so pre-Sept-2022 dates refuse. The timeline also leaves out the statutory amendment by Act 1 of 2018, s.2 (w.e.f. 9-2-2018), which raised the ceilings to 10 cr and 100 cr and changed the turnover basis (corpus s.2 footnotes 19, 21, 22). It also omits the proviso exclusions (holding/subsidiary, s.8, special Act). Those decide 'not small' without any threshold, and A's basis line 'one under set limits for capital and turnover' leaves them out too.
findings.recommendation: Draw only held instruments as solid. Show 92(E) as 'not held'. Add the 2018 Act amendment. Add the proviso questions to the small-company question, since they can answer definitively without thresholds (classify.py checks them first).

findings.issue: The document check on a board resolution flags '⟳ Law has changed / potential issue' for a threshold increase. A company that was small under the lower limits of 700(E) is still small under the higher limits of 880(E), assuming the same figures.
findings.evidence: A and B docs: the 14 Aug 2025 resolution 'treats the company as a small company... Those limits were revised later by G.S.R. 880(E). The resolution should be read again'. 880(E) raised the limits from 4 cr / 40 cr to 10 cr / 100 cr (gsr880e_registration.json operative_clause; lawyer_summary.py: 'limits were raised'). A raised ceiling cannot turn a small company into a non-small one. The real risk is that the company's own figures changed.
findings.recommendation: Say 'Limits changed after this date (raised). A company that was small on 14 Aug 2025 on these figures remains small. Check whether your figures have changed.' Keep the stale marker only where the change could flip the outcome.

findings.issue: The 120-day gap and the 7-day notice are computed conservatively without saying so, and the draft notice asserts delivery facts it cannot know.
findings.evidence: 'next must be held by 14 Oct 2026' is 16 Jun plus 120 days. s.173(1) says 'not more than one hundred and twenty days shall intervene', and read strictly (days between meetings, excluding both) that allows 15 Oct 2026. The backend uses (b-a).days <= 120, the conservative reading. The drafts state 'This notice is sent at least seven days before the meeting, as s.173(3) requires' and C marks s.173(3) 'Met' before anything is sent. SS-1 (ICSI) excludes the day of sending and the day of the meeting and adds 2 days for post. I have not verified SS-1 against a held copy; the backend does not hold it.
findings.recommendation: Label the date 'latest date, counted conservatively'. Show s.173(3) as 'Send by 1 Oct 2026' (a pending action), not 'Met'. Note that Secretarial Standards are not held.

findings.issue: s.177 abstention for a private company, and there is no 'not legal advice / professional judgement' framing on outputs a user can 'Approve'.
findings.evidence: All mockups show s.177 as '? Can't tell' for a Pvt Ltd because Rule 6 is 'held but not reviewed' (obligations.py _audit_committee). That matches the backend, but a practising lawyer knows Rule 6 prescribes public companies only, so showing 'can't tell' for a private company will cost credibility. No mockup carries a professional-judgement note, while website AGENTS.md line 37 requires legal copy to be marked 'not legal advice'.
findings.recommendation: Prioritise review of Rule 6 so the private-company case returns 'Doesn't apply'. Add one persistent line in the approval area: 'Placedon shows what the law says and where it comes from. It is not legal advice. The approver remains responsible.'

strengths_worth_keeping: A's duties screen line 'Showing 9 of the 15 duties Placedon checks today. A blank or can't-tell row never means the company is compliant' is exactly the right scope honesty and should be the pattern for all copy.

Statutory figures and quotations match the corpus: the s.96(1) opening words and the six-month proviso, s.173 120 days / four meetings / seven days, s.149(1)(a) two directors for a private company, s.149(3) 182 days, s.135(1) Rs 500 cr / 1000 cr / 5 cr.
Date arithmetic is correct: 31 Mar + 6 months = 30 Sep, 16 Jun to 26 Sep = 102 days, 16 Jun + 120 days = 14 Oct, 26 Sep to 8 Oct is more than 7 days.
The five-state vocabulary with 'Can't tell is never a pass' and naming the missing fact matches obligations.py ROW_STATES and the no-confidence contract. No confidence numbers appear anywhere.
The FEMA 'Not held' answer is a correct out_of_scope treatment: no answer from memory, and the missing law is named.
Approval is locked while a blank remains, which fits the deterministic, source-per-part drafting model.
reviews.preferred_direction: A as the base, taking C's glossary and 3-step framing only for onboarding. A has the fewest unsupported claims and already discloses its 9-of-15 scope. B's date-travel promise depends on a point-in-time capability the backend explicitly lacks, so B should not lead unless date travel is limited to dated thresholds and deadlines.
open_questions: Is G.S.R. 880(E) considered 'attested' by is_attested() today? The registration shows VERIFIED_INSTRUMENT and CORROBORATED with an automated Gazette match but null download provenance. The small-company copy depends on the answer, and I could not run the engine because the local python3 is older than 3.10.

Does the backend hold the commencement instrument for s.96 / s.173 (1 Apr 2014, S.O. 902(E))? If not, how does the product keep its promise to cite 'the notification that set its wording' for original-2013 sections?

Should s173_slice treat an incomplete calendar year with fewer than 4 meetings as NOT_COMPLIANT, as it appears to now, or as undetermined until 31 Dec? The mockup, the law and the engine currently disagree three ways.
Will Watch (IBBI, sanctions) and document upload ship at all, given UX_INTERACTION_SPEC.md marks document upload 'Cut' and the backend has no sanctions module?
Should the product show that the backend's 'APPLIES_NOT_SATISFIED' for an AGM not yet held (26 Sep, deadline 30 Sep) differs from legal default? The company is not yet in breach.

reviews.summary: None of the three mockups is ready for a pilot demo. They share one problem that outweighs the differences between them. All three show G.S.R. 880(E) as 'not yet checked against the Gazette', but the backend says a named reviewer registered and corroborated it on 2026-09-10. So the flagship s.2(85) currency story, our one moat that competitors cannot copy, ends in 'can't tell' on every screen. B proves the moat best in a 15-minute demo: its date control and timeline are the currency strip from UX_INTERACTION_SPEC §4. But B has no free-text Ask and nothing to bring a user back. A best keeps weekly users, because it has an attention home and a Watch inbox, but it hides currency inside one screen out of six. C explains the product well to a founder but costs a Company Secretary (CS) extra clicks. None of them serves the buyer the documents name: a practising CS with 40-80 clients, or an in-house team working in matters. All three also spend space on Drafts, which the business plan excludes and ComplyRelax already gives ICSI members free.

findings.issue: All three mockups hide the moat. They show G.S.R. 880(E) as unverified, so the s.2(85) small-company answer is always 'can't tell' and never shows the dated ₹10 crore figure the whole product thesis is built on.
findings.evidence: A Main.dc.html: rowsRaw s.2(85) says 'Its text hasn't yet been checked against the Gazette'. The Watch item for G.S.R. 880(E) reads '? Needs checking'. B Sentence.dc.html: the timeline mark says '2025 · not yet checked' (dashed). The partial answer on 14 Aug 2025 says '700(E)… waiting for a person to review it', so both dates give no figure. C Guided.dc.html: step 2 says 'Two rules we depend on are not yet confirmed: G.S.R. 880(E)…'. The backend disagrees. placedon-law-backend/checker/currency.py (lines 252-258) says 'G.S.R. 880(E) was registered on 2026-09-10, identity and verbatim clause both checked by a named reviewer, status CORROBORATED' and calls the old wording 'wrong in the direction that makes an honest system look like it holds nothing'. The checker/api.py self-test (lines 736-760) expects /v1/document-check to return governed_then 700(E), governs_now 880(E), and both CURRENT. UX_INTERACTION_SPEC §3.1 puts '₹10,00,00,000 · G.S.R. 880(E) · as at 01-Dec-2025' in the ANSWERED state. Caveat: whether 700(E) is attested on disk right now decides whether 2025 dates read CURRENT. I could not run the engine to confirm this.
findings.recommendation: Rebuild the sample data from real engine output (POST /v1/ask and /v1/document-check with the sample profile) rather than hand-written copy. Make 'Are we a small company?' ANSWERED today, with ₹10 crore, G.S.R. 880(E) and 01 Dec 2025 shown next to the figure. Keep one honest PARTIAL example on a provision that really is unheld, such as the s.177 Rule 6 row, so the demo shows both a proof and an abstention. Add a rule: mockup copy about which instruments are held must come from currency.instrument_status, not from memory.

findings.issue: None of the mockups serves either named buyer. Each is built around a single company, but the business plan's buyer is a practising CS with 40-80 clients, and PLAN_17's beta buyer is an in-house team working in Matters. The screens fit a founder, who is the secondary, low-willingness-to-pay segment.
findings.evidence: bp/docs/BUSINESS_PLAN.md §3: 'Primary: practising Company Secretaries… serving 40–80 clients each'. INTERVIEWS.md §7: 'The ten calls go to Company Secretaries'. PLAN_17 §0: 'the smallest system a real in-house legal team can use'. Its beta HAS list includes 'Matters, and a Vault'. M10 screen 2 is 'Matters list and matter page'. A's header is hard-wired to one company ('Sample Company Pvt Ltd' plus CIN), with no client switcher. B's subject list for duties is ['Sample Company Pvt Ltd']. C's step 1 asks for one company's facts, and its glossary explains 'CIN' and 'Section', which a CS does not need.
findings.recommendation: Settle the buyer before choosing a direction, since the two repos contradict each other: CS in the 2026-08-16 plan versus in-house legal in the 2026-09-24 PLAN_17. If CS, the home screen should be a portfolio: every client, with its next hard deadline and its 'can't tell' count, sorted by urgency. If in-house legal, add Matters. Either way, move C's glossary into an optional help panel instead of making it permanent layout.

findings.issue: All three spend space on a Drafts feature. Drafting is excluded by the business plan, no interviewee asked for it, and document generation is already free to ICSI members through ComplyRelax. In a pilot it pushes Placedon into the Harvey and Spellbook category and away from its wedge.
findings.evidence: BUSINESS_PLAN.md §2 excludes 'Drafting, document review, litigation', noting that drafting 'is where professional trust ends'. INTERVIEWS.md §6: 'Nobody asked for drafting'. bp/backend/CLAUDE.md line 21: 'Document generation is commoditised: ComplyRelax is free to ICSI members until 31 Mar 2029'. PLAN_17 §0 does not list drafting among what a beta has. A has a full 'Drafts' nav item and screen; it is also feature '05' on the Overview. B has the 'a draft of' verb. C has task 05, 'Draft a notice or resolution'.
findings.recommendation: Cut Drafts from the pilot build. Keep the provenance underline legend, which marks each part as from the record, typed by you, worked out from law, or a section. Apply it to answers and to the forensics report, which is where it helps prove the claims.

findings.issue: None of the mockups addresses the one feature a buyer asked for unprompted: counterparty identity verification with a 'verified' mark. Instead, A and C put OFAC sanctions first, which matters little to an Indian private company buying from domestic suppliers.
findings.evidence: INTERVIEWS.md §2 records PAN, GST and bank name-match, returned to three times, and 'एक verified का sign लग जाए'. §5 notes that the CIN → name lookup already exists, with 3.67M records at ₹0. A watchRaw includes 'Sanctions list checked: no match for 3 counterparties' against OFAC. C's Watch task compares against 'the OFAC sanctions list'. Only the IBBI item comes close, and it stops at 'Compare the CIN… before relying on it', which leaves the comparison to the user when the engine could do it.
findings.recommendation: In the Watch/counterparty area, lead with 'Supplier CIN → registered name, status, match/mismatch'. Use the existing OGD lookup, with provenance and an as-at date. Run the IBBI match by CIN automatically instead of asking the user to do it. Leave GST, PAN and bank checks as a clearly labelled 'not yet' tile until the feasibility result mentioned in INTERVIEWS.md §5 comes back.

findings.issue: B is the best at proving the moat in a demo but the worst at keeping users. There is no free-text Ask, the timeline always shows s.2(85) whatever the verb, only two dates can be chosen, and nothing tells a returning user what changed since last week.
findings.evidence: Sentence.dc.html: the 'ask' verb subjects are three fixed questions, and there is no input element for a question. The marks array is hard-coded to the s.2(85) instruments and is shown even for AGM, watch and draft. The dates object holds only 'today' and '14 August 2025'. Watch is one verb among five, not a default view or a count. The only instruction is 'Click any underlined words… That is the whole interface.' UX_INTERACTION_SPEC §6.1: 'the first ten uses… shown on a phone… during a fifteen-minute conversation'. A 50px sentence at 1440 px does not reflow to 360 px (PLAN_17 M10: 'on a 360px screen').
findings.recommendation: Don't ship B as the app. Use its parts inside A: an 'as of [date]' control on every answer, duty row and document, backed by an unrestricted date picker, and the currency strip on each provision's Source view. Make sure the strip also works as a table, as UX_INTERACTION_SPEC §7 requires.

findings.issue: C's three steps add work on every visit for a daily professional user. They also stage a deterministic, millisecond-fast result as a visible process, which the spec explicitly rejects. The Watch 'task' makes an ongoing inbox look like a one-time wizard.
findings.evidence: Guided.dc.html: every task requires 'Check it' then 'See the result'. The Ask step-1 fields are readonly (readonly="{{ yes }}"), so you cannot type a question. Watch task 04 says 'Choose what to watch' and then shows '4 new items' only after two clicks. The home page has no deadline or attention summary, so the AGM that is due in 4 days is invisible until you open task 01. UX_INTERACTION_SPEC §6.2: 'No loading skeletons. Deterministic paths return in milliseconds.' PLAN_17 §0 exit criteria: used 'at least twice a week for four weeks'.
findings.recommendation: If anything from C is kept, turn 'We check' into a collapsible 'How we got this' trace under the result. A CS who signs filings will value that audit trail. Drop it as a gated step, and never make Watch a wizard.

findings.issue: A has the right shell for keeping users (an attention home and an inbox), but it breaks the two-screen rule and does not show currency on the main Ask answer. The ANSWERED AGM figure has no instrument or as-at date beside it.
findings.evidence: Main.dc.html has six nav screens (Overview, Ask, Company duties, Documents, Watch, Drafts). UX_INTERACTION_SPEC §5 cuts the Dashboard ('Zero clients, zero queries') and says 'a third screen ships only when a named user asks for it by name'. PLAN_17 M10, the later document, does allow Ask, Vault, Watch and Settings, so the two plans conflict. On A's Ask screen the answered figure's basis is 'Worked out from s.96(1): six months after 31 Mar 2026', with no 'as at' date and no note that the provision is unamended. Spec §1: 'Next to the number'. C does worse: 'No notification has changed this rule since, so none is cited' marked '– Not needed', which hides the currency claim when it should state it.
findings.recommendation: Keep A's frame with four surfaces: Attention (home), Ask + Source, Duties, and Watch. Merge Documents into the matter or client view and cut Drafts. On every figure, print '[section] · [instrument or "as enacted"] · in force [date]' in mono under the number, including unamended provisions such as s.96(1) (in force 01 Apr 2014).

findings.issue: The feedback control in the mockups does not collect demand data. Both the spec and PLAN_17 treat per-answer feedback as the only pre-revenue telemetry.
findings.evidence: A has 'Was this useful?' on the Ask answer. B and C have no feedback control. UX_INTERACTION_SPEC §3.2 calls for '[ Tell us this is blocking you ]' in PARTIAL, as a 'demand signal, not a support ticket'. PLAN_17 §0 wants 'a feedback button on every answer' and 'at least 59 answers labelled'.
findings.recommendation: Add 'This is blocking me' to every PARTIAL answer and every CAN'T TELL duty row. Log the provision ID, since that decides what gets verified next.

findings.issue: Documents: the three mockups disagree on forensics claims and on whether documents are digital. B's past-date check marks law based on 700(E) as '✓ Verified' while the same mockup says 700(E) is 'awaiting review', which contradicts itself.
findings.evidence: Sentence.dc.html docSets[1]: 'Law it relied on, then' is 'ok' (✓ Verified), 'using the limits of 14 Aug 2025'. The same file's partial answer says 'G.S.R. 700(E) · awaiting review'. INTERVIEWS.md: documents are 'सब physical' (four sources). A's scanned-minutes card ('We don't report problems in a document we couldn't read') is the only mockup that deals honestly with that.
findings.recommendation: Keep A's 'couldn't read, so no findings' state as the standard. Never mark as verified any document check that depends on an instrument we have not attested.

strengths_worth_keeping: A: the 'What needs attention' home tiles ('AGM due in 4 days', '3 duties can't tell', '1 relies on old law'). This is the weekly-return hook PLAN_17's twice-a-week exit criterion needs.
A/B: the Watch 'Why you're seeing this' path chips (instrument → section → duty → company). They show the deterministic chain visibly, which GC AI's span citations cannot do.
B: 'as of [date]' as a first-class control, plus the instrument timeline. This is the currency strip from UX_INTERACTION_SPEC §4 and the strongest single moat moment in any mockup.
A: the scanned-minutes card ('We don't report problems in a document we couldn't read. Nothing here is a finding.'). It is honest about physical and scanned documents.
ALL: no confidence scores, 'can't tell is never a pass', and five row states that map one-to-one to checker/obligations.py ROW_STATES.
C: the step-2 check trace, as a collapsible audit trail. A CS who personally certifies MGT-7/AOC-4 needs to see what was checked.
reviews.preferred_direction: A hybrid: A's shell (attention home, Duties, Watch inbox, Ask + Source), with B's 'as of [date]' control and currency strip on every figure, and C's check trace as a collapsible 'How we got this'. Cut Drafts and the permanent glossary, and rebuild the sample data from real engine output so s.2(85) shows the ANSWERED ₹10 crore under G.S.R. 880(E). A keeps weekly users; B's parts prove the moat in the demo.
open_questions: Who is the pilot buyer: a practising CS with a client portfolio (BUSINESS_PLAN.md, INTERVIEWS.md) or an in-house legal team with Matters (PLAN_17)? The home screen is different for each, and none of the three mockups fits either.

Is G.S.R. 880(E) servable end to end today? currency.py says it is CORROBORATED as of 2026-09-10, but 2025-dated answers depend on 700(E)'s on-disk attestation. Someone should run POST /v1/ask 'Are we a small company?' on the sample profile before the council decides.
Does the two-screen rule in UX_INTERACTION_SPEC §5 (2026-08-16) still bind, or did PLAN_17 M10 (2026-09-24) replace it? The mockups follow neither.
Has the counterparty-verification feasibility check (GST/PAN/bank, INTERVIEWS.md §5) returned? If CIN-level verification is all that is buildable, should it replace OFAC as the lead Watch item?
Is the demo device a phone (UX spec §6.1) or a desktop? All three mockups are fixed at 1440x960, and B's sentence layout will not survive 360 px.

reviews.summary: None of the three mockups is ready to build as it stands. All three share one five-chip status vocabulary, but that vocabulary is overloaded: the same black filled chip means Met, Answered, Verified, Checked and Done. None of them draws an empty, loading or transport-error state. The evidence blocks leave out the in-force date, the instrument and the text-basis line that PLAN_13 requires. A reads well but looks like a generic sidebar SaaS app with KPI tiles. B has the strongest brand presence, and its timeline is the currency strip that UX_INTERACTION_SPEC §4 calls the product's distinctive component. But B's central interaction (moving the date into the past) shows point-in-time law that the engine says it cannot verify, and B has no free-text question field. C is the easiest to understand, but it wraps even a single question in a 3-step wizard and has no place that shows urgency. I recommend a hybrid: A's working screens, C's language and its "what we checked" trail, and B's timeline shown per provision with the date fixed at today.

findings.issue: There are no empty, loading or transport-error states anywhere. The only way the design shows 'no answer' is the dashed grey 'can't tell' chip, so when a service error is added later it is likely to be styled the same way, and a transport failure will look like an abstention.
findings.evidence: Main.dc.html askIt() only sets showAskNote ('This mockup answers the three sample questions above'), and '+ Upload a document' (line 218) has no handler or state. Sentence.dc.html and Guided.dc.html have no free input that could fail. PLAN_13_ASSISTANT_UX.md §7.11 specifies a ServiceError card: 'No result · The service did not return a result, so there is no answer, partial or otherwise … Send again'. AGENTS.md says 'A transport failure must NEVER render as an abstention'. PLAN_13 also gives ServiceError a 'Dashed Ink-80 border', while the mockups' cant chip is 'border: 1px dashed #5B6472'. Both are dashed grey, which is the collision in waiting.
findings.recommendation: Design the ServiceError card now, in the same component set as the answer states, and make it look nothing like an abstention: a solid Ink rule, no status chip, the heading 'No result', the kept question and a 'Send again' button. Change PLAN_13's dashed border to solid so no dashed treatment is shared. Also draw a first-run empty state for Ask, Documents and Watch, and use the single inline caption 'checking the source…' (UX_INTERACTION_SPEC §6.2) instead of any skeleton.

findings.issue: B's defining interaction is moving 'as of' back to 14 Aug 2025 and getting past-dated duties, answers and a document verdict. The engine has no point-in-time capability, so this interaction cannot be built truthfully. The past-date screen also states which law was in force (G.S.R. 700(E)) as a settled fact.
findings.evidence: Sentence.dc.html lines 214 and 233 hold the dates 'today' and '14 August 2025'. timelineNote reads 'On 14 Aug 2025 the small-company limits came from G.S.R. 700(E)', and dutiesPast recomputes s.96(1) for FY 2024-25. PLAN_13 §9: 'as_of is today, and only today, in v1. The engine has no point-in-time capability (law_version.point_in_time_verified is false)… So the field is read-only.' checker/ask.py:614-615 confirms point_in_time_verified is False even when a date is requested.
findings.recommendation: Keep the timeline but make the cursor read-only and fixed at today. Use it to show the history of each instrument (governed then, governs now), not to recompute results for a past date. If a past date is ever allowed, the card must lead with the engine's 'not a point-in-time version' line.

findings.issue: Status chips are overloaded, and the same fact gets different chips on different screens. One visual (black fill) carries at least five meanings. G.S.R. 880(E), which is unverified, appears as '? Needs checking' (grey) on Watch but as '⟳ Law has changed' (gold, action-needed) on Documents. That second chip asserts a change the product elsewhere says it has not confirmed.
findings.evidence: Main.dc.html: SC maps answered to the 'met' style, so '■ Answered' looks the same as '✓ Met', '✓ Verified' (DL.ok) and '✓ Checked' (watch). Guided.dc.html has K.done '✓ Done' with the met style, and it puts a '✓ Met' chip on an Ask verbatim quote (row('met','s.96(1)','“…within a period of six months…”')). Main.dc.html watchRaw[0] is ck:'cant' '? Needs checking', while docsRaw[1] is 'stale' → notmet chip, 'Those limits were revised later by G.S.R. 880(E)'. Labels also differ between mockups: A and B use '! Not met yet' / '… Not known yet', C uses '! Needs action' / '… Comes later'. checker/obligations.py defines exactly five row states.
findings.recommendation: Separate three vocabularies and give each its own component. (1) Obligation row states: five, mapped 1:1 to ROW_STATES, with the same wording everywhere. (2) Ask turn states (answered/partial/out_of_scope): rendered as a heading word, not a chip, as PLAN_13 row 1 says. (3) Process-trail ticks: a plain mono '✓' with no chip. Any verdict that depends on an unverified instrument inherits 'can't tell' and never gets the gold action chip.

findings.issue: The evidence presentation falls short of the PLAN_13 and UX spec contract. Figure blocks have no in-force date and no instrument. No verbatim text has its 'Text as ingested… current consolidation' basis line. The partial answer for s.2(85) shows no verbatim text at all, even though the spec says this is the state where verbatim text matters most.
findings.evidence: Main.dc.html figure block: figBasis 'Worked out from s.96(1)…', with no 'In force from'/instrument. PLAN_13 §9: a figure block 'always carries instrument and in-force date'. Main.dc.html qs[1] (partial) has hasQuote:false. UX_INTERACTION_SPEC §3.2: 'Show the verbatim text in the partial state, always'. PLAN_13 §2 row 2: NOT CONFIRMED renders before CONFIRMED, but A has no CONFIRMED group. Sentence.dc.html has no verbatim anywhere; its sources aside lists labels only. Guided.dc.html squeezes a verbatim fragment into a 15px sans table cell. A's headline 'By 30 Sep 2026.' repeats figValue '30 Sep 2026' directly below it.
findings.recommendation: Build one evidence stack and reuse it in every mockup's result area, in this order: stamp ('Asked as of … · No model used') → state heading → NOT CONFIRMED → CONFIRMED → figure block (value, 'In force from', full instrument) → verbatim block in serif with a dashed-rule TextBasisLine → a Sources column made of citation records. Do not repeat the figure in the headline.

findings.issue: B has no free-text question field, and on screen it looks like a navigation sentence that has taken over the page. Ask is limited to three canned subjects. The 50px italic sentence plus the open tray and the timeline use about half the 960px height before any result appears. The timeline shows s.2(85) small-company history even when the verb is 'a draft of a notice of the next board meeting'.
findings.evidence: Sentence.dc.html verbs.ask.subjects is a fixed list of 3 quoted questions, with no input. The sentence uses font-size 50px, line-height 1.3 and font-style: italic in slotStyle(). DESIGN_SYSTEM.md §3: 'Never italicize… italics read as uncertain'. The marks array is hard-coded to s.2(85) whatever the verb. The timeline sub-labels are font-size 11px, and DESIGN_SYSTEM.md says 'no font size below 12px'. The timeline has no <table> fallback, which UX_INTERACTION_SPEC §7 requires.
findings.recommendation: If anything from B's sentence is kept, keep it as a compact 20-24px upright breadcrumb over a real text field. Tie the timeline to the provision the result cites, hide it when no provision has instrument history, and put a table under it for screen readers.

findings.issue: The wizard applies friction evenly, so the easy task pays the same cost as the hard one. Asking one question takes three screens and two clicks. Step 1 fields are read-only, which is a dead end. The home screen has nowhere to show urgency: 'AGM due in 4 days' is only visible at task 01 → step 3.
findings.evidence: Guided.dc.html: tasks[1] (Ask) runs through the same steps ['Tell us','We check','Your result']. The inputs have readonly='{{ yes }}'. The home view renders only the task cards and 'How every task works'. The s.96(1) deadline appears only in tasks[0].headline, shown at step 3. By contrast, Main.dc.html tiles[0] 'AGM due in 4 days' is the first thing on the Overview.
findings.recommendation: Put an attention strip at the top of C's home, using A's tiles but ranked, with the deadline visually dominant. Let Ask go straight from the question to the result. Show 'We check' as an expandable trail inside the result, not as a separate step. Keep steps only for multi-input tasks such as duties and drafts.

findings.issue: A's layout is generic SaaS. Its flat hierarchy puts the one urgent item on the same footing as everything else, and it explains itself three times. The Ask screen squeezes the answer into a column about 450px wide, and the question field sits below the answer.
findings.evidence: Main.dc.html Overview: a dark 248px sidebar with hint lines, four identical tiles (the 'AGM due in 4 days' tile is styled like '1 law change'), a numbered '01–05 … Try it' feature grid ('New here? Here is everything Placedon does'), and a legend. These are the numbered-feature-card and KPI-tile patterns AGENTS.md warns read as template or AI slop. Ask uses grid-template-columns: 280px minmax(0,1fr) 320px inside a 1112px main area, and the <form> comes after the grid. PLAN_13 §2 row 11 keeps the composer first. Its secondary button reads 'Was this useful?' instead of the demand-signal action 'Tell us this is blocking you' (UX_INTERACTION_SPEC §3.2).
findings.recommendation: Remove the feature grid (the nav hints already describe each tool) and rank the tiles so the deadline dominates. On Ask, fold the suggested questions into the empty state, put the composer first, and give the answer column at least 640px next to a 320px Sources column.

findings.issue: The two brand sources contradict each other, and the mockups follow only one of them. The type scale is also inconsistent across the three mockups and larger than the design-system tokens.
findings.evidence: bp/docs/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md: Slate accent, Playfair Display, Caution #8B4513 for abstention, Display 32px, Body 14px. placedon-claude-legal-3300/AGENTS.md: Brass Gold #C9A24B, Fraunces, Cool Grey #5B6472 for abstention. The mockups follow AGENTS.md. H1 sizes are 40/34 in A, 50 in B and 46/36 in C. A alone uses about 11 distinct font sizes. The notmet chip uses gold-muted #9F743B, which AGENTS.md reserves 'for citations only', and A's Draft also uses it for citations, so the gold border no longer tells a citation apart from an action.
findings.recommendation: Declare AGENTS.md the brand source and retire the conflicting DESIGN_SYSTEM.md tokens. Define a 6-step type scale shared by all screens. Give the 'needs action' chip a colour-free form (bold Ink border plus the '!' glyph) so gold-muted means citation and nothing else.

findings.issue: Every mockup is a fixed 1440x960 board, and none shows narrow widths. The spec says the first demos will happen on a phone.
findings.evidence: All three files use a width: 1440px root with data-props $preview 1440x960. UX_INTERACTION_SPEC §6.1: 'the first ten uses of this product will be shown on a phone'. AGENTS.md checklist: 'responsive to 360px'. B's 50px sentence and A's three-column Ask grid cannot collapse to that width without being redesigned.
findings.recommendation: Before choosing a direction, produce a 360px frame of the Ask result (a partial answer with verbatim text) and of the duties table for each candidate. Whichever survives that width decides the shell.

strengths_worth_keeping: Best from A: the Watch 'Why you're seeing this' causal chain (G.S.R. 880(E) → s.2(85) → Board's report duties → company), with a 'What to do' box. It maps directly to GET /v1/instruments/{frag}/affected and turns a feed into an explanation. Runner-up: the Draft provenance encoding (solid, dotted, double and gold underlines plus a dashed blank box, with a legend) and approval that stays locked while a blank remains. It works without colour and does not look like other products.

Best from B: the dated instrument timeline, with a hollow dashed node for the unverified G.S.R. 880(E). It is the 'currency strip' that UX_INTERACTION_SPEC §4 calls the one component competitors cannot copy. Graft it into the Sources panel for each provision, with the cursor fixed at today, the ₹ figure on each node once verified, and a table fallback. B's dark frame with a cream result sheet is also the most distinctive brand treatment of the three.

Best from C: the 'We check' trail ('Here is exactly what Placedon checked, in order'). It makes the deterministic engine visible and matches the event-log idea. Graft it as an expandable section inside every result, not as a wizard step. The glossary that highlights the terms the current task uses and the dashed 'Not yet: FEMA, SEBI, IBC' card are also worth keeping as an honest statement of scope.

Shared across all three, keep: an unreadable scan is labelled '? Couldn't read' with 'Nothing here is a finding'. 'A can't tell row is never a pass' is stated beside the table. Mono is used for every section, CIN and date. Every status chip has a glyph as well as a colour. Targets are 44px and filters use aria-pressed.
reviews.preferred_direction: A hybrid. Use A's shell and working screens (the duty table with a detail panel, Watch with its causal chain, provenance-underlined drafts). Replace A's Overview with C's task-first 'What do you need to do today?' home, topped by a ranked attention strip. Show C's 'We check' trail as an expandable section inside each result, and the glossary as an on-demand drawer. Add B's instrument timeline per provision in the Sources column, with the date fixed at today. Drop B's editable past date and C's wizard for Ask. This combines the strongest evidence layout, the clearest language and the one distinctive visual device without building anything the engine cannot honour.
open_questions: Which brand source is binding: AGENTS.md (gold, Fraunces, grey means abstention) or bp/docs/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md (slate, Playfair, brown Caution means abstention)? The mockups follow AGENTS.md, but PLAN_13 still speaks in Slate, Caution and Playfair terms.

PLAN_13 §7.11 gives ServiceError a dashed Ink-80 border. Should the owner change it to a solid rule so no dashed treatment is shared with the abstention grey? I am not certain Ink-80 and #5B6472 are distinguishable to users at a glance.

Does the Watch feed (OFAC, IBBI, Gazette) have a backend source? checker/api.py lists only events and instruments/affected routes, and I did not verify whether a sanctions or insolvency ingest exists behind /events. If it does not, A's and B's Watch screens overstate what the engine does.

Should the Ask turn state be a heading word (PLAN_13 row 1, 'Partly answered' as the largest element) or a chip, as in all three mockups? This decides whether the chip vocabulary can be kept for obligation rows only.

Is B's timeline allowed to show ₹ figures on the nodes (UX_INTERACTION_SPEC §4 does) while G.S.R. 700(E) and 880(E) are unattested, or must the nodes stay unlabelled until attested, as B currently leaves them?

reviews.role: Frontend engineering feasibility lead (Next.js 16 / React 19 / Tailwind v4, placedon-claude-legal-3300)
reviews.summary: None of the three mockups can be ported as they are. Each is a fixed 1440x960 board: the styling is inline strings built inside renderVals(), and all data is hard-coded there. So every direction means rebuilding the UI from scratch on the existing src/lib/engine client and src/components/surfaces. The main cost is the same for all three and is not the layout. The typed client covers only six routes (types.ts ENGINE_ROUTES still says /v1/ask "DOES NOT EXIST"), and there is no backend route at all for Drafts, counterparty or OFAC/IBBI Watch, or file upload. About half of what every mockup shows is therefore not buildable against today's engine. Between the directions, C maps most cleanly onto one-route-per-task Server Components with URL-addressable steps. A is the most familiar to build but the widest in scope. B is the riskiest: its sentence state has no URL, its timeline has no data source, and its fixed 50px editable sentence will not survive 360px.

findings.issue: Every mockup presents Drafts (Approve, fill the blank), counterparty Watch (OFAC/IBBI matches) and document upload ('Draft board resolution.pdf', 'Minutes, scanned copy') as working features. No backend route exists for any of them.
findings.evidence: placedon-law-backend/checker/api.py docstring lists 8 routes: compliance-pack, ask, document-check (takes profile facts + document_date, not a file; _DOC_CHECK_KEYS = PROFILE_KEYS | {document_date}), mca-strip, health, events, event, instruments/affected. It has no draft, upload or counterparty route. OFAC/IBBI live only in checker/operations.py and operation_store.py, with no HTTP surface. types.ts DRIFT 4: the events stream 'is NOT per-company… v0 serves law-change events only'. Yet Main.dc.html Watch, Sentence.dc.html watch[] ('OFAC list: no match for 3 counterparties') and Guided.dc.html task 04 all render per-company counterparty items. PLAN_17 puts upload and the Watch inbox behind M5 Vault and M9 Monitoring, both before M10.
findings.recommendation: Phase 1 ships only what the routes support: Duties (compliance-pack), Ask (/v1/ask), Document check as a form taking document_date plus facts, and law-change Watch labelled per DRIFT 4. Drafts, upload and counterparty items should appear as clearly marked 'not yet available' states or be left out. Mock data for them must not become the design contract.

findings.issue: The typed engine client in the site is stale and blocks Ask in every direction. There is no ask() or mcaStrip() method and no placedon.ask/0 schema, and a code comment forbids adding /v1/ask.
findings.evidence: src/lib/engine/types.ts L1-14: 'Exactly six routes exist. /v1/company/{cin}/standing and /v1/ask DO NOT EXIST — never add them here.' provider.ts EngineProvider lists only the six methods. AGENTS.md L58 repeats this. The contract, web/assistant/contract.md §2, defines the envelope (state answered|partial|out_of_scope, turn_id, parent_turn_id, as_of, context, figures[], citations[], law_version) and D12/D18 (no state on failure, 500 contract_violation).
findings.recommendation: Step 0 for any direction: fix AGENTS.md and the types.ts header, add an askSchema (zod) mirroring contract.md with a discriminated union on state, add ask() and mcaStrip() to both HttpEngineProvider and MockEngineProvider, and extend tests/contracts.mjs. Estimated effort is about 2-3 days. Every mockup's Ask panel depends on it.

findings.issue: B keeps its entire state in component state (verb, subj, date, open), so no answer can be linked to, bookmarked, reloaded or audited. It also depends on a data source that does not exist: a per-section version timeline.
findings.evidence: Sentence.dc.html: this.state = { verb, subj, date, open, venue, approved }. There is no route or URL reflection. marks[] are hard-coded (2014 s.2(85), G.S.R. 92(E), 700(E), 880(E) at fixed % positions). The date picker offers only 'today' | '14 August 2025'. The backend has as_of on compliance-pack, ask, document-check and events (supported), but no route returns a provision's version history. The only related data is figures[].effective_from/effective_to on an Ask turn and /v1/instruments/{frag}/affected, which goes the other way (instrument to obligations).
findings.recommendation: If any of B survives, serialise the sentence into searchParams (/app?show=duties&of=U7499...&asof=2025-08-14) and render it server-side. Build the timeline only from figures[] effective dates, or request a new backend route first. Reuse B's as-of control inside A or C instead of adopting B's shell.

findings.issue: B cannot be built responsively as designed. The 50px serif sentence of inline buttons, the absolutely positioned percentage timeline and the fixed 150/100/190/170px result grids break well before 360px, which AGENTS.md makes binding.
findings.evidence: Sentence.dc.html: font-size: 50px sentence with max-width 1300px, timeline marks at position:absolute left:55%/66%/84% (the 2021/2022/2025 labels collide on narrow widths), result grid 'minmax(0,1fr) 300px', duty rows 'grid-template-columns: 150px 100px minmax(0,1fr)'. AGENTS.md L76: 'responsive to 360px'. PLAN_17 M10 done-when: 'on a 360px screen and with a keyboard only'.
findings.recommendation: If B continues, it needs a separate small-screen design: the sentence as a stacked form, the timeline as a vertical list. Budget roughly 1.5x the layout effort of A or C.

findings.issue: Step 2 'We check' shows a narrated checklist ('Looked up the 15 duties…', 'Checked each section is in force…') that no route returns. The frontend would have to invent it, which conflicts with the rule against client-side inference. Step 1 fields are readonly placeholders, so no real input handling was designed.
findings.evidence: Guided.dc.html tasks[].checks built with chk('done', …) as static strings. contract.md D11: on the document path 'No stages: the orchestrator is the model path and this route never enters it'. PLAN_13 row 7 replaced 'Checked on its own' with showing evidence_pack.retrieval_query from the response. Guided.dc.html L103: <input … readonly>.
findings.recommendation: Build step 2 only from response fields: law_version.statement, evidence_pack.retrieval_query, provenance, cannot_verify[]/not_confirmed[]. Where no field exists, merge steps 2 and 3. Step 1 must be a real react-hook-form + zod form reusing compliancePackRequestSchema / documentCheckRequestSchema, which already exist in types.ts, with a server action calling the engine.

findings.issue: The 5-state chip vocabulary is redefined in each mockup and differs between them. None of them matches the labels the site already renders, so porting them creates three competing mappings of RowState to label.
findings.evidence: Sentence L: notmet '! Not met yet', pending '… Not known yet'. Guided L: notmet '! Needs action', pending '… Comes later'. Main has its own L/SL/DL maps. The existing src/app/product/compliance-pack/page.tsx STATE_LABEL uses 'Satisfied' / 'Not satisfied' / 'Undetermined' / 'Cannot determine'. The Ask states (■ Answered / ◧ Partly answered / □ Not held) are hand-mapped in each mockup. types.ts already has rowProductClass() and isAbstainingRowState().
