findings.recommendation: Build one StateChip component keyed on RowState and AskState, with a single label table in src/lib, and make it the only place labels live. Pick the copy once in council. Test with a snapshot per state and assert that CANNOT_DETERMINE and DOES_NOT_APPLY never share a label.

findings.issue: A has the most surface area: six screens, each a master-detail layout with fixed-width side panes, and 'Copy with sources' and 'Was this useful?' buttons that do nothing. That puts it at roughly the full M10 L-sized scope before any backend gaps are closed.
findings.evidence: Main.dc.html: Ask grid '280px minmax(0,1fr) 320px'; Duties 'minmax(0,1fr) 380px'; Docs '320px 1fr'; Watch '420px 1fr'. The feedback and copy buttons have no onClick (L137-138). State { screen, q, filter, row, doc, w } is all local, so the selected duty row and document are not deep-linkable. PLAN_17 M10 is rated L and requires 'a feedback control on every answer'.
findings.recommendation: Map screens to App Router segments (/app/duties/[obligationId], /app/documents/[id], /app/ask/[turnId]) so the detail pane is a URL and back/forward works. On narrow screens, use parallel or intercepted routes to collapse the three-column Ask into one column with inline Sources, as PLAN_13 describes for 320-400px. Wire feedback to a server action. Cut Overview from phase 1.

findings.issue: Streaming for Ask is not needed and is contradicted by the docs. The engine is a synchronous deterministic stdlib server, and PLAN_13 explicitly removes streaming. PLAN_17 M10 still asks for 'chat with streaming answer'. Building an SSE path would add cost without benefit.
findings.evidence: api.py: handle() is a pure function wrapped by scripts/serve_api.py (stdlib). PLAN_13 L30 lists streaming among the things 'subtracted'. PLAN_17 M10 screen 3 says 'streaming answer'. HttpEngineProvider uses cache:'no-store' with a timeout.
findings.recommendation: Submit Ask through a server action or route handler and use React 19 useActionState/useFormStatus for the pending state, with a Suspense boundary for the turn card. Record in the council agreement that streaming is out, and correct PLAN_17.

findings.issue: The server-only boundary is a runtime throw, not a build-time guard. Because every mockup is highly interactive (trays, filters, step buttons), there is a real risk someone imports '@/lib/engine' into a 'use client' component to get the types or the chip helpers.
findings.evidence: src/lib/engine/server-guard.ts: 'Stands in for import "server-only"… if (typeof window !== "undefined") throw'. index.ts re-exports types and helpers (isAbstainingRowState, rowProductClass) from the same barrel that imports the provider.
findings.recommendation: Split pure types and helpers into src/lib/engine/shared (client-safe) and keep providers behind server-only. Add the real 'server-only' package or an eslint no-restricted-imports rule for 'use client' files.

findings.issue: None of the markup can be reused. The styling is inline style strings built in JS (chip(), slotStyle(), approveStyle) with raw hex values rather than the site's tokens. Fonts (Archivo, Fraunces, IBM Plex Mono) are loaded from a Google Fonts link rather than through next/font.
findings.evidence: All three files: 'style="{{ r.chip }}"', colours #0C0C0D/#F4EFE6/#C9A24B/#5B6472 hard-coded. src/lib/tokens.ts and globals.css hold the site tokens.
findings.recommendation: Treat the mockups as specs only. Port the copy and the state tables (the renderVals data arrays are good fixture material for MockEngineProvider and Playwright tests via tests/browser.mjs), and rebuild the visuals with Tailwind v4 against the existing tokens.

strengths_worth_keeping: The existing reusable pieces are solid and cover the core of every direction: EngineResult<T> (errors.ts, where transport failure is never an abstention), zod request schemas (compliancePackRequestSchema, documentCheckRequestSchema with the document_date<=as_of refine), MockEngineProvider for offline dev and tests, and SurfaceShell/Citation/Stamp/EngineErrorPanel/AbstentionCard/ProvenanceFooter in src/components/surfaces/surface-shell.tsx plus evidence-card.tsx.

C's structure maps directly onto the App Router: /app/tasks/[task]/[step] with step 1 as a form (server action), step 3 as a Server Component fetching the engine, and each task tied to one engine route. It is the cheapest direction to deep-link, test and make responsive.
B's as-of control is cheap and backed by real data: as_of is accepted by compliance-pack, ask, document-check and events. It is worth keeping as a global searchParam control in A or C.
All three mockups keep the draft 'Approve locked while a part is blank' rule as a pure derived boolean. This is easy to unit-test once a draft route exists.
The renderVals() data arrays (duties today vs 14 Aug 2025, three Ask states, document checks) are ready-made fixtures for MockEngineProvider and for the per-state visual regression tests.
reviews.preferred_direction: C as the shell and flow (task-first, URL-addressable steps, one route per task), with A's master-detail Duties and Ask panes inside the task results and B's as-of date as a global searchParam control. This is the lowest-risk build: it maps onto existing routes and components, it is testable per step, and it reaches 360px without a redesign.
open_questions: Is the web app meant to call the engine directly with PLACEDON_API_ORIGIN, or only through the M3 gateway (PLAN_17 M10: 'talking only to the gateway, server-side')? If only the gateway, M10 cannot start until M3 and M4 land, whichever mockup is chosen.
Will the backend add a provision version-history route? Without one, B's timeline and any 'how this law changed' view can only be built from figures[] effective dates.
Should Drafts, upload and counterparty Watch be omitted from phase 1 or shown as disabled 'coming later' states? Showing them risks the overclaiming that AGENTS.md forbids.
Streaming: does PLAN_13 (no streaming) or PLAN_17 M10 (streaming answer) win? I recommend PLAN_13.
Which chip vocabulary is canonical: the site's 'Satisfied / Cannot determine' or the mockups' 'Met / Can't tell'? The choice affects AGENTS.md voice rules and existing /product pages.

Is there a test runner beyond tests/contracts.mjs and tests/browser.mjs? package.json has no test script, and phased delivery needs one (vitest or node:test plus Playwright) before M10 starts. I did not confirm what browser.mjs covers.

reviews.summary: None of the three mockups is ready for real client data. None of them says what happens to a document after upload: no copy on storage, retention, deletion, matter scoping, who can see it or which processor handles scans. Two things matter more because they could cause legal or reputational harm on the first live use. First, the sanctions result is shown as a green-equivalent tick ("Checked / No match"). The backend's own contract says an empty OFAC screen means only "not on the list as published on <date>", and matching is exact-name only. Second, the IBBI item claims a "similar name" match, but the backend has no fuzzy matcher and explicitly says fuzzy matching "invents hits". Approval is a one-click anonymous action with no named approver or timestamp in B and C. The generated notice also states as fact something Placedon cannot know. A is the most honest of the three: it states sample data clearly, has a "Why you're seeing this" path, tells the user to compare CINs, and says "record keeps who approved it and when". It also has the largest surface where data could be exposed. C frames candidates best in its step 2 ("needs a person to confirm"). B hides almost everything a trust reviewer needs.

findings.issue: A sanctions 'no match' is shown as a clean bill of health, using the same black tick chip as '✓ Met' and '✓ Verified'.
findings.evidence: Main.dc.html watchRaw[3]: label '✓ Checked', ck 'met', body 'Your three counterparties were compared with the US Treasury's OFAC list today. None matched.', todo 'Nothing.' Sentence.dc.html watch[0]: 'OFAC list: no match for 3 counterparties', ck 'met'. Guided.dc.html task 04 rows: row('met','26 Sep 2026','No sanctions match for your 3 counterparties.'). The backend says the opposite in placedon-law-backend/checker/feeds/ofac_sdn.py lines 55-58 and 294-296: 'An empty screening result ... is therefore "not on the list as published on <date>", never "not sanctioned"'. The same file says matching is exact on the normalised name and 'misses transliterations and aliases'. A user who relies on 'Nothing' to do could onboard a sanctioned party whose name is transliterated.
findings.recommendation: Never use the 'met' chip for a screening result. Use a distinct neutral state and wording like: 'Not found on the OFAC SDN list as published on <Publish_Date>. Exact-name match only; aliases and transliterations can be missed. This is not a sanctions clearance.' Show the list's publish date, not 'today'. Remove 'Nothing' from the 'What to do' line.

findings.issue: The IBBI 'Possible match ... similar name' item depends on a fuzzy name-matching capability the backend does not have and deliberately rejects. It also names a real-looking counterparty next to the word 'insolvency'.
findings.evidence: Main.dc.html watchRaw[2]: 'Possible match in an insolvency announcement: Supplier A Pvt Ltd ... A company with a similar name appears'. Sentence.dc.html: 'A similar name in an IBBI announcement'. Guided.dc.html: 'Possible insolvency match for Supplier A Pvt Ltd'. A grep of checker/ finds no fuzzy or similarity matcher. checker/feeds/ofac_sdn.py line 63 says 'fuzzy matching invents hits; neither may enter a Ring 0 decider'. checker/feeds/ibbi.py lines 27-32 say IBBI data is servable only if reproduced 'accurately' and 'not in a misleading context', which is 'why nothing here is summarised, scored or re-labelled'. The mockups re-label it as '? Possible match' and omit ATTRIBUTION_TEXT. If a user forwards this to a supplier or a bank, the screenshot says 'insolvency' beside a named company, which is a defamation and credit-harm risk.
findings.recommendation: Match only on CIN, or on exact normalised name, and show the matched field. Title the item 'IBBI published an announcement naming <exact name as published> on <date>', with the IBBI attribution text and a link. Keep the A instruction 'Compare the CIN before relying on it' and make it mandatory: provide a 'Confirmed same entity / Not the same entity' action whose result is logged with the reviewer's name. Do not put the counterparty's name next to 'insolvency' in list titles until a person confirms the match.

findings.issue: Document upload has no disclosure about confidentiality, retention, deletion, matter scoping or processing. For law firms bound by client confidentiality, this is the moment trust is won or lost.
findings.evidence: Main.dc.html Documents screen shows only '+ Upload a document' and 'Upload a notice, minutes or a resolution.' Guided.dc.html task 03: field 'Draft board resolution.pdf', help 'PDF or Word.' A grep of all three files finds 0 occurrences of privacy, delete, retention, encrypt or confidential. PLAN_17 M5 (placedon-law-backend/docs/PLAN_17_BETA_BUILD.md lines 322-360) specifies per-tenant envelope encryption, matter-scoped search, a per-tenant retention policy, crypto-shredding delete, and scans routed to Azure Document Intelligence as CLIENT data. M10 screen 6 requires 'Settings: retention, consent for evaluation use (off by default), delete data'. PLAN_17 step 0.6 leaves the DPDP position on third-party personal data in customer documents with counsel. Director names in minutes are personal data. No mockup shows a Settings or Vault screen.
findings.recommendation: Add a short line next to the upload control: 'Stored encrypted in India under your organisation's key. Visible only to members of this matter. Deleted after <N> days, or now: [Delete].' Say plainly that scanned pages are sent to Microsoft Azure Document Intelligence (Central India) for text extraction. Add a Settings screen with retention, evaluation consent (off by default) and delete-all. Add a 'Delete permanently' action to every document row. Keep the copy pending counsel review under PLAN_17 step 0.6.

findings.issue: Approval is an anonymous one-click action. B and C claim 'Approved and recorded' without saying who approved, when, or what version was approved. The only gate is 'no blanks', not whether the underlying law and facts are sound.
findings.evidence: Main.dc.html approveHelp: 'Approved. The record keeps who approved it and when.' This is the best of the three, but no user identity appears anywhere in A. Sentence.dc.html and Guided.dc.html: 'Approved and recorded.' In all three, approveDisabled = !filled, so only the venue blank blocks approval. No mockup shows a signed-in user, a matter, or an audit trail view. PLAN_17 lines 103-105 require the gateway to write an audit row per action with tenant and user.
findings.recommendation: On approve, show the approver's name, time (IST) and a document hash or version, for example 'Approved by <name> · 26 Sep 2026 14:02 IST · version 3'. Add a visible 'History' link on every draft and document. Show the signed-in user and matter in the header. Say 'Approved for use by you', not a bare 'Approved', so it is not mistaken for Placedon's legal sign-off.

findings.issue: The generated board notice asserts a future fact Placedon cannot know. If the user sends it late, the signed notice itself contains a false legal statement.
findings.evidence: Main.dc.html draft: 'This notice is sent at least seven days before the meeting, as s.173(3) requires.' Sentence.dc.html: 'It is sent at least seven days ahead, as s.173(3) requires'. Guided.dc.html check: 'Checked 8 Oct 2026 gives the seven days' notice s.173(3) asks for', marked met. On 26 Sep 2026 that is true only if the notice goes out by 1 Oct 2026. Nothing tracks or warns about the dispatch date.
findings.recommendation: Remove the self-certifying sentence from the notice body. Put the constraint in the side panel instead: 'Must be sent by 1 Oct 2026 (s.173(3)).' Block or warn on approval after that date. Record the dispatch date as a user-entered fact with its own provenance.

findings.issue: User-supplied facts and verified facts share one '✓ Met' / '✓ Verified' appearance. The backend's three output classes (VERIFIED_FACT, DETERMINISTIC_CONSEQUENCE, SIGNAL) are not visible, so a user cannot tell what Placedon proved from what they typed themselves.
findings.evidence: placedon-law-backend/checker/event_log.py lines 49-52 and 105-108: an event with no verifier 'cannot be a VERIFIED_FACT; it is a SIGNAL'. Main.dc.html rowsRaw s.149(1): 'Two directors are on record' shown as '✓ Met', with no statement of whose record. Main.dc.html doc check 'What it is': '✓ Verified', based on 'It says so on its face.' Guided.dc.html step 1 fields are readonly sample values with no provenance marker. Only B's duties sources say 'Company facts: supplied by you', and A's s.135 row says 'On the figures you gave us'.
findings.recommendation: Put a provenance tag on every '✓' row: 'from MCA record', 'from your input', or 'worked out'. Do not label a document's self-description 'Verified'. Use M8's 'PARTIALLY_VERIFIED' or classification wording. Carry A's draft legend (solid, dotted and double lines) into the compliance and document views.

findings.issue: The Watch inbox shows OFAC and e-Gazette observations to what will be a paying user, but the backend currently refuses to serve those feeds commercially because their licences are unverified.
findings.evidence: checker/feeds/ofac_sdn.py lines 44-50: LICENCE_UNVERIFIED, 'an observation from this feed refuses commercial serving until the terms are confirmed'. checker/feeds/egazette.py line 90: LICENCE = LICENCE_UNVERIFIED. checker/feeds/__init__.py _NEVER_COMMERCIAL includes LICENCE_UNVERIFIED. Main.dc.html, Sentence.dc.html (sources 'e-Gazette of India', 'OFAC sanctions list') and Guided.dc.html task 04 all present these as live items.
findings.recommendation: Design the state the backend will actually return: 'Source not yet cleared for display', or show the item only as a link to the official page. Otherwise, clear the licences before beta. Do not ship a Watch design that depends on data the engine will refuse to serve.

findings.issue: B has no document intake, no approval context and no persistent sample-versus-live boundary beyond one header chip. Its 'as of' date travel can be misread as a record of what the company actually did in the past.
findings.evidence: Sentence.dc.html header: 'Sample data · not a real company'. The dutiesPast rows say, for example, 'It was not yet late', which is a judgement about the company's past conduct derived from today's facts. The 'Approve' button sits inside a reading sheet with 'Approved and recorded.' There is no user, matter or history.
findings.recommendation: If B's timeline is kept, label past views 'Law as it stood on <date>. Company facts are today's unless you supply historical ones.' Do not show conduct verdicts such as 'not yet late' for past dates without historical facts.

findings.issue: The sample-data disclosure is weaker than in A and B. The Watch set-up step implies consent to screen third parties without saying what is stored.
findings.evidence: Guided.dc.html header shows only 'Sample data'; A and B say 'Sample data · not a real company'. Task 04 field 'Counterparties: 3 suppliers', help 'Checked for insolvency and sanctions.' Nothing says the counterparty list is stored, for how long, or that directors' names in it are personal data.
findings.recommendation: Use the full 'Sample data · not a real company' wording, and in the live product, a persistent 'Live data: <company>' state. Add a line to the counterparty step saying what is kept, how long, and how to remove a counterparty.

findings.issue: There is no 'Known limitations' link or 'not legal advice' framing, and a feedback control exists only in A.
findings.evidence: PLAN_17 M10 screen 7 requires 'A feedback control on every answer; a "Known limitations" page linked from the footer of every app screen.' A grep finds 'Was this useful?' only in Main.dc.html. No mockup contains 'advice' or 'limitation'.
findings.recommendation: Add a footer link on every screen: 'Known limitations · What Placedon does not check'. Add feedback to every answer in B and C. Include a short 'Placedon shows the law and its sources; it is not legal advice' line near approvals and exports ('Copy with sources').

strengths_worth_keeping: A Watch detail: 'Why you're seeing this' as a traceable chain (IBBI announcement → name → your supplier list), plus 'What to do: Compare the CIN in the announcement with your supplier's CIN before relying on it'. This is the right candidate-not-finding pattern and should be mandatory.
A scanned-minutes report: 'We don't report problems in a document we couldn't read. Nothing here is a finding.' This matches M8 and protects users from false findings.
A compliance footer: 'A blank or "can't tell" row never means the company is compliant.' The same idea appears in B and C and should appear on every export.
C step 2 'Here is exactly what Placedon checked, in order', including 'One name match needs a person to confirm it'. This is a visible audit of process that a lawyer can cite.
A approval copy 'The record keeps who approved it and when'. This is the right promise, but it needs a visible name and timestamp.
The A draft provenance legend (company record / you typed it / worked out / section / blank). Extend it to every factual row.
No confidence percentages anywhere, consistent with AGENTS.md and ask_contract.
reviews.preferred_direction: A hybrid built on C's shell (task flow, glossary, explicit 'We check' step), with A's Watch evidence chain and CIN-compare step and A's approval-audit promise, plus a new Vault/Settings trust layer (retention, delete, matter scope, processor disclosure). The deciding factor is that C's step structure is the best place to disclose data handling and name-match uncertainty at the moment of intake.
open_questions: What will the IBBI watcher actually match on: CIN, exact normalised name, or something else? The mockups assume 'similar name' matching, which the backend does not implement.
Will OFAC and e-Gazette licences be cleared before beta? If not, what should the Watch inbox show for those feeds?

Counsel's DPDP position (PLAN_17 step 0.6) on director and third-party personal data in uploaded minutes and counterparty lists: is a notice at upload enough, or is a data processing agreement needed first?
Is the default retention period set per tenant or per matter, and can a law firm set a period per client matter to match its engagement terms?
Can approval need two people (maker and checker) for board documents, and should approval be locked while any 'can't tell' row feeds the draft?
Will the 'Copy with sources' export carry the sample/live flag and the list publish date, so a pasted result cannot circulate without its caveats?

reviews.summary: All three mockups are polished answers to the wrong question. They show one company, when the buyer is a Company Secretary (CS) handling 40 to 80 client companies. They fill the screen with features the backend does not serve (Drafts, counterparty/OFAC watch) and that the business plan excludes. They also describe a 15-duty engine as "every duty the Act gives". Worst, the product's one claimed moat is the currency strip ("which figure is current?"), and it abstains in every demo state: s.2(85) is "can't tell" today and also on 14 Aug 2025. So the unusual Mockup B is a timeline with no figures on it. A is a generic compliance-SaaS sidebar that hides point-in-time law behind a static header label. C adds a ceremonial "We check" step and a glossary that defines "Section" for professionals who certify MGT-7. B is the only one with an idea a competitor could not copy, but as built it is partly a gimmick: two hard-coded dates, canned subjects, and sentence combinations that make no sense.

findings.issue: The product's differentiator (which prescribed figure is current) never produces an answer in any mockup, so the demo proves the churn case instead of the value case.
findings.evidence: bp/docs/UX_INTERACTION_SPEC.md §4 calls the currency strip 'the product made visible' and draws it with figures (₹50L → ₹2cr → ₹4cr → ₹10cr under G.S.R. 92(E)/700(E)/880(E)). In Sentence.dc.html the timeline marks carry only 'limits revised', with no figures. timelineNote and the s.2(85) row say 880(E) is 'not yet checked' today, and in the past state 700(E) is 'waiting for review, so no limit is shown'. Main.dc.html q2 'Are we a small company?' is 'partial' with 'we show no limit'. Guided.dc.html task 01 check 4 is '? Can't confirm' on 880(E). backend checker/prescribed_thresholds.py:108 SOURCE_880 = 'UNRESOLVED'. UX_INTERACTION_SPEC.md §9 names the falsifier itself: a CS shown PARTIAL who says 'this is useless, just give me an answer'.
findings.recommendation: Hold the UI decision until at least one threshold instrument (700(E) is the obvious one) is verified end to end. The hero demo must be a currency strip with real figures and a resolved answer, followed by a single dashed 880(E) segment. If no threshold can be verified before the pilot, lead the demo with s.96/s.173 date arithmetic and stop marketing the strip.

findings.issue: The unit of the product is wrong. Every mockup is built around one company, but the stated buyer manages 40 to 80 client companies.
findings.evidence: bp/docs/BUSINESS_PLAN.md §3: 'Primary: practising Company Secretaries… serving 40–80 clients each'. Main.dc.html header hard-wires one CIN (U74999DL2015PTC000001) with no switcher. In Sentence.dc.html the duties/watch subjects array is ['Sample Company Pvt Ltd']. The Guided.dc.html header shows a single company name. None of the three has a client list, a cross-client deadline view or bulk actions. INTERVIEWS.md §1 confirms the CS buyer.
findings.recommendation: Add a portfolio layer before choosing A, B or C: a matrix of clients × the 15 duties, sorted by nearest deadline. Group abstentions by their cause, e.g. '880(E) unverified blocks s.2(85) for 31 clients', so that one fix clears many rows. That is the 'radically different direction' below.

findings.issue: The copy overclaims coverage. It says 'every duty the Act gives', but the engine has 15 obligations, and the mockups show 7 to 9 rows with no denominator.
findings.evidence: Main.dc.html features[1]: 'See every duty the Act gives it'. Sentence.dc.html verbs.duties.hint: 'Every duty the Act gives a company'. Guided.dc.html task 01 blurb: 'See every duty the Act gives it'. Only C's step-2 text is honest: 'the 15 duties Placedon covers'. backend checker/obligations.py lines 620-793 define exactly 15 obligation IDs. The rows shown are 9 in A, 8 in B (today) and 7 in C. This breaks the AGENTS.md 'Honesty — do not overclaim' section.
findings.recommendation: Replace every instance with 'the 15 duties Placedon covers'. Show the denominator on every duty view (e.g. '9 of 15 shown · 6 don't apply'). Link to a coverage page that lists which common duties are NOT covered (e.g. s.90 SBO and s.139(2) auditor rotation, both listed in BUSINESS_PLAN §2 scope).

findings.issue: The mockups pad the product with features the backend does not serve and the business plan excludes. This hides how narrow the engine is.
findings.evidence: backend checker/api.py:655-661 serves 8 routes: health, ask, compliance-pack, document-check, mca-strip, and 3 event routes. There is no draft route and no counterparty/sanctions route. checker/event_log.py:46 KINDS = (COMPANY_FACT, LAW_CHANGE), with no counterparty or sanctions kind. BUSINESS_PLAN.md exclusions table: 'Drafting… drafting is where professional trust ends'. Yet Drafts is a top-level nav item in A, a verb in B and task 05 in C, and the Watch views show 'OFAC list: no match for 3 counterparties'. INTERVIEWS.md §2: the only buyer-side interviewee asked for PAN/GST/bank-name match, not US OFAC screening.
findings.recommendation: Cut Drafts from the pilot UI. Replace the OFAC counterparty card either with nothing or with the MCA strip (which does have a route). If counterparty checks stay, make them the PAN/GST/name-match the interviewee asked for, and label them 'not built yet'.

findings.issue: 'Can't tell' is a dead end. Missing user facts and Placedon's own corpus backlog are shown with the same grey chip, so the user cannot tell whose job it is to fix. That drives churn.
findings.evidence: Main.dc.html rowsRaw: s.149(3) 'cant' needs the user's director-days, while s.2(85) and s.177 are 'cant' because of Placedon's unreviewed 880(E) and Rule 6. All three use the same '? Can't tell' chip. No mockup gives an input to supply the missing days: C's step-1 inputs are readonly='{{ yes }}', and A's detail panel only states what is missing. In A's duties, 5 of 9 rows are not a verdict (3 cant, 2 pending), and the Overview tile headlines '3 duties' can't tell. The IBBI 'possible match' (a SIGNAL under event_log.py:51) also uses the abstain grey chip, which AGENTS.md reserves for abstention only.
findings.recommendation: Split the non-answer into three visible types. First, 'We need from you', with an inline input so the row resolves on the spot. Second, 'Placedon is still verifying', with an owner and an ETA. Third, 'Signal, not fact'. Show the count of the first type as a to-do. Never put the second type in the user's attention count.

findings.issue: The sentence interface is part gimmick. Only 2 dates are hard-coded, the subjects are canned, and some verb/subject/date combinations make no sense, so 'that is the whole interface' does not hold up in real use.
findings.evidence: Sentence.dc.html: dates = { today, past:'14 August 2025' } is the entire date range, with no picker. The ask subjects are 3 fixed questions and there is no free-text box, unlike A's askbox. The grammar produces 'Show me a draft of a notice of the next board meeting as of 14 August 2025' (drafting a future meeting against past law) and 'what is new for Sample Company as of 14 August 2025', but the watch data ignores the date. The 50px Fraunces sentence cannot hold 40-80 clients or a long question. The timeline is the only part that matches the spec.
findings.recommendation: Keep B's timeline and its movable 'you are here' cursor as the core. Make the date a real picker that is present on every view. Drop the sentence as the navigation.

findings.issue: C is patronising and ceremonial for the primary buyer. A 'We check' step pretends there is processing, and the glossary explains basics to professionals.
findings.evidence: Guided.dc.html needs 3 clicks for every task ('Check it' → 'See the result' → 'Back to all tasks'), yet the engine is deterministic and responds instantly. Step 2 is a narrated checklist. The glossary defines 'Section… s.96(1) means section 96, sub-section 1' and 'CIN… registration number' for a CS who personally certifies MGT-7/AOC-4 (BUSINESS_PLAN §3). The Ask field help says 'Type your question the way you'd ask a colleague'. The result is not kept: 'Back to all tasks' resets task to -1.
findings.recommendation: If C's framing survives, it belongs to the secondary buyer (founders) only. Put the result first and make 'How we checked' an expandable trace. Collapse the glossary by default. Keep results so a CS can return to them.

findings.issue: A looks like every compliance-calendar SaaS. Its one distinctive property, point-in-time law, is shown as static header text.
findings.evidence: Main.dc.html has a sidebar with Overview/Ask/Company duties/Documents/Watch/Drafts and a 4-tile 'What needs attention' grid. The header shows 'Law as of 26 Sep 2026' as a plain span, with no control. There is no timeline anywhere in A, even though UX_INTERACTION_SPEC §4 calls the strip 'Nothing else in this market has this'. A buyer comparing A with TaxGuru/ClearTax ROC calendars would only see a section column as the difference.
findings.recommendation: If A's structure is chosen for familiarity, the as-of date must become a global, interactive control, and the currency strip must appear inline on every figure-based row. Otherwise A is a commodity.

findings.issue: Legal and labelling nuance a practising CS will spot: a duty that is not yet due is labelled 'Not met', and the Ask state names differ from the backend contract.
findings.evidence: A/B/C mark s.96(1) '! Not met yet' / '! Needs action' 4 days before the 30 Sep 2026 deadline. Nothing is overdue yet, and the Registrar's extension under the s.96(1) proviso is not mentioned. I am unsure how obligations.py maps a pre-deadline AGM (APPLIES_NOT_SATISFIED vs APPLIES_UNDETERMINED), so this should be verified. The mockups use '□ Not held' where checker/ask_contract.py:13 STATES uses 'out_of_scope'.
findings.recommendation: Use 'Due in 4 days' for obligations that are live but not yet breached, and reserve '!' for a breach. Add the extension note. Align the state names with the contract, or record the mapping.

findings.issue: B inverts the brand on the main canvas (dark ground) and uses the gold accent as a timeline cursor, while the result sheet is cream. Two themes appear on one screen.
findings.evidence: Sentence.dc.html body background is #0C0C0D, the result article is #F4EFE6, and the cursor is #C9A24B 'you are here'. AGENTS.md allows gold for only one accent element per view, which B does respect. The split theme cuts the result's reading area to about 1440-56*2-300-32 px wide, beside a 300px dark source column in low contrast (rgba .66-.7).
findings.recommendation: Keep one theme per screen. Check the contrast of the rgba(244,239,230,0.66) captions against #0C0C0D at 12-13px.

strengths_worth_keeping: B's timeline with a movable 'you are here' cursor, and its dashed marker for the unverified G.S.R. 880(E). This is the only UI element that expresses the moat and matches UX_INTERACTION_SPEC §4 (dashed segment, instrument number, not 'as amended').

A's Documents view: 'Law it relies on, then' vs 'now', plus the scanned-minutes case ('We don't report problems in a document we couldn't read. Nothing here is a finding'). This is honest abstention done well.
Mono section references and instrument numbers on every row in all three mockups (AGENTS.md brand signature), and no confidence percentages anywhere (ask_contract.py FORBIDDEN_KEYS).
C's step-2 line 'Looked up the 15 duties Placedon covers'. It is the only honest denominator in any mockup and should become the standard wording.
reviews.preferred_direction: None as built. My direction is a hybrid: a multi-client 'CS docket' shell (clients × 15 duties, abstentions grouped by cause), with B's as-of timeline as a global control and inline strip, and A's Documents then/now panel. Drafts and OFAC are cut. The deliverable is an exportable, citation-stamped compliance annexure the CS can attach to a client file. The reason: the buyer's unit of work is the portfolio and the certificate, not one company's screen.
open_questions: What share of the 15 duties × a realistic client mix will come back 'can't tell' or 'pending' at pilot launch? If it is above ~30%, is any UI enough to prevent churn?
Can G.S.R. 700(E) (or any threshold instrument) be verified before the pilot, so the currency strip shows a real figure even once?
Has any practising CS been shown the PARTIAL state (UX_INTERACTION_SPEC §9 falsifier)? What did they say?
Why do Drafts and OFAC counterparty screening appear in all three mockups when BUSINESS_PLAN excludes drafting and api.py has no route for either?
Is the pilot deliverable a screen or an artifact (PDF annexure / MGT-7 working paper) that a CS can put in a client file? The mockups assume a screen.

(4) Watch: opened all four items and read the 'Why you're seeing this' chain. (5) Drafts: tried to approve with the venue blank (locked), then filled it and approved.

The home page promises 'every answer carries the law it rests on and the date that law took effect'. The one screen where that matters most breaks the promise. The backend contract has it: checker/ask_contract.py validates 'instrument' and 'effective_from' on citations. The UI just drops it.

The quote under s.96(1) is the opening words ('Every company other than a One Person Company shall in each year hold…'). The six-month rule the answer depends on is in the first proviso (corpus/companies_act/1287.json). Citing the right section with the wrong words is exactly the failure that made me distrust these tools. Mockup C quotes the proviso correctly.

s.2(85) is shown as 'Can't tell' and s.173(1) as '✓ Met' at the same time. The board-meeting regime depends on small-company status (s.173(5)). Your own engine refuses in exactly this case: checker/obligations.py returns 'the s.173(5) regime depends on small-company status, which cannot be determined'. The UI shows a pass the engine wouldn't give.

Documents labels the draft resolution '⟳ Law has changed' with the amber 'not met' style. Watch labels the same G.S.R. 880(E) '? Needs checking'. So is the law changed or unverified? You can't flag a document as stale on a notification you say you haven't checked.
Overview says 'Documents: 1 relies on old law'. That repeats the same unverified claim as a headline number.

The status labels ('… Not known yet', '! Not met yet') differ from the Ask states ('■ Answered', '◧ Partly answered', '□ Not held'). 'Partly answered' borrows the dotted 'pending' style, so there are two visual languages on one screen.
'Was this useful?' does nothing. 'Copy with sources' is the one button I'd actually use, and I can't see what it produces.
walkthrough.trust_reaction: Not for advice. Maybe as an associate's first-pass checklist, and only if every row opened to the verbatim text, its footnoted amendment history and the effective date. The abstentions ('we won't guess this one') earn some respect. Then the tool marks s.173 Met on facts it can't have, calls a 30 Sep AGM date 'Answered' while ignoring the fifteen-month limb, and says 'hold the AGM' four days out without a word on notice. Any one of those in a DD report with my firm's name on it is a problem. The good part: the detail panel's split between what was found, what is still needed and the rule is the right structure for a DD schedule.

Half of DD asks whether something was valid when it was done, not today. The timeline strip under the sentence (2014 → G.S.R. 92(E) → 700(E) → 880(E), dashed) is the product's best idea, just badly executed.

walkthrough.trust_reaction: As a daily tool, no. It's a single sentence with canned answers, white text on black, sized for a keynote. As a concept I'd steal two things. First, a global 'law as of [any date]' control. Second, the per-provision currency strip with real figures and G.S.R. numbers. Build those into A. An associate who can prove what the figure was on the date of an allotment saves me a paragraph of caveats in the DD report.

walkthrough.first_60_seconds: 'What do you need to do today?' and five task cards with 'Start'. This is written for a founder or a junior CS, not a law firm. The three-step 'Tell us / We check / Your result' pattern is clear. The glossary ('Section: A numbered part of an Act') is fine for a founder and patronising to anyone on my floor. I'd hide it by default.
walkthrough.tasks_tried: Ran all five tasks through all three steps. Jumped straight to step 3 with the step buttons (allowed). Went back. Filled the venue and approved the draft.
confusions: Step 1 fields are read-only. The only thing I'm told is 'Filled in with sample data'. So 'Tell us' tells me nothing about what I'd actually have to enter.

Provenance gap. Step 1 of 'Company duties' collects name, CIN, type, FY end, number of directors and last board meeting. Yet step 3 says 'No CSR committee needed: below all three limits' and '✓ Met' for board meetings. I never supplied net worth, turnover or profit, and a single last-meeting date can't prove four meetings with 120-day gaps. Where did those facts come from? That's precisely the question I'd ask an associate.
Step 2 lists '✓ Done: Checked each section is in force as of 26 Sep 2026' without showing a single effective date. A checkmark that says 'trust me, I checked' is exactly what I don't trust.

The Ask task shows the right proviso quote ('…within a period of six months, from the date of closing of the financial year.'). Better than A. Its step 2 then says 'No notification has changed this rule since, so none is cited'. Since when? Say 'unchanged since [date] per India Code as fetched on [date]'.
The document task marks '! Found an issue: That law changed after the document was written' based on G.S.R. 880(E), which the same screen calls 'not yet checked'. It's the same contradiction as A.
The Watch task's result label '4 new items' has the pending chip. That isn't a status, it's a count.
walkthrough.trust_reaction: Clearest for a layperson. Least useful for me: it's one company, one task at a time, and hides the evidence behind steps. The 'We check' step is the right idea (show the working), but it has to show dates, instruments and verbatim text, not checkmarks. I wouldn't put this in front of an associate on a DD. I might put it in front of a client's finance team.

quotes: "You quoted the opening words of 96(1) and gave me the answer from the proviso. That is the exact failure that got the last AI tool thrown out of my practice group."

"'Hold the AGM by 30 September' when it is 26 September? There's no mention of 21 days' notice, shorter-notice consent or an extension from the Registrar of Companies (ROC). A first-year would get that note back from me in red."
"You say you haven't checked 880(E) against the Gazette, and in the next breath you tell me my resolution relies on 'old law'. Pick one."
"The notification is dated 1 December 2025 and it's September 2026. Ten months and nobody has read the Gazette? That's not honesty, it's a staffing problem you've made into a feature."
"The 'as of' date is the only thing here I'd pay for. Give it to me for any date, show me the rupee figure at that date, and give me the G.S.R. number next to it."

"Where do my documents go? Which server, which country, who can read them, are they used for anything? None of the three screens says a word about it, and that's the first question my General Counsel will ask."
"I don't use tools. My associates do. Show me what they hand me: a schedule I can paste into a DD report with the date the law was pinned."
"Honestly, 'can't tell' is the most reassuring thing on the screen. It's the green ticks that worry me."
legal_objections: s.96(1): 'Last allowed date 30 Sep 2026' is labelled '■ Answered' (A, B, C), but it only applies the six-month proviso. The substantive limb also caps the gap between AGMs at fifteen months. Without the last AGM date the answer is at most 'Partly answered'. It also ignores the third proviso (Registrar may extend by up to three months). Both are in corpus/companies_act/1287.json, and checker/obligations.py _decide_agm checks the fifteen-month gap, so the UI is less careful than the engine.
A's s.96(1) quote is the section's opening words, but the six-month rule it relies on is in the first proviso. The citation doesn't support the proposition. C gets this right.

AGM four days away: the 'What to do' in A's Watch ('Hold the AGM by 30 Sep 2026') and C's result say nothing about s.101 notice (21 clear days), shorter-notice consent of members, or whether the articles modify this for a private company under the 2015 private-company exemption notification (I believe G.S.R. 464(E); unverified). Nor do they say that an ROC extension has to be sought before the due date. On these facts the advice is incomplete to the point of being dangerous.

s.137 (A and B '… Not known yet' / C '… Comes later'): 'The deadline counts from the AGM date, which isn't set yet' is wrong as stated. s.137(2) (corpus 1328.json) sets a backstop if no AGM is held: 30 days from the last date the AGM should have been held, i.e. 30 Oct 2026 here. checker/obligations.py _decide_aoc4 doesn't implement s.137(2) either. That's a backend gap, not just a UI one.

s.92(4) (A): the same point. The engine's own docstring notes the 'should have been held' limb (sixty days from 30 Sep 2026, i.e. 29 Nov 2026). The UI should show the latest possible date, not 'isn't set yet'.

s.173(1) '✓ Met' (A, B, C) while s.2(85) is '? Can't tell'. The board-meeting regime depends on small-company status (s.173(5)), and checker/obligations.py explicitly refuses in this case. 'Met' is also premature with three meetings in a year still running. It should read 'on track', not 'met'.

s.177 '? Can't tell' for a private limited company. As I understand it, Rule 6 of the Companies (Meetings of Board and its Powers) Rules, 2014 prescribes only classes of public companies. The abstention is technically defensible because the rule text is unreviewed, but a practitioner answers it in seconds and the tool looks ignorant. Review Rule 6 before launch.

s.149(3): 'stayed in India … during the year' (A, B). Say 'financial year'. That's the current wording as I recall it, after the 2017 Amendment Act, and the corpus should confirm it. The period matters in DD.

s.135(1): 'below all three CSR limits on the figures supplied' doesn't say which financial year's figures. The test is the immediately preceding financial year. Mockup C never collects those figures at all.

Document checks (A, B, C): whether an AGM notice was valid is mainly a s.101/s.102 question (notice period, explanatory statement), not a s.96 one. '✓ Verified' on 'What it is' overclaims, and 'Signature: no digital signature found' is irrelevant for most notices.

The '⟳ Law has changed' flag on the 14 Aug 2025 resolution rests on G.S.R. 880(E), which the product itself calls unverified. That breaks the product's own abstention rule and would wrongly cast doubt on a client document in a DD report.
B's timeline shows G.S.R. 700(E) as solid/verified, while B's answer text says the copy is 'waiting for a person to review it'. The display contradicts itself on the point that matters most.

The small-company limits are never shown as rupee figures in any mockup, so a practitioner can't check them. (The spec itself says the 2025 figures need primary-source verification. I can't confirm the G.S.R. 880(E) number or date from memory.)

Draft board notice (A, B, C): no time of meeting, agenda, date of notice, signatory or video-conference option. It also recites statutory compliance in the notice body ('sent at least seven days ahead, as s.173(3) requires'), which no practitioner drafts and which asserts a sending that hasn't happened. 'Approve' after filling only the venue gives a false sense of completeness.

'Approved and recorded' (A, C): software approval of a draft is not a board act. The wording should make clear it's the user signing off a draft, with name and time. It should also have a maker-checker step, because I delegate.

Watch sanctions: '✓ Checked … no match' against OFAC alone isn't a sanctions clearance for an Indian DD. It needs the UN Security Council consolidated list and the Indian (MHA/UAPA) lists at least, and it should state its name-matching method. A tick implies clearance.

Nowhere does the tool pin and show which version of its law text it used (it keeps sha256 and fetched_at per section in the corpus JSON). Without that, an output can't be defended later when someone asks 'what did the tool say on that date and why?'.
must_haves: On every row and answer: the verbatim operative words (the right sub-clause or proviso), the instrument (G.S.R./S.O. number), the effective-from date and the amendment footnotes. One click away, not hidden behind a checkmark.
A global 'law as of [any date]' control (B's idea) in the A layout, applied consistently to duties, answers, documents and watch. Not two hard-coded dates.
A currency strip with actual rupee figures per node and G.S.R. numbers, per UX_INTERACTION_SPEC.md §4, with a table fallback.
An export: a DD schedule in Word/PDF with section, finding, still needed, source, effective date, 'as of' date and corpus version or hash, suitable to paste into a DD report annex.
Many entities at once: DD targets and their subsidiaries, not one sample company. CIN lookup to pull MCA master data (the backend already has POST /v1/mca-strip).
A written confidentiality position on screen: where data is stored (India), retention, who can access it, that nothing is used for training, and the NDA/privilege posture. Ideally a no-upload mode.
Consistent status semantics across all screens. One state per instrument: if G.S.R. 880(E) is unverified, every dependent output is 'can't tell', never 'law has changed' or 'Met'.
Maker-checker: associate prepares, partner or senior associate approves, with names and timestamps in the record.
A visible list of what Placedon does NOT check (all 15 duties shown, plus the untested ones), so omissions are explicit.
Practical-consequence notes where the law creates them: backstop deadlines under s.137(2) and s.92(4), notice periods, ROC extension.
dealbreakers: Any green '✓ Met' or 'Answered' that the engine itself would not produce (s.173 while small-company status is unknown; s.96 ignoring the fifteen-month limb). One such false pass in a DD report ends the trial.
Any quote that doesn't contain the words the answer relies on (A's s.96(1) quote).
No clear statement on data residency and confidentiality before any client document is uploaded (Documents in A and C, Watch counterparties).
No pinned version, date and hash on outputs, so the tool's answer can't be reproduced later.

Obvious notifications left 'not yet checked against the Gazette' for months (G.S.R. 880(E), dated 01 Dec 2025, still unchecked on 26 Sep 2026). If the Gazette isn't read, the product's core promise is empty.
Canned-question-only interaction (B) in the shipped product.
personas.would_use_weekly: No for me personally. Maybe for my associates on DD mandates, but only as a first-pass applicability checklist, and only once the must-haves exist: verbatim text with effective dates, any-date 'as of', export, many entities, and a confidentiality statement. The fixes the product has to make first are removing false passes and settling the conflicting states for unverified notifications. Covering only the Companies Act, and only about 15 duties, also limits it. A real DD touches FEMA, stamp duty, labour and sector rules, so this would be one annex, not the workflow.
personas.willingness_to_pay: Hourly billing makes 'saves associate time' a weak argument. I'd pay for defensibility and for fewer written-off hours on fixed-fee DDs. That means a firm-wide licence, not per-seat for partners, bought the way we buy research databases. My simulated guess: a free pilot on two live mandates, then perhaps ₹3–6 lakh a year firm-wide if it produced exportable, date-pinned DD schedules across many entities with MCA data. Zero if any false pass turned up during the pilot. Per-query or per-company pricing wouldn't suit how a firm like mine budgets. (Simulated figure, not market research.)
personas.preferred: A. Its row list with the 'What we found / Still needed / The rule' detail panel is the closest to a DD schedule an associate would build, and it holds up on a large monitor. It needs B's 'as of [any date]' control and currency strip (with real figures), and C's 'We check' idea turned into real evidence (dates, instruments, verbatim text). B is the most distinctive concept and the least usable screen. C suits founders or a client finance team, not a law firm.

personas.persona: Simulated General Counsel, mid-size listed Indian manufacturing company (parent listed on the main board, 12 subsidiaries of which roughly 9 are private companies, 1 is a step-down foreign-facing entity and 2 are public unlisted). Legal team of four plus one company secretary on the payroll. Reports to the board and the audit committee. Owns the legal-tech budget. Today uses a secretarial compliance tool licensed through the CS team, an Excel master calendar, and trials of GC AI-style assistants. Sceptical of anything that "knows the law" and of anything I cannot put in front of the audit committee. Simulated feedback, not a real interview.

walkthrough.first_60_seconds: I got it at once: a sidebar with Overview, Ask, Company duties, Documents, Watch, Drafts, and a header saying 'Law as of 26 Sep 2026'. The four tiles (AGM due in 4 days, 3 duties can't tell, 1 law change, 1 document on old law) are the right idea for a Monday-morning view. Then I looked for the entity switcher and there isn't one. The header shows one CIN, U74999DL2015PTC000001, fixed. I have thirteen entities. That was my first 60 seconds: this is built for one company, not a group.
walkthrough.tasks_tried: (1) Overview, AGM tile, then Company duties: clicked s.96(1), s.173(1), s.2(85) and s.177 and read the detail panel. (2) Filters: 'Needs attention' shows not met, can't tell and pending together, which is what I want. (3) Ask: clicked all three sample questions and typed my own ('What is the notice period for our AGM as a listed company?'). All I got was 'This mockup answers the three sample questions above.' (4) Documents: all three. The scanned-minutes result ('We don't report problems in a document we couldn't read') is the most honest line in the product. (5) Watch: read the 'Why you're seeing this' path chips for G.S.R. 880(E). (6) Drafts: filled the venue and approved.

No calendar. There is no month view, no ICS export, and no 'next 90 days' list. The only dates are inside row text. The business plan's own interview says the real need 'is a calendar-and-status problem' (bp/docs/INTERVIEWS.md), and the UI doesn't show one.

The s.173(1) row is 'Met' with the text 'Three held this year'. s.173(1) needs at least four meetings a year. 'On track' is not 'Met'. Calling it Met is how a junior gets something wrong in a board note.
The duty list has no owner, no assignee, no 'done / evidence attached'. My team is four people. Who is handling the AGM?
'Copy with sources' and 'Was this useful?' in Ask do nothing. That's fine for a mockup, but I can't tell what 'copy with sources' produces, and that output is what I'd paste into a board note.
The Watch 'Law change' item says 'What to do: Nothing yet.' I want to know who is checking it and by when. An open item with no owner and no ETA is useless to me.
Drafts: the approve button unlocks once 'venue' is filled, but the notice has no meeting time and no agenda. Placedon calls it complete when it isn't.
walkthrough.trust_reaction: Partly. I would trust the abstentions ('can't tell', 'not held', 'couldn't read') more than I trust most tools, because they refuse to bluff. I would not trust the green 'Met' chips. Two of them rest on facts the screen shows it doesn't have: the 15-month limb for the AGM and the four-a-year count for board meetings. I would not put this output in front of the audit committee without my CS re-checking every 'Met'. That means it saves me nothing on the rows that matter.

walkthrough.first_60_seconds: A black screen and a 50px serif sentence: 'Show me what the law requires of Sample Company Pvt Ltd as of today.' The strapline says 'Click any underlined words to change them. That is the whole interface.' It's clever. My first thought was that my team won't use this daily. My second was that the timeline and the 'as of' date are the only genuinely new thing across all three mockups, and I'd want that inside A or C.
walkthrough.tasks_tried: (1) Changed verb to 'the answer to' and cycled the three questions. (2) Moved the date to 14 August 2025 and re-read Duties, Ask and Document check. (3) 'what has changed under' the draft board resolution of 14 Aug 2025, today and past. (4) Watch and Draft verbs. I tried to type a date and couldn't: the date tray offers only 'today' and '14 August 2025'. I tried to pick a different company and the subject tray has one entry.
confusions: You can only choose two dates. The feature I'd pay for is 'as of the date of this board meeting' or 'as of the date the transaction was approved', and I can't enter one.

It contradicts itself on the same instrument. The timeline plots G.S.R. 700(E) as a solid (verified) dot. The past-date small-company answer says 'Our copy of it is waiting for a person to review it, so we show no limit'. The past-date document check then marks 'Law it relied on, then' as '✓ Verified' for a resolution relying on those same 700(E) limits. One of those three is wrong.

Timeline: '2014 · s.2(85) in force' followed only by notifications. The definition's statutory ceiling was itself amended by the Companies (Amendment) Act, 2017, if I remember right. I'd want the Act amendments on the same line, not just G.S.R.s. I'm not certain of the commencement date, so check it.
The 'What the marks mean' legend uses glyphs (✓ ! … – ?) while the Ask answers use a different set (■ ◧ □). That's two symbol systems on one screen.
Dark background with 12px text at 60-66% opacity in the timeline sub-labels ('2025 · not yet checked'). My board members are over 55. I'd get complaints.
There's no navigation back to a list of things needing attention, so there's no inbox. Every visit starts from a blank sentence.
walkthrough.trust_reaction: Not for daily use. I'd trust the concept of a point-in-time answer more than anything in A or C. That is exactly what a GC needs when a regulator asks 'what did the law say when you approved this?' But the three-way contradiction on G.S.R. 700(E) in this very file would make me distrust the whole product in a demo. If I saw that live, the meeting would be over.

walkthrough.first_60_seconds: 'What do you need to do today?' and five task cards (Company duties, Ask, Documents, Watch, Drafts), each Tell us / We check / Your result, plus a glossary explaining what a Section, CIN and Gazette are. I understood it in ten seconds and felt talked down to in twenty. This is built for a founder with no CS, which is fine, but it isn't me. The step 2 'We check' list is good: it shows the audit trail of what the engine did.
walkthrough.tasks_tried: All five tasks, all three steps each. I tried to edit the step 1 fields to enter a subsidiary's facts and couldn't: every input is readonly ('Filled in with sample data'). I clicked the step buttons out of order. Step 3 is reachable without passing step 2, which is fine. On Drafts I filled the venue and approved.

Task 01 step 2 says 'Looked up the 15 duties Placedon covers'. Step 3 shows 7 rows. Where are the other 8? A says 9 of 15. The two mockups disagree on how many are shown and neither lists the rest.

Task 02 step 2 says 'No notification has changed this rule since, so none is cited.' 'Since' when? It doesn't say.

The 'Other laws: FEMA, SEBI, IBC and more / Not yet' card is honest. But SEBI LODR is half my compliance calendar, and seeing it greyed out on the home page tells me on day one that this covers maybe 40% of my obligations.

The step 2 'here is exactly what Placedon checked' list is the single element I'd show my audit committee, because it's a process record. For my practice, though, C is a teaching UI. "The 'as of' date in the dark one is the only thing here my current secretarial software can't do. Put it in the normal app and let me type any date."
"Your own business plan says listed companies aren't the buyer. Fine. Then don't put SEBI on the roadmap card, or tell me when it's coming."
legal_objections: s.96(1) AGM answer overclaims (A: Ask q1 and duties row 1; B: Ask; C: task 02 'Answered'). The copy itself cites the second limb: 'no more than fifteen months after the last one'. No mockup captures or shows the date of the last AGM. If the last AGM was, for example, 20 Jun 2025, fifteen months ends 20 Sep 2026 and the AGM is already late. The answer should be 'partial' and name 'date of last AGM' as missing, or show the gap limb as checked. The backend already decides the gap limb from supplied AGM dates (checker/obligations.py _decide_agm, lines ~299-330). The UI discards that input.

s.96(1) proviso: the Registrar can extend by up to three months, and general extensions have been granted in past years. 'Last allowed date 30 Sep 2026' should say 'absent an extension'. The backend docstring says the extension limb is 'NOT decided here' (checker/obligations.py ~line 301), so the UI must not present 30 Sep as absolute.

AGM notice period (s.101: 21 clear days, shorter notice only with member consent) is absent. A 4-days-out alert with no AGM on record is really 'notice deadline already missed unless you obtain consent for shorter notice'. A GC calendar must back-compute notice and dispatch dates, not only meeting dates.

s.173(1) marked '✓ Met' on 'Three held this year' (A duties row 2, B dutiesToday, C task 01). The section requires a minimum of four meetings every year. Three by September is 'pending/on track', not met. Separately, the backend's s.173 check itself declines when small-company status is undetermined ('the s.173(5) regime depends on small-company status, which cannot be determined', checker/obligations.py ~line 270). The same sample company shows s.2(85) as 'Can't tell', so the engine as written would not return Met for s.173 at all. The mockup is inconsistent with the backend.

s.173(1) 120-day computation: 'last was 16 Jun 2026... next is due by 14 Oct 2026'. The statute says not more than 120 days shall 'intervene' between two meetings. Whether 14 or 15 Oct is the last permissible date depends on exclusive or inclusive counting. Show the counting convention, or my CS will argue about it in every review.

s.2(85) 'Can't tell' for Sample Company is presented as blocked only on G.S.R. 880(E). The s.2(85) proviso excludes holding and subsidiary companies (and s.8 and special-Act companies) regardless of limits, and the backend models this (checker/classify.py lines 16, 78, 248: 'a subsidiary is excluded by the proviso'). The mockups never ask whether the company is a holding or subsidiary. For all 12 of my subsidiaries the answer is determinable today ('not small, proviso (A)'), and the UI would wrongly show 'Can't tell'.

G.S.R. 880(E) (dated 01 Dec 2025 in the mockups) as the 2025 small-company revision: I believe the thresholds were revised again in late 2025, but I am not sure of that notification number or date. The mockups treat it as unchecked, which is correct. The Document-check '⟳ Law has changed' verdict (A doc 2, B doc 2 today, C task 03 '! Found an issue') then asserts a change based on that same unchecked instrument, which breaks the product's own abstention rule.

G.S.R. 700(E) is inconsistent within B. The timeline dot is solid (verified), the past Ask says 'our copy is waiting for a person to review it', and the past document check says '✓ Verified' for law relying on it. The verification status of one instrument must be one fact, shown identically everywhere.

Draft board notice (A Drafts, B draft verb, C task 05): (a) a notice cannot certify its own dispatch ('It is sent at least seven days ahead, as s.173(3) requires'). Placedon does not know the dispatch date, and that line would sit wrongly in a statutory notice. (b) There is no meeting time and no agenda. Secretarial Standard SS-1, made mandatory via s.118(10), expects date, time, venue and agenda with notes. (c) There is no video-conference participation option. Approval unlocking after the venue alone gives false assurance of completeness.

s.177 audit committee row says 'can't tell' pending Rule 6. For a listed parent, s.177 applies on the face of the Act (the mockup's own basis text says 'Every listed public company'). A group product must decide the Act limb first and abstain only on the prescribed-class limb.

Watch / sanctions: 'Sanctions: no match for 3 counterparties' against OFAC alone is a misleading comfort statement for an Indian entity. The UN Security Council consolidated list and Indian notified lists (UAPA/MHA) are the primary ones. Label the chip by list checked, e.g. 'OFAC SDN: no match', never a generic 'Sanctions ✓'.

Watch / insolvency: IBBI announcements only. For counterparty risk I'd also expect NCLT admission orders and the IBBI CIRP public announcements with CIN. The mockup's 'compare CINs' advice is right, but the product should do the CIN comparison itself, since the CIN is in the announcement.

'Checked each section is in force as of 26 Sep 2026' (C task 01 step 2): in force per what source? I need the commencement notification (S.O. number) for each section on the result, not just the section number. That is the product's own promise ('the notification that set its wording and the date it took effect'), and none of the Duties rows shows an instrument or effective date except the s.2(85)/177 abstentions.

Listed-company duties are wholly absent: SEBI LODR reg. 17-21 board committees, reg. 30 disclosures, s.149(1) woman director and s.149(4) independent directors for listed companies, s.203 KMP. For my parent entity the 15-duty list covers a minority of what I track. The business plan explicitly excludes listed companies (bp/docs/BUSINESS_PLAN.md s.2 'SEBI / listed company obligations' and s.3 'Not the buyer: ... listed companies'). The UI should state that scope limit on the duties screen, not only on a greyed card in C.
must_haves: Multi-entity: a group/portfolio view across all CINs with an entity switcher, and facts entered once per entity and remembered. Rows should show the entity name.

A real compliance calendar: next 30/90/365 days across entities, with back-computed notice and dispatch deadlines (s.101 AGM notice, s.173(3) board notice), filing deadlines (s.137 30 days, s.92(4) 60 days), and ICS/Outlook export.
Every 'Met' must show the facts it relied on and the limbs checked. Where a limb (15-month gap, four-a-year count, first-AGM nine months) wasn't tested, the row cannot be Met.
One verification status per instrument, shown identically on the timeline, Ask, Duties, Documents and Watch, with who verified it and when.
Free 'as of' date entry (from B), available inside the normal workspace. Point-in-time answers are the differentiator.
An exportable, board/audit-committee-ready report: PDF/Excel with section, instrument, effective date, status, facts relied on, generated-at timestamp and engine version.

Ownership and workflow: assign a duty to a team member, attach evidence (minutes, filing SRN), maker-checker approval on drafts, and an audit log of who approved what. 'Approved and recorded' must name the person.
Watch items with an owner and ETA for the verification backlog (e.g. 'G.S.R. 880(E) review scheduled by <date>'), and email/Teams alerts. I won't log in to look.
A clear scope statement on every results screen: 'Companies Act, 2013 only; 15 duties; SEBI LODR, FEMA and labour not covered'.
The s.2(85) proviso (holding/subsidiary) captured in company facts, so subsidiaries resolve without waiting on thresholds.
The step 2 'what Placedon checked' trace from C, available as an expandable panel on every A-style row.
dealbreakers: Single-company only. If the group view isn't there, I stop evaluating. I will not maintain 13 separate workspaces.
Any green 'Met' that rests on a fact the product never collected (s.96 last-AGM date, s.173 four-a-year). One of those in a board pack and the tool is banned by my CS.

Internal contradictions on verification status (G.S.R. 700(E) in B; 880(E) 'unchecked' yet driving a '! Found an issue' / '⟳ Law has changed' verdict). If the product can't agree with itself, I can't cite it.
No export or audit trail. Output I can't put in an audit committee file has no value to me.
No SEBI/listed-company coverage, and no roadmap date. I'd accept this only if it's priced as a subsidiary-level tool, not a GC tool.

Unclear AI use. The pitch says no language model decides anything, but the business plan prices a measured '₹2.91 per answer' on 'Sonnet' (bp/docs/BUSINESS_PLAN.md s.4). I need a written statement of what, if anything, a model touches (question parsing? wording?) before my IT and data-protection review signs off. I may be misreading that cost line, so clarify it.
personas.would_use_weekly: Maybe, and only for the subsidiaries. As shown, no. None of the three mockups handles more than one company, there's no calendar or export, and the parent's listed-company duties are out of scope. If A gained a group view, a real calendar with notice-date back-computation, B's free 'as of' date and C's 'what we checked' trace, my CS would use it weekly for the nine private subsidiaries. I'd look at the group dashboard weekly and at Watch whenever an alert arrived. The abstentions are the reason I'd keep it. The overclaimed 'Met' chips are the reason I'd drop it.
personas.willingness_to_pay: In its current single-entity form: nothing. That's a founder's tool, and the plan's ₹3,000-6,000 per year band (bp/docs/BUSINESS_PLAN.md s.4) is about right for it. With multi-entity, calendar, export and audit trail: roughly ₹1.5-3 lakh a year for the group (13 entities, 5 seats), benchmarked against our secretarial software licence and what a GC AI-style seat costs. I'd need a paid pilot at a fraction of that for one quarter, with a written accuracy and abstention report at the end. SEBI LODR coverage would roughly double what I'd pay. Without it, this is a supplementary tool, not a replacement for anything.
personas.preferred: A as the base, taking B's 'as of' date control and timeline (made free-entry and put in A's header next to 'Law as of') and C's step 2 'Here is exactly what Placedon checked' trace as an expandable panel on every A row and answer. B alone is a demo, not a daily tool. C alone is for a first-time founder and is too slow and patronising for a legal team. Whichever is chosen, fix the engine-truth issues first: the s.96 15-month limb, s.173 'Met' on three meetings, the s.2(85) proviso, and one verification status per instrument. Those decide trust, and layout doesn't.
