walkthrough.first_60_seconds: OK, this is a normal dashboard, so I know where things are. Sidebar has Overview, Ask, Company duties, Documents, Watch and Drafts. The home tiles say 'AGM due in 4 days', '3 duties can't tell', '1 law change' and '1 relies on old law'. My first question is: which company? The header shows one company, Sample Company Pvt Ltd, and there is no client switcher. I have 40 clients. My real first question every morning is 'which of my clients are in trouble this week', and this screen cannot answer it. The 'New here? Here is everything Placedon does' block with five cards is marketing I will scroll past from the second day on.
walkthrough.tasks_tried: (1) Company duties: I clicked the rows. s.96(1) shows 'Not met yet', due 30 Sep 2026, none on record. s.173(1) shows 'Met' with three meetings and the next due 14 Oct 2026. I checked the arithmetic: 16 Jun plus 120 days is 14 Oct, and 102 days ago is right. s.137(1) and s.92(4) show 'Not known yet' because the AGM date isn't set, which is fair. The footer says 'Showing 9 of the 15 duties' and I cannot see the other six. (2) Ask: I tried the three canned questions. Typing my own question only shows 'This mockup answers the three sample questions above'. The AGM answer is clean and quotes s.96(1). 'Copy with sources' is the button I would actually use, to paste into a client email. (3) Documents: 'Minutes, scanned copy - Couldn't read'. That is exactly what my clients send on WhatsApp, and it fails. (4) Watch: the OFAC match and IBBI name match are there, and the 'Why you're seeing this' path is nice. (5) Drafts: I filled the venue and Approve unlocked.
confusions: Only one company. There is no client list, no switcher and no cross-client view of 'due this week'.
The overview tile says '3 duties' can't tell, but the duties screen shows only 9 of 15. Which 3 out of how many? What about the six hidden duties?
The duty labels 'Not met yet' and 'Not known yet' are close enough to misread when I scan quickly.
Watch shows G.S.R. 880(E) as '? Needs checking', but Documents shows the same notification as '⟳ Law has changed' in the stronger warning colour. Either you know the law changed or you don't.
In the draft notice there is no field for the meeting TIME, and Approve still unlocks after I type only the place.
The draft body includes 's.173(3) requires... latest allowed date is 14 Oct 2026' inside the notice text. Is that meant to go to directors? No real notice says that.
No form names anywhere: AOC-4, MGT-7/MGT-7A, ADT-1, DIR-3 KYC, MGT-14. I think in forms, not sections.
walkthrough.trust_reaction: Partly. I would trust the s.96 date arithmetic and the verbatim quote. I would not trust the duties table, because it marks s.173(1) 'Met' while the same screen says small-company status is 'can't tell'. Which s.173 regime applies depends on that status. Your own engine refuses this case: obligations.py _decide_board returns None with 'the s.173(5) regime depends on small-company status, which cannot be determined'. So the mockup overclaims beyond what the engine would say. Once I see one confident green tick that is wrong, I stop trusting every green tick.

walkthrough.first_60_seconds: A black screen with a huge serif sentence: 'Show me what the law requires of Sample Company Pvt Ltd as of today'. It looks like a design award entry. It took me a moment to see that the dotted words are the controls. The timeline showing 2014, G.S.R. 92(E), G.S.R. 700(E) and G.S.R. 880(E) (dashed) is actually the most interesting thing I have seen in any of the three. I have never had a tool show me which notification governed on a given date.
walkthrough.tasks_tried: (1) Changed the date to 14 Aug 2025. The duties list changes, and s.173 becomes 'can't tell' because the sample has no older meeting dates, which is honest. (2) Changed the verb to 'the answer to' and picked 'Are we a small company?'. I got 'We can't confirm this yet', and on the past date it says 'G.S.R. 700(E) awaiting review'. So the product cannot tell me small-company status on ANY date, old or new. (3) Tried 'what has changed under the draft board resolution of 14 Aug 2025'. The sentence is ungrammatical and I had to read it twice. (4) Tried to type a question. There is no text box. I can only choose from three questions. (5) Draft: filled the venue and approved.
confusions: The only date choices are 'today' and '14 August 2025'. For point-in-time work I need any date: the date of a past default, a condonation or compounding matter, or the date a client's resolution was passed.
'what has changed under the AGM notice of 01 Jun 2024' is not English a CS would say.
The legend uses symbols (✓ ! … – ?) while the sheet uses words, and 'Not known yet' here is called 'Comes later' in mockup C. Three mockups use three vocabularies.
The dark theme and 50px serif are hard to read for long, and useless on my phone.
There is no way to pick a client, upload a document or type anything except the venue.
walkthrough.trust_reaction: I trust its honesty more than A's. It tells me when it doesn't know. But I cannot work in it. It is a demo of the idea of point-in-time law, not a place I would clear 40 clients' September filings. The timeline should be a feature inside A, not a product of its own.

walkthrough.first_60_seconds: 'What do you need to do today?' Five task cards, plus a dashed card for FEMA/SEBI/IBC saying 'Not yet'. That card is good, because it tells me up front what not to ask. Each task has three steps: Tell us, We check, Your result. The glossary on the right explains what a 'Section' and a 'CIN' are. I have been a CS for years, so this is written for my client's accountant, not for me.
walkthrough.tasks_tried: (1) Company duties: Step 1 shows the prefilled fields, read-only. Step 2 lists 'Looked up the 15 duties...' as a checklist. Step 3 gives the result, headlined '1 duty needs action now'. That is three clicks to reach what A shows in one. (2) Ask: same three steps for one question. Step 2 says 'No notification has changed this rule since, so none is cited'. (3) Check a document: 'Draft board resolution.pdf', and the result chip is '⟳ The law has changed since'. (4) Drafts: the one blank is the meeting place, and there is still no time field. (5) Watch: four items, and the result chip '4 new items' uses a status colour for a plain count.
confusions: Step 2 'We check' is theatre for me. Show me the result and let me expand the audit trail if I want it. At 40 clients, three clicks per task is 120 clicks I don't have.
The Step 1 fields are read-only, so I can't test changing, say, the number of directors.
The Ask flow puts a single question through a wizard. No one asks a colleague a question in three steps.

The Documents Step 2 says 'That law changed after the document was written' with '! Found an issue', while the same page admits G.S.R. 880(E) is not checked. That contradicts the 'never guess' promise on the home page.
The duties result shows 7 rows, not 15, and has no s.92(4) row. Mockup A has s.92(4), so the two mockups show different duty sets.
'Back to all tasks' after the result means I lose the result, and I see no save, export or history.
walkthrough.trust_reaction: Same data as A, so the same s.173 'Met' problem. The wizard makes it feel slower and more 'consumer', which lowers my trust that it is built for professionals. I would recommend C to a founder who doesn't have a CS. I would not use it myself.

quotes: I have forty clients. Where is the list of forty clients?

You told me AGM by 30 September with four days left. Fine. But no notice has gone out, and s.101 wants 21 clear days. What I actually need to hear is 'you need short-notice consent or a GNL-1 extension'. You didn't say that.
You're telling me s.173 is met while you can't tell me if the company is small. Those two can't both be right.
Audit committee, can't tell, for a private limited? Rule 6 only talks about public companies. That one row makes me doubt the rest.
Every client sends me WhatsApp photos of signed minutes. If 'scanned copy - couldn't read' is the answer, the Documents tab is dead for me.
The timeline with the notifications is the first genuinely new thing I've seen. Put it in the normal app.
Nobody sends a board notice that explains s.173(3) to the directors, and it has no time of meeting. I can't send this.
ComplyRelax is free. For money I need something ComplyRelax can't do, and that is the all-clients deadline view plus point-in-time law.
Copy with sources is the one button I'd press daily.
OFAC? My clients are small trading and IT services companies in Bengaluru. Nobody is asking me about the US Treasury.
legal_objections: s.96(1) AGM advice is incomplete (A, B, C). As of 26 Sep 2026 with no AGM on record, the practical question is notice. s.101(1) needs 21 clear days, so an AGM by 30 Sep now requires shorter-notice consent under the s.101(1) proviso (majority in number and 95% of paid-up share capital), or an extension of up to three months from the RoC under the s.96(1) proviso via Form GNL-1, applied for before the due date. The backend already lists the RoC extension as a limb it cannot decide (obligations.py, the limbs_not_decided note beside the AGM obligation), but none of the mockups show that caveat. A 'Last allowed date 30 Sep 2026' shown without 'unless extended by the RoC' overstates things.

s.173(1) marked 'Met' in A (rowsRaw), B (dutiesToday) and C (tasks[0].rows) is wrong in two ways. First, the applicable regime depends on small-company status: s.173(5) gives small companies at least one meeting in each half of the calendar year with a gap of at least 90 days. All three mockups say that status is 'can't tell', and obligations.py _decide_board refuses the same case with 'the s.173(5) regime depends on small-company status, which cannot be determined'. So the mockups contradict both the law and the engine. Second, even under the standard regime, 'three held this year' is not yet 'four every year'. In September the correct state is 'on track / pending', not 'Met'.

s.177 audit committee shown as 'can't tell' for a PRIVATE company (A, B). To my understanding, Rule 6 of the Companies (Meetings of Board and its Powers) Rules, 2014 prescribes only classes of PUBLIC companies (paid-up capital of 10 crore or more, turnover of 100 crore or more, or loans, debentures and deposits above 50 crore). A private company is outside s.177 on the face of the Act and the Rule. The engine abstains because the Rule is 'held but not reviewed' (obligations.py, S-177-RULES), which is principled, but to a practitioner it reads as not knowing the basics. At minimum the row should say 'applies only to public companies; your company is private; Rule not yet reviewed' rather than a bare '? Can't tell'.

The draft board meeting notice (A Drafts, B draft, C task 05) is not a valid notice. It has no time of meeting. There is no mention of video-conferencing participation, which, as I recall, s.173(2) and Rule 3 of the Meetings of Board Rules require the notice to offer where that facility is provided. There is no agenda, and SS-1 expects the agenda and notes to go with the notice. It also embeds statutory commentary ('as s.173(3) requires', 'latest allowed date 14 Oct 2026') in text meant for directors. Approve unlocks once only the venue is filled, which contradicts the rule 'approval locked while anything is blank'.

Unverified notification treated as a finding (A Documents '⟳ Law has changed' on the draft resolution; C task 03 '! Found an issue'). The product admits G.S.R. 880(E) is 'not yet checked against the Gazette' (A Watch, B timelineNote), yet in Documents it asserts the resolution relies on superseded limits. Pick one: the document check should be '? Can't tell whether the limits changed' until the instrument is verified.

The promise is 'exact section, the notification that set its wording, and the date it took effect'. The Ask answers show only 'Companies Act, 2013 · s.96(1)', with no commencement instrument and no in-force date. I believe s.96 commenced on 1 Apr 2014 via the general commencement notification, but I'd want the product to show it. C even says 'No notification has changed this rule since, so none is cited', which is the opposite of the headline promise.

Small-company status is unanswerable on every date shown. Today depends on G.S.R. 880(E), which is unverified, and 14 Aug 2025 depends on G.S.R. 700(E), which is 'awaiting review'. Small-company status drives MGT-7A versus MGT-7, the s.173(5) meeting regime, the cash flow statement exemption, auditor rotation and more, so leaving it open blocks a large share of the practical value. Separately, I am not certain the Dec 2025 revision is numbered G.S.R. 880(E). Please verify the number and date before putting it on a timeline.

Duty coverage misses what drives my September: DIR-3 KYC (Rule 12A of the Appointment and Qualification of Directors Rules; I'm not certain whether the annual cycle has since changed), ADT-1 within 15 days of the AGM (s.139), MGT-7A for small companies/OPCs, and late-fee computation under the Registration Offices and Fees Rules. A shows 'Showing 9 of the 15 duties' and C shows 7, and neither lists which 15.

Sanctions watch checks OFAC only. For an Indian private company, the UN Security Council consolidated list and the MHA UAPA designated lists are the relevant ones. Showing '✓ Checked, no match' against the US list alone gives a false sense of clearance.

IBBI counterparty match by similar name (A and C Watch) should match on CIN first. Showing a 'Possible match' with the CIN comparison left to me is fine as a flag, but the CIN should be displayed side by side.
must_haves: Multi-client portfolio view: all my companies, sorted by nearest statutory deadline, with a filter for 'due in the next 7/30 days'.
Deadlines expressed as MCA forms (AOC-4, MGT-7/7A, ADT-1, DIR-3 KYC, MGT-14, DPT-3, MSME-1) with due date and late-fee exposure, not just section numbers.
AGM row that knows about notice (s.101 21 clear days, short-notice consent) and RoC extension (GNL-1), and says 'last date unless extended'.
No 'Met' when a prerequisite classification is 'can't tell'. Row states must match what the engine in obligations.py actually returns.
Scanned/photographed document intake that works on WhatsApp-quality images, or at least lets me type the date and document type when OCR fails.
Free-text Ask with 'Copy with sources' output I can paste into a client email, including section, instrument and in-force date.
Arbitrary point-in-time date picker (B's timeline idea) inside the normal workspace, not only today and one preset date.
Draft notices that are legally complete (date, time, venue, VC option, agenda) with no statutory commentary in the body, exportable to Word so I can put it on the client's letterhead.
A visible list of which duties are covered and which are not.
One consistent set of status words across all screens.
dealbreakers: Single-company only. If I have to open 40 separate workspaces, I won't use it.
A confident 'Met' that is wrong (the s.173 row). One false green tick and I stop relying on the tool, because it is my professional liability, not yours.
Scanned documents failing by default, since that is 90% of what I receive.
Draft notices I can't send without rewriting them. ComplyRelax templates are already sendable and free.
Mockup B as the main interface: no client picker, no typing, two dates, no phone usability.
Mockup C's forced three-step wizard for every task, at my volume.
Pricing per client. At about ₹1,000-2,000 a year for the whole practice I'll try it, but per-client pricing kills it.
personas.would_use_weekly: Maybe, and only as mockup A with a multi-client view added. The honest 'can't tell' and 'Copy with sources' are genuinely useful for client emails and for protecting myself. But today it covers one company, a subset of duties, no forms and no scans, while my week is AOC-4, MGT-7 and DIR-3 KYC across 40 clients. Without the portfolio deadline view I'd open it maybe once a month for a point-in-time question.
personas.willingness_to_pay: Per practice, not per client. I'd pay ₹1,000-2,000 a year to try it, which is the practice-management band BUSINESS_PLAN.md itself cites. I'd go to ₹3,000-6,000 a year only if it gives me the 40-client deadline dashboard with form-level due dates and late-fee exposure, plus the point-in-time notification timeline. ComplyRelax is free for me as an ICSI member, so drafting alone is worth zero to me.
personas.preferred: A (Workspace). It is the only one I could work in quickly and repeatedly. Two changes: add a client switcher and a portfolio home, and move B's notification timeline and any-date picker in as a feature on each duty and answer. C's glossary and wizard suit a founder with no CS, not me. Offer them as an optional 'explain' mode at most. B is a good demo for a pitch, not a working tool.

personas.persona: SIMULATED user (not a real interview). A junior associate in the first week at a mid-size corporate law firm in Delhi. Fresh law graduate. Has only used case-law and statute search databases. Not yet confident on the Companies Act, 2013. A senior has said "check this company's compliance position by end of day". Opens Placedon with no training, is short on time, is sceptical of anything that looks like a black box, and is scared of handing the senior something wrong.

walkthrough.first_60_seconds: OK, this looks like software I already know. The first thing I read is the tile 'AGM due in 4 days'. Good, that's an obvious fire to report to my senior. The 'New here? Here is everything Placedon does' block and the 'How to read the labels' legend on Overview helped me. Within a minute I knew the five tools and what the five chips mean. legal_objections: AGM advice is incomplete and could mislead (A Company duties s.96(1) row and Watch 'What to do: Hold the AGM by 30 Sep 2026'; B duties; C task 01 headline). Four days out, with no AGM on record, a general meeting can't be convened on the standard 21 clear days' notice under s.101(1). The practical options are shorter-notice consent (s.101(1) proviso) or, if already missed, the consequences under s.99 and default filings. Also, the s.96(1) proviso extension by the Registrar (up to three months, not for the first AGM) is never mentioned. I'm unsure how the private-company exemption notification of 5 Jun 2015 affects s.101 via the articles, so the product should flag that too rather than stay silent.

The s.173(1) 'Met' row is internally inconsistent with the s.2(85) 'Can't tell' row (A rowsRaw s.173(1) st:'met'; B dutiesToday; C task 01 rows). s.173(5) gives small companies a relaxed regime, so which regime applies depends on small-company status. The backend agrees with me. In /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-abdulazeez/8ba6f282-a147-4e24-95e0-1aee555fec91/scratchpad/placedon-law-backend/checker/obligations.py, the s.173 decider (around lines 266-274) returns None with 'the s.173(5) regime depends on small-company status, which cannot be determined' when small_company refuses. So the mockup shows a 'Met' the engine would not produce. It should read 'Can't tell' or 'On track under either regime', with the reasoning shown.

'Met' is also a forward-looking overclaim for s.173 ('Three held this year ... next due by 14 Oct 2026'). Four meetings a year can't yet be 'met' in September with three held. That's 'on track', not 'met'. And 'this year' should say whether it means the calendar year (the Secretarial Standard reading) or the financial year.

s.177 audit committee shown as 'Can't tell' for a PRIVATE company (A rowsRaw; B dutiesToday). s.177(1) and Rule 6 of the Companies (Meetings of Board and its Powers) Rules, 2014 are framed around listed public companies and prescribed classes of PUBLIC companies. To my understanding a Pvt Ltd falls outside, so this should be 'Doesn't apply'. The backend's _audit_committee returns INSUFFICIENT_DATA for every non-listed-public company (obligations.py around lines 144-164), so the error comes from the engine, not just the mockup. I'm a week-one associate, so a senior should confirm, but I'd raise it. Over-abstaining on a clear point makes me doubt the abstentions I can't check.

The board notice draft (A Drafts, B Draft, C task 05) has no TIME of meeting, no agenda, no date of notice, no signatory ('By order of the Board'), and no mode of participation. Under Secretarial Standard 1 (as I understand it) a notice states date, time and venue and carries the agenda. The notice text also recites its own compliance ('sent at least seven days ahead, as s.173(3) requires'), which doesn't belong in an operative notice. The 'Approve' button unlocks once only the venue is filled, so 'nothing is blank' is false when time and agenda are missing.

The core promise, 'the section, the notification that set its wording, and the date it took effect', isn't shown on the answered Ask state. A's source panel shows 'Companies Act, 2013 · s.96(1)' with no commencement date or instrument. C step 2 says 'No notification has changed this rule since, so none is cited' but still gives no in-force date. I believe s.96 commenced 1 Apr 2014, but I'm not certain of the notifying S.O. number, and I shouldn't have to know it: that's the product's job.

The document check asserts '⟳ Law has changed' (A docsRaw; C task 03 resLabel and step 2 'That law changed after the document was written') based on G.S.R. 880(E). Every other screen calls 880(E) unverified. Asserting a change on the strength of an unverified instrument contradicts the product's own abstain-rather-than-guess rule. It should be 'A later notification may have changed this, not yet checked'.

CSR row 'Doesn't apply: below all three limits' (A, B, C) shows no figures, no year, and no mention of which financial year is 'immediately preceding'. I can't verify it, and 'figures you gave us' isn't something I can cite in a note.

s.149(3) copy in B says 'days each director spent in India this year'. The test runs over the financial year, and the proviso for newly incorporated companies is different. A says 'during the year'. Say 'financial year'.

The sanctions check uses OFAC only (A Watch; C task 04). For an Indian company a practitioner would expect UN Security Council and MHA/UAPA lists as the baseline. A US-only list shown with a '✓ Checked' chip suggests diligence that hasn't been done.
'Is this a small company?' is presented as a duty in all three. It's a classification that drives other duties, and mixing it into the duty list muddies what the company must DO.

No 'not legal advice / verify before relying' boundary, and no statement of the corpus version date anywhere on the duties sheets. For a tool whose output a junior might forward, that's a professional-responsibility gap.

In the C task 01 flow, 'Last board meeting 16 Jun 2026' alone isn't enough to decide s.173. You need all the meeting dates in the period, and the backend itself refuses without them. The input form should ask for the full list.
must_haves: A way to enter or look up a REAL company (CIN field or MCA master-data pull) and edit the facts. Without this I can't do my actual task in any mockup.
An explicit coverage statement on every duties result: 'Placedon checks N duties. It does NOT cover: [list]. This is not a full compliance review.' Plus a 'show all 15' option.
An exportable, dated memo or PDF of the duties sheet, with each row's section, in-force date, notification, facts relied on, and what's missing. Something I can attach to an email to my senior.
On every answer: section + in-force date + instrument (or 'original text, no amending notification'), plus the actual statutory text in a panel, as A's s.96(1) quote does.
A single 'What we still need from you' list that collects the missing facts from every 'Can't tell' row into one form.
Consistent labels across every screen (one vocabulary for Met / Not met / Pending / N.A. / Can't tell), and rename '□ Not held' to something like 'Law not in Placedon'.
A date control that either applies to EVERY view or visibly says 'this view ignores the date'.
Practical next-step guidance where the law gives options (AGM: notice period, shorter notice, extension), not just 'hold it by X'.
C's glossary and 'We check' log kept in whatever design wins.
dealbreakers: Any 'Met' or 'Doesn't apply' that turns out to be wrong. One wrong green row, like s.173 while small-company status is unknown or CSR without figures, and I stop trusting the whole sheet. That's worse than no tool.
Not being able to put in my own company. A sample-only product is a brochure.
Silent partial coverage: presenting 7 or 9 duties as 'the compliance position'.
A date control that ignores the date on some screens (B Watch and Draft).
Stating the law has changed on the basis of an instrument the product itself says is unverified.
An 'Approve' button on a draft that is legally incomplete (no time, agenda or signatory), because it suggests the draft is ready to send.
personas.would_use_weekly: Maybe, and only C (or A with C's glossary and 'We check' log). As a first-year I'd use it weekly as a starting checklist and a way to find the right section fast, especially the 'can't tell, here's what's missing' rows, which teach me what facts to ask the client for. I would not use it as a source to cite until it covers my company, shows in-force dates and instruments on every answer, and fixes the s.173/s.177 inconsistencies. B: no.
personas.willingness_to_pay: Personally nothing. I'm a first-week associate and the firm pays for tools. I'd push for a firm trial if it could produce an exportable, dated, sourced duties memo for a real CIN. I'd tell my senior it's worth roughly what the firm pays for one more search-database seat per team, provided the coverage disclaimer is clear. I'm not the buyer, so treat this as low-confidence.
personas.preferred: C - Guided. It's the only one where I understood the scope in the first minute (the 'Not yet: Other laws' card), found my exact task on the first screen, and understood the terms (the glossary). Its 'We check' step gives me a basis-of-review I can show my senior. For a second or later visit I'd want A's Company duties detail panel (What we found / Still needed / The rule) and A's 'Showing 9 of 15' honesty brought into C. B is last: it's the most striking design, but I can't type a question or enter a company, and the date control is unreliable across views.

agree_with: Backend alignment engineer, critical finding 1, and Legal auditor, critical 2: the '880(E) not yet checked' story is out of date. I re-checked this. corpus/sources/gsr880e_registration.json has classification VERIFIED_INSTRUMENT (line 26) and status CORROBORATED (line 31). This changes my own Round 1 finding. The contradiction between Documents and Watch goes away once the sample data is regenerated. It was never a wording problem.

Backend engineer, critical 2, Legal auditor, critical 1, and all four simulated customers: s.173(1) 'Met' cannot happen while s.2(85) is unresolved, and three meetings in September is not 'met'. This is the most damaging comprehension failure in all three mockups, because users generalise from one false tick to every tick. The CS said 'Once I see one confident green tick that is wrong, I stop trusting every green tick', and the junior said 'One wrong green row... worse than no tool'.

Backend engineer, critical 3, and Legal auditor, major (15-month limb): the flagship 'Answered: By 30 Sep 2026' is really a partial answer. The first-time user's first answer must not be an overclaim.

Interaction critic, major 3, and Feasibility lead, major (StateChip): split the vocabularies into three separate components. Obligation rows get 5 states. Ask turns get 3 states, shown as a heading word rather than a chip. Process ticks get a plain mark. This is a stronger version of my own critical finding on status vocabulary, and I adopt it.

Devil's advocate, major ('Can't tell is a dead end'): split non-answers into 'We need this from you' (with an inline input), 'Placedon is still verifying' (with an owner and ETA), and 'Signal, not fact'. This fixes my APPLIES_UNDETERMINED vs CANNOT_DETERMINE comprehension finding better than relabelling alone. It is phrased as whose move it is, and a novice can act on that.
Trust reviewer, critical 1, and Legal auditor, major (OFAC): a sanctions 'no match' in the met/checked style reads to a novice as clearance. The junior persona read it exactly that way.
Accessibility specialist, critical 1, and Interaction critic, minor: require 360px frames before scoring layouts. I did not weight this enough in Round 1.

Accessibility specialist, major 3: move focus to the new result heading and announce the state word in a live region. It also helps sighted first-time users, who currently cannot tell that C's step content changed above the button.

Product strategist, critical 2, and Devil's advocate, critical 2: the buyer works across a portfolio. Three of the four simulated customers named single-company scope as a dealbreaker ('I have forty clients. Where is the list of forty clients?').

Legal auditor, major (s.137(2) and s.92(4) fallback deadlines), and the CS persona on s.101 notice: 'isn't set yet' hides the most useful fact. Showing outer deadlines is a comprehension gain as well as a legal one.
Brand guardian, critical 1: gold-muted on the 'not met' chip. Accessibility and brand agree that 'needs action' should be encoded in ink weight plus a glyph.

challenge.target: Devil's advocate, critical 1 (SOURCE_880 = 'UNRESOLVED' means the moat never answers; 'hold the UI decision until a threshold is verified')
challenge.argument: The evidence is misread. At checker/prescribed_thresholds.py:101-106, SOURCE_880 is described as the marker 'an UNSERVABLE 880(E) row shows', i.e. the India Code handle placeholder. It is not the instrument's verification state. The registration JSON is VERIFIED_INSTRUMENT/CORROBORATED, and the backend engineer's live /v1/ask run served ₹10 cr with 880(E) and its effective_from. The moat can answer today. The fix is to regenerate the samples, not to hold the decision.

challenge.target: Brand guardian, vote B-as-frame (score 7.5)
challenge.argument: Brand distinctiveness is being scored above whether users can get the job done and whether the answer is true. B's central interaction (moving the date into the past and recomputing everything) is forbidden in v1 by PLAN_13 §9 and is buggy even as a mockup: Watch and Draft ignore the date. Every simulated persona rejected B as a working tool. B's dark shell with a 50px italic sentence also fails reflow and focus visibility. Keep B's devices (the one gold cursor, the per-provision strip), not its frame.

challenge.target: Accessibility specialist and Frontend feasibility lead, vote C as shell
challenge.argument: A reflow-friendly structure does not have to be a wizard. C's home hides the only urgent item, and C forces 3 clicks per task. Both personas who do repeat work (CS, GC) called that disqualifying, and even the junior who preferred C asked for A's detail panel. The feasibility lead's own recommendation for A (URL segments /app/duties/[id], so the detail pane collapses to list→detail on narrow screens) gives the same 360px behaviour without a mandatory step. C's contribution should be its language, the glossary and the 'How we checked' trail, not the gating.

challenge.target: Trust reviewer, preferring C's shell because disclosure happens at intake
challenge.argument: Disclosure belongs next to the control that triggers it (the upload button, the counterparty list), and that control exists in any shell. Choosing the shell for that reason costs urgency on the home screen for no disclosure gain.

challenge.target: Product strategist, 'cut ... the permanent glossary', and Devil's advocate ('patronising')
challenge.argument: Make it collapsible, not gone. The junior associate called C's glossary 'the first time any legal database has explained what a G.S.R. is without making me feel stupid', and founders are the secondary segment. An on-demand drawer, closed by default, with dotted-underline popovers on first use costs a professional nothing.

challenge.target: Brand guardian, badge word 'Abstained' / 'Abstained in part'
challenge.argument: I accept the brand word only if every badge carries its reason in the same line. The junior misread 'Not held' as 'meeting not held', which shows that bare badge words fail on first read. Proposed: 'Abstained: law not in Placedon (FEMA)' and 'Abstained in part: needs date of last AGM'. The badge word alone must never be the whole message. This needs a 5-user test before it is frozen.

challenge.target: Product strategist and Devil's advocate: settle the buyer before any direction
challenge.argument: Agreed that it must be settled. But a portfolio layer sits on top of the per-company workspace; it does not replace it. A multi-client home still drills into A's per-company duties and detail view. So the council can choose the per-company layout now and make the portfolio home a gating condition, instead of blocking all layout work.

challenge.target: Simulated GC persona, SEBI LODR / listed coverage as a dealbreaker
challenge.argument: Do not let it pull scope. BUSINESS_PLAN.md §3 says listed companies are not the buyer. The comprehension fix is an explicit scope line on every duties result ('Companies Act, 2013 only · 15 duties · SEBI/FEMA not covered'), not new coverage.

debates.changed_my_mind: Yes, on three points. (1) I had treated 880(E)'s 'not yet checked' state as a real abstention whose only problem was inconsistent wording. The engine holds it CORROBORATED (I re-read the registration JSON), so the right fix is to regenerate every sample from engine output. Relabelling would have made the mockups honest-looking and wrong. (2) I had scored A's home as the gold standard, but A's '1 duty needs action now' and 'AGM due in 4 days' headlines come from a row state the engine does not return (backend engineer). The attention home must be driven by the derived-deadline items and missing-fact counts the engine actually produces. (3) I underweighted the portfolio buyer and the 360px requirement. My A score stays highest for per-company comprehension, but I no longer think any mockup as built is fit to pilot.
debates.vote: Hybrid 'A-core': A's per-company workspace (a duties table with a What we found / Still needed / The rule detail panel, an honest Ask with all three states shown, and an attention home computed from engine output) under a multi-client portfolio home. Grafted on: B's one-gold, per-provision currency strip with a date control limited to what the engine covers; C's plain language, a glossary drawer closed by default, and 'How we checked' as a collapsible trail. Drafts and OFAC are cut from the pilot.
non_negotiables: Every sample state must be engine-reproducible: regenerate the fixtures from real /v1/compliance-pack, /v1/ask and /v1/document-check output. No 'Met' or 'Answered' the engine would not return (s.173, s.149(1), s.96 as Answered). 880(E) is shown as held, with ₹10 cr, the G.S.R. number and 'in force from 01 Dec 2025' beside the figure.

One status grammar in three separate components: 5 obligation row states keyed to ROW_STATES, 3 Ask states shown as a heading word, and plain process ticks. out_of_scope never shares the abstain style. Signals (IBBI) never use the verified style. A single label table is shared by the site and the app.

Every non-answer says whose move it is: 'We need from you: <fact>' with an inline input, 'Placedon is still verifying: <instrument>, owner/ETA', or 'Signal, not a finding'. Every abstention badge carries its reason in the same line.

Urgency is visible on arrival: the home screen (portfolio or company) shows the nearest real deadlines, including derived outer deadlines (s.137(2), s.92(4)) and notice-by dates, ranked. No wizard gate before a result. 'How we checked' is collapsible.
Coverage is honest: all 15 duties can be reached, the denominator is shown, and a scope line appears on every duties and answer view. Never write 'every duty the Act gives'.

Any date control applies to every visible view or visibly disables itself with a reason. Past dates are limited to figures the engine covers and carry the 'section text is today's consolidation' line.
No control looks interactive while doing nothing. Read-only sample fields look read-only, and dead buttons are disabled with the reason stated.
A 360px frame of the Ask partial answer and of the duties view must exist and pass before build. Focus goes to the new result heading and the state word is announced.

Usability test with 5 target users (at least 2 practising CSs) before the labels are frozen. Pass bar: each can explain the difference between 'we need a fact from you' and 'Placedon is still verifying', and none reads a sanctions or 'Met' row as more than it is.

agree_with: Usability researcher, 'status vocabulary is not consistent' (critical, ALL): I agree. For assistive tech this is also an accessibility problem. The chip is announced as its text, so '✓ Met', '✓ Verified', '■ Answered' and '✓ Checked' become four spoken words sharing one visual style. A screen-reader user and a sighted user end up learning different mappings. One label table keyed to obligations.py ROW_STATES and ask_contract.py STATES fixes both groups at once.

Usability researcher, B's date control does not apply to Watch or Draft (critical): I agree, and this is also a 3.3.x / 1.3.1 problem. The heading 'as of {{ dateShort }}' (Sentence.dc.html:78) programmatically labels content it does not govern, so a screen-reader user who navigates by heading gets a false context with no visual cue to correct it.
Frontend feasibility lead, one StateChip component keyed on RowState/AskState: I agree. It is also the only practical way to make my 'glyph in an aria-hidden span' fix stick across the product.

Frontend feasibility lead, App Router segments for the duty detail and the Ask turn, plus C's URL-addressable steps: I agree. Real navigation gives us focus reset and browser back/forward, and it fixes the silent screen swaps in A (Main.dc.html main area swaps with focus left on the sidebar) without hand-built focus management.

Interaction critic, ServiceError must not look like an abstention (critical): I agree. Changing PLAN_13's dashed Ink-80 border to solid also removes a case where only colour tells two dashed-grey states apart (1.4.1). The ServiceError card also needs role=alert, not the polite live region.

Interaction critic and Product strategist: require a 360px frame before choosing a direction. This matches my Round 1 critical finding (1.4.10 Reflow; PLAN_13_ASSISTANT_UX.md:75 'the pane is the deliverable').
Interaction critic: the Ask state should be a heading word, not a chip (PLAN_13 row 1). It gives screen-reader users a heading to jump to and the live region a single word to announce. I adopt it.

Brand guardian, re-token 'needs action' in ink with a heavier border and '!' rather than gold-muted: I agree. A solid 2px ink border also clears 1.4.11 on cream, which the current 1.5px #9F743B on #FBF3E2 barely does.

Brand guardian, B's 11px timeline sub-labels at 60% opacity: I agree with raising them to 12px or more. My Round 1 computed that rgba(.6) on ink passes 4.5:1 (6.49:1), so size, not contrast, is the failing dimension.

Trust reviewer and Legal auditor: the OFAC 'no match' must not use the met chip. Beyond the legal risk, the chip's accessible text is '✓ Checked', which is what a screen-reader user hears with no qualification. The qualifying sentence must be in the same accessible name or linked with aria-describedby, not only in a nearby body paragraph.

Devil's advocate: split 'can't tell' into 'we need from you' (with an inline input) and 'Placedon still verifying'. That split creates the inline, labelled form fields a keyboard user can act on in place. Today C's read-only inputs (Guided.dc.html:103) are focusable fields that silently refuse input, which confuses screen-reader users (announced as 'edit text, read only' at best).
Backend and Legal auditors: 880(E) is CORROBORATED, so the dashed 'unverified' node in B is false. Dashed-means-abstain is the non-colour encoding I endorsed, and it has to be true to be accessible.

challenge.target: Usability researcher and Legal auditor: 'A as the base' on first-time comprehension and fewest unsupported claims
challenge.argument: A's comprehension score was earned at 1440px with a 248px sidebar, a three-column Ask (280/1fr/320, Main.dc.html:108) and a 380px detail aside (Main:174-176). None of that exists at 360px or in the 320-400px Word pane. There the sidebar becomes a menu, the master-detail becomes two views, and the Overview's feature strip plus tiles plus legend stack into several screens of scrolling. So we have not measured A's first-60-seconds advantage in the target container at all. Choose A's content (attention tiles, the What we found / Still needed / The rule panel, 'Showing N of 15'), not A's shell, unless someone draws A at 360px and it survives.

challenge.target: Brand guardian: B's dark ink shell as the frame
challenge.argument: B's frame is the hardest of the three to make accessible. It has no h1-h6 at all (I re-checked: grep finds headings only in Main and Guided). The tray is inserted after all three slot buttons, which breaks focus order (2.4.3). The timeline is absolutely positioned at percentages with no table fallback (UX_INTERACTION_SPEC §7). Its base rule is 2.91:1, failing 1.4.11. The 50px italic sentence cannot reflow. Keeping the ink shell and the gold cursor as brand elements is fine. Making the sentence the frame is not.

challenge.target: Brand guardian's rationale that the gold cursor is B's single accent
challenge.argument: The cursor is a 2px vertical line and the only indicator of 'you are here'. As built, it carries position meaning with nothing but a thin coloured line (1.4.1/1.4.11 risk depending on background). If it survives, it needs a text label ('Today, 26 Sep 2026') and must be exposed as the current row in the table fallback (aria-current).

challenge.target: Product strategist and Devil's advocate: 'collapse the glossary by default' and 'patronising'
challenge.argument: I agree with collapsing it, since a persistent 330px column cannot survive 360px anyway. But do not delete the function. Defined terms are a WCAG 3.1.3/3.1.4 (AAA) aid, and the junior-associate persona called C's glossary 'the first time any legal database has explained what a G.S.R. is'. Make it an on-demand disclosure plus dotted-underline <dfn> popovers on first use, reachable by keyboard (a button, not hover-only).

challenge.target: Usability researcher: 'Make the header date a control' (borrowing B's slot)
challenge.argument: The direction is right, but B's slot pattern is the wrong control: a button whose accessible name is a sentence fragment and that opens a two-option tray that destroys focus on close. Use a native date input (or labelled combobox) with a visible label 'Law as of', min/max bounded to engine coverage (the backend engineer notes s.2(85) before 15-Sep-2022 returns ThresholdUnavailable), and an aria-describedby note explaining the coverage floor. Out-of-range dates must be refused with an inline error (3.3.1), not silently accepted.

challenge.target: Frontend feasibility lead, streaming out (minor)
challenge.argument: I agree that streaming should go. The pending state still needs an accessible announcement: useFormStatus pending must set aria-busy on the answer region and announce 'Checking the source' once. Otherwise a fast deterministic reply and a hung request sound the same (nothing).

challenge.target: Interaction critic: 'give the answer column at least 640px next to a 320px Sources column'
challenge.argument: That is a desktop-only fix. It must be paired with the PLAN_13 below-820px rule (one column, Sources as an in-flow disclosure after the answer), or it recreates the reflow failure.

debates.changed_my_mind: Partly. In Round 1 I preferred C as the structural base mainly because it collapses to one column. Two things shift me. First, the customer feedback (CS, GC and partner all rejected the forced three-step wizard) and the interaction critic's point that 'We check' is ceremonial convinced me that C's wizard gating is the wrong behaviour. The accessible part of C is its one-column order, its <ol> steps with aria-current, and its text-row provenance, and those survive as an expandable 'How we checked' section. Second, the backend and legal findings showed that the trust signals I was protecting (the dashed 880(E) node, '✓ Met' on s.173) are factually wrong. So encoding correctness comes before encoding accessibility. I have not changed my view that no direction should be chosen without a 360px frame, and that B's sentence-as-frame is the least accessible. I also could not resolve my open question about how the dc runtime renders disabled='false' or readonly. There is no support.js in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-abdulazeez/8ba6f282-a147-4e24-95e0-1aee555fec91/scratchpad/mockups/project (only canvas.json and the three .dc.html files), so this remains unverified and is moot for the Next.js rebuild.
debates.vote: Hybrid 'single-column core, A content': a one-column-first layout that collapses to the 320-400px pane (C's flow order and <ol>/aria-current step semantics, with the wizard gate removed). It contains A's attention tiles (ranked) and A's duty rows with the What we found / Still needed / The rule detail as a routed view. It adds C's glossary as an on-demand disclosure, a native bounded 'Law as of' date input (B's idea, not B's slot widget), and B's timeline rebuilt as a real <table> with a visual strip on top, per provision. Drafts, OFAC and IBBI are out.
non_negotiables: A 360px frame (and a 320px Word-pane frame) of the home, a partial Ask answer with verbatim text, and the duty list must exist and pass 1.4.10 Reflow before build. No root overflow:hidden, and no fixed-px grid columns below 820px.

A focus indicator of at least 3:1 against its actual background on every surface: a two-tone ring (ink outline plus cream halo). This fixes the 1.0:1 cases on A's and C's dark chrome and B's cream sheet.

Every result or answer region is an <article> with an h2. On change, focus moves to that h2 and one polite live region announces the state word. ServiceError uses role=alert and looks nothing like an abstention (solid rule, no dashed treatment).

Programmatic state for everything selected or current: aria-current on nav and steps, aria-pressed or aria-selected on rows and options, radio groups (fieldset/legend) instead of B-style trays. Visible selection indicators must be at least 3:1 and not a background tint alone (A's 1.16:1 row tint fails).

One label table in code (StateChip) keyed to ROW_STATES and Ask STATES. Glyphs go in an aria-hidden span, the word is the accessible name, and out_of_scope gets a style distinct from abstain. Qualifiers such as 'OFAC SDN only, exact-name, as published <date>' must be part of the accessible name or linked with aria-describedby.

Provenance must never be conveyed by underline style or colour alone. Use C-style text rows, or visually hidden text or aria-describedby on each span, and no gold-vs-black distinction without a shape difference.
Any timeline or currency strip must have a real <table> underneath: instrument, what changed, in force from, verification state. The 'you are here' cursor needs a text label.

Real forms: the Ask form submits with Enter via onSubmit (no page reload), inputs have <label for>, read-only sample fields look read-only and say so, and the Approve lock uses aria-disabled plus aria-describedby pointing at the reason, not native disabled.
Input and secondary-button boundaries at 3:1 or better (1.4.11). Text floor 12px, and 13px for sections, instruments and dates. A global prefers-reduced-motion rule. 44px targets kept.
The duty list uses table semantics (or a list with explicit header association), and a filter that hides the selected row resets or re-selects visibly.

agree_with: Legal accuracy auditor, findings 1 and 2, and all three customer personas: s.173(1) 'Met' is impossible. obligations.py _decide_board returns None while s.2(85) is undetermined, and s.173 counts only calendar years that have ended. Also, 'three meetings' is not 'four'. This is the single most trust-destroying pixel in all three mockups.

Legal auditor, finding on s.137(1): the UI omits the no-AGM backstop, and I would sharpen it. I re-checked the code. The backstop is an ENGINE gap for AOC-4 and a UI gap for MGT-7. _decide_aoc4 (checker/obligations.py:429-445) returns None with 'no AGM date was given' and has no s.137(2) limb. _decide_annual_return (447-469) does implement the 'should have been held' limb for s.92(4). The partner persona's claim that s.137(2) is not implemented is correct. The auditor's framing covers only half of it.

Legal auditor and CS/associate personas on s.177: I confirmed obligations.py:145-164. For every non-listed company, including Pvt Ltd, _audit_committee returns INSUFFICIENT_DATA pending S-177-RULES review. The mockup copy faithfully reflects an engine abstention that practitioners read as ignorance. The fix is to review Rule 6 in the backend first, not to change the UI.

Usability researcher finding 3 and my own round 1: s.149(3) is APPLIES_UNDETERMINED, not CANNOT_DETERMINE. The two abstention states must be visibly distinct and each must name its blocker (missing_facts vs blocked_by).

Usability researcher finding 8 and legal auditor minor finding: document check flagging '⟳ Law has changed' is wrong on two counts. The premise that 880(E) is unverified is false, and a threshold INCREASE cannot flip a small company to non-small. The engine's document_check does return superseded for s.2(85) on any pre-Dec-2025 date, so this is also a backend noise problem. document_check should narrow to obligations the document relies on, or report direction of change.

Frontend feasibility lead findings 1-2: types.ts ENGINE_ROUTES and AGENTS.md are stale. ask()/mcaStrip() and a zod askSchema mirroring contract.md are step 0 for ANY direction. Drafts, upload, counterparty Watch have no route.

Trust reviewer on OFAC/IBBI: checker/feeds/ofac_sdn.py says an empty screen means 'not on the list as published on <date>', says fuzzy matching invents hits, and marks feeds LICENCE_UNVERIFIED (never commercial). No mockup may render a met-style tick or a 'similar name' insolvency match.

Product strategist, trust reviewer, devil's advocate: cut Drafts from the pilot. drafting.py implements only an AGM notice, needs a named reviewer, and has no route. The business plan excludes drafting.

Accessibility and interaction critic: ServiceError must never look like abstention (AGENTS.md; errors.ts EngineResult already separates transport failure). A dedicated non-dashed 'No result' card is required.

Brand guardian: gold-muted #9F743B is for citations only and Cool Grey dashed is for abstention only. The status chip must be keyed to backend enums, not reused across VERIFIED_FACT/SIGNAL/process ticks.

Product strategist, devil's advocate, CS and GC personas: a multi-entity/portfolio home is required. This is compatible with the backend because compliance-pack is stateless per-profile and can be fanned out per CIN server-side.

challenge.target: Devil's advocate, finding 1 (cites prescribed_thresholds.py:108 SOURCE_880 = 'UNRESOLVED' as proof 880(E) is unresolved)
challenge.argument: This misreads the file. Lines 102-108 describe SOURCE_880 as the fallback marker shown only while the registration is NOT attested. _source_880() (320-331) returns served_source_url(registration()) whenever the record is attested. corpus/sources/gsr880e_registration.json says classification VERIFIED_INSTRUMENT, status CORROBORATED. My round-1 live runs served ₹10 cr under 880(E) from 2025-12-01 and ₹4 cr under 700(E) for 14-Aug-2025. So the premise that the moat 'abstains in every demo state' is an artefact of stale mockup copy, not an engine limit. The recommendation to 'hold the UI decision until 700(E) is verified' is therefore unnecessary. The fix is to regenerate the sample from engine output. Caveat: the Gazette match is automated and download provenance is null, so the honest label is 'attested by a named reviewer; Gazette copy matched automatically'.

challenge.target: Product strategist, finding 1 caveat, and legal auditor's open question on whether 700(E)/880(E) are servable
challenge.argument: This is resolved rather than open. Both are servable in the live handlers today (all_thresholds() CORROBORATED; /v1/company/{cin}/events returns THRESHOLD_MOVED as VERIFIED_FACT). The council should treat it as settled, with the Python-3.9 scratch-copy caveat. Then the real residual s.2(85) blocker becomes the proviso facts (holding/subsidiary/s.8/special Act) and whatever exclusion the engine reports as unverified, not 880(E).

challenge.target: Brand guardian's preferred direction: B as the frame
challenge.argument: B's frame asserts global point-in-time law. PLAN_13 §9 says as_of is today-only in v1, and ask.py sets point_in_time_verified=False even when a date is passed. The engine supports past as_of only for prescribed thresholds (from 15-Sep-2022) and row decisions over supplied facts, not section text, Watch or drafts. A dark sentence shell that promises date travel everywhere would ship the exact overclaim the brand forbids. Brand signature must not outrank engine truth. Keep B's timeline as a per-figure component.

challenge.target: Legal accuracy auditor and interaction critic: 'no date travel at all' / 'fix the cursor at today'
challenge.argument: This overcorrects. For thresholds the engine genuinely answers past dates (14-Aug-2025 gives 700(E) ₹4 cr with effective_from/effective_to). That is the one capability the partner and GC personas said they would pay for. The correct rule is narrower: allow as_of per figure key within its coverage floor, refuse below it (ThresholdUnavailable before 15-Sep-2022), and label every past view 'section text is today's consolidation'. This needs a written PLAN_13 amendment, not a ban.

challenge.target: Accessibility specialist and frontend lead: C as the shell
challenge.argument: C's step 2 'We check' narrates checks no route returns ('Checked each section is in force', 'No notification has changed this rule'). ask_contract.validate rejects stages on general turns (K9) and rejects effective_from on section citations. Building C means either inventing engine output client-side or collapsing step 2 into response fields. Once step 2 is collapsed, C is A's result pane with extra clicks. C's reflow advantage is real but can be achieved in A's IA with one-column stacking below 820px.

challenge.target: Usability researcher: C 'most usable' / junior associate persona preference for C
challenge.argument: The first-time comprehension win comes from C's glossary and scope card, which are portable. The buyer evidence (CS with 40 clients, GC with 13 entities, partner) all preferred A plus portfolio. Optimising the shell for the week-one user at the expense of the repeat daily user contradicts BUSINESS_PLAN §3.

challenge.target: Devil's advocate finding 9: unsure whether pre-deadline AGM is NOT_SATISFIED
challenge.argument: I checked this in round 1. With the sample facts, the engine returns s.96 as APPLIES_UNDETERMINED (limbs_not_decided includes the Registrar extension, and there are gap-limb needs). The live compliance pack summary was not_satisfied:0. So '! Not met yet' on s.96 is not what the engine returns. 'AGM due by 30 Sep' must be a separate derived-deadline item from checker/agm.py, which currently has no route.

debates.changed_my_mind: Yes, on three points. (1) The customer personas convinced me that single-company is a dealbreaker, not a later feature. I now require a portfolio home, and it is backend-feasible by fanning compliance-pack out per stored profile. (2) I had framed the s.137 backstop only as a UI omission. Re-checking _decide_aoc4 shows it is an engine gap for AOC-4, so it goes on the backend list, not the design list. (3) I had scored B's date travel as mostly unsupportable. The partner and GC feedback made clear that the narrow, engine-backed slice (dated thresholds with instrument and effective range) is the paid differentiator. I now want that slice kept and scoped, not dropped. I did not change my view that 880(E) is corroborated. The devil's advocate's contrary evidence is the fallback constant, not the served state.
debates.vote: Hybrid 'A-shell, engine-true': A's information architecture (attention home upgraded to a multi-entity portfolio, Duties master-detail, Ask + Sources, law-change Watch). Add B's dated-figure timeline and as-of control scoped per figure key. Add C's glossary as an on-demand drawer and its check trail as a collapsible panel built only from response fields. Cut Drafts, OFAC/IBBI and file-upload for the pilot.
non_negotiables: Every sample and every state in the final mockup is generated from real engine output (POST /v1/compliance-pack, /v1/ask, /v1/document-check, GET /v1/company/{cin}/events) on the sample profile, not hand-written. Specifically: 880(E) and 700(E) are shown as attested/CORROBORATED with evidence_state, not 'not yet checked'.

No row state the engine cannot return: no s.173 or s.149(1) 'Met' for this profile, and no s.96 'Not met' four days before the deadline. One label table keyed on obligations.ROW_STATES (5) and ask_contract.STATES (3), in a single StateChip, with APPLIES_UNDETERMINED (shows missing_facts) visibly distinct from CANNOT_DETERMINE (shows blocked_by rule).

No 'Answered' sample that /v1/ask cannot return. Either the backend exposes checker/agm.py's deadline (six-month and fifteen-month limbs, extension undecided) as a figure/row on a route, or the AGM answer renders as partial with 'date of last AGM' named missing.

'In force from' appears only on figures[].effective_from with the instrument. Section text always carries the law_version statement ('current consolidation, not point-in-time'). No stages and no 'checked each section is in force' on general turns.

The as-of date is allowed only per figure key within its coverage floor (s.2(85): 15-Sep-2022 onward), refuses below it, never applies to Watch or drafts, and is gated on a written PLAN_13 §9 amendment including the rule that no figure's effective_from may be later than as_of.

Pilot screens ship only against existing routes. Drafts, OFAC/IBBI, counterparty and file upload are removed or shown as 'not yet available'. Watch shows only /v1/company/{cin}/events with output_class badge, 'at' and 'known_at', and the _V0_SCOPE sentence verbatim.

Document check renders the engine's three buckets (superseded / cannot_verify / verified) with governed_then to governs_now, coverage.sentence and the unchecked list. The user supplies document_date. No 'What it is ✓ Verified', signature or OCR claims.
All 15 duties are shown with summary counts in the header, plus a visible provenance footer (law_version, scope sentence, what_it_is_not).
A ServiceError card that is visually unlike any abstention.

Backend work items are recorded as preconditions, not UI tasks: s.137(2) backstop in _decide_aoc4; Rule 6 review so private companies resolve s.177 to does-not-apply; document_check narrowed to relied-on obligations (or reporting direction of change); an AGM-deadline route; a portfolio/profile store if multi-entity ships. On the site side, fix the types.ts/AGENTS.md route list and add ask()/mcaStrip().

agree_with: Backend alignment engineer, critical finding 1, and Legal auditor, critical finding 2: G.S.R. 880(E) is not unverified. corpus/sources/gsr880e_registration.json lines 26 and 31 read classification VERIFIED_INSTRUMENT, status CORROBORATED. So the storyline is wrong in all three mockups. AGENTS.md:31-32 says 'Never invent a statutory figure/section/date'. An abstention that gives a false reason breaks the brand's honesty rule as badly as an invented figure. This is now the top brand issue, above the colour tokens.

Legal auditor critical 1, Backend critical 2, and all three customer personas: s.173(1) shown as '✓ Met' is a false pass. A false green tick destroys the 'witness, not a tool' positioning (AGENTS.md:6) faster than any visual flaw. The customers' line 'can't tell is the most reassuring thing on the screen; it's the green ticks that worry me' is the brand's value proposition, confirmed from outside.

Usability researcher critical 2, Accessibility minor, Interaction critic major, Frontend major: one status grammar. This agrees with my chip findings. Separate the obligation row states (5, from ROW_STATES), the Ask turn states (3) and process ticks. Give out_of_scope its own treatment rather than reusing the abstain grey.
Interaction critic minor and Product strategist: 'needs action' should be encoded without colour (bold ink border plus '!'), so gold-muted means citation only. This is the fix I proposed in Round 1.

Interaction critic critical 1: a ServiceError must never look like an abstention. PLAN_13 §7.11 gives it a dashed border, which collides with the dashed abstain rule in AGENTS.md:14-15. It must be solid.

Trust reviewer critical 1 and 2: the OFAC 'no match' shown with the met-style chip, and the IBBI 'similar name' match. Showing a SIGNAL with the heaviest VERIFIED visual is a brand-honesty violation. The site's class 'Signal, not asserted' (AGENTS.md:53 predictive_signal) has to be visible.
Legal auditor and Devil's advocate on scope overclaim: 'every duty the Act gives it' breaks AGENTS.md 'do not overclaim'. Use 'the 15 duties Placedon checks today' everywhere.
Accessibility critical 2: the focus ring disappears on ink chrome (A, C) and on B's cream sheet. A two-tone ring is also the brand-safe fix, because it avoids adding a coloured focus accent.

Product strategist and Devil's advocate on cutting Drafts and OFAC: bp/docs/BUSINESS_PLAN.md excludes drafting ('where professional trust ends'). Keeping it on screen presents the brand as a Harvey/Spellbook-type product, which it is not.

challenge.target: Usability researcher, Legal auditor, Backend engineer, and three of the four simulated customers: 'A as the base' without brand conditions
challenge.argument: I accept A's information architecture. But A as built is the design the Interaction critic called 'generic SaaS': numbered 01-05 feature cards, four identical KPI tiles, a 'New here?' brochure. AGENTS.md warns against these template patterns, and A breaks the one-accent rule (gold nav bar plus a gold-muted chip on the same screen, Main.dc.html:357 and 336). The senior partner persona called that block 'marketing I will scroll past'. 'A as base' must mean A's IA re-skinned in the house system: ink shell, one gold element, citations in mono, no feature tour. Otherwise we ship a commodity that a buyer comparing ROC-calendar tools cannot tell apart (Devil's advocate, finding on A).

challenge.target: Accessibility specialist and Frontend lead: 'C as the shell'
challenge.argument: C has zero Brass Gold (#C9A24B count = 0 in Guided.dc.html). Its register ('the way you'd ask a colleague', 'Plain words are fine') is the least judgment-like of the three. The CS and GC personas both called it patronising. The reflow advantage is real, but it comes from C's single column, not from its wizard. A's screens can collapse to one column below 820px as PLAN_13 specifies. Reflow is a layout requirement to impose on the winner, not a reason to adopt C's voice and ceremony.

challenge.target: Interaction critic: 'Replace A's Overview with C's task-first What do you need to do today? home'
challenge.argument: Every simulated professional (CS, GC, partner) wanted urgency or portfolio first, not a task menu. The home headline should be a claim ('Obligations for <company> as of 26-Sep-2026: 1 needs action, N abstained'), not a question to the user. That is the house register, per AGENTS.md: 'claim, then evidence'.

challenge.target: Usability researcher and Trust reviewer: keeping first-person humility copy ('We won't guess this one', 'We can't tell yet')
challenge.argument: AGENTS.md:24-29 says humility appears once, in the abstention itself. Repeating 'we' apologies on every row weakens the abstain signal and reads as hedging. Rows should read as claim plus basis: 'Abstained. Requires: days in India per director (s.149(3)).'

challenge.target: Devil's advocate: 'B inverts the brand on the main canvas; two themes on one screen'
challenge.argument: It is the opposite. The live site uses the dark ink shell with cream paper for documents (PLAN_13 §27, the .ddoc-paper pattern). B is the only mockup at parity with the site. Ink chrome around a cream answer sheet is one theme, not two. The contrast concern about rgba(.66) captions is valid, and the fix is a minimum opacity, not a switch to a light shell.

challenge.target: Frontend lead and Interaction critic on labels: making 'Partly answered' canonical, or treating the site's 'Satisfied / Cannot determine' as the default
challenge.argument: I re-checked PLAN_13_ASSISTANT_UX.md: line 970 and §27 at line 1661 (dated 2026-09-17, later than row 1 at line 52) replace 'Partly answered' with 'Abstained in part', and 'Abstained' when confirmed[] is empty. The reason given there: 'Partly answered over a turn that answered nothing is an overclaim', and §7.12 says that turn will dominate. The canonical Ask words are therefore Answered / Abstained in part / Abstained / Not held. All three mockups and the Usability researcher's recommendation still use the superseded word.

debates.changed_my_mind: Yes, on three points. (1) In Round 1 I praised B's dashed G.S.R. 880(E) marker as the correct abstention mark. It is not: the instrument is VERIFIED_INSTRUMENT / CORROBORATED on disk (gsr880e_registration.json:26,31), so the dashed marker is a false abstention and brand-dishonest. The flagship brand device, as drawn, misstates the facts. (2) I scored B 7.5 and wanted it as the frame. Backend, Legal, the customers and PLAN_13 §9 ('as_of is today, and only today, in v1') show that B's date travel promises point-in-time law the engine cannot give. B also has no free-text Ask, and its Watch and Draft ignore the date. A brand built on 'we never assert what we cannot prove' cannot let its signature interaction overclaim. I now keep B's visual identity (ink shell, cream answer paper, the single gold 'you are here' cursor, the per-provision timeline), not its interaction model. (3) I accept that the IA should come from A, because every professional persona needs urgency, the detail panel and portfolio scale, and those live in A. My Round 1 score for A was about layout; the brand fix is to re-skin it, not to replace it. What did not change: the chip palette violations (gold-muted used as a status, Cool Grey used decoratively) and the abstention lexicon remain critical, and I verified again that PLAN_13 §27 mandates 'Abstained in part'.
debates.vote: Hybrid 'A-structure in B's skin'. Use A's information architecture (attention/portfolio home, the Duties master-detail with What we found / Still needed / The rule, Ask plus Sources, Watch limited to law-change events). Render it in B's brand shell: ink chrome, answers on cream paper, exactly one Brass Gold element per view. B's instrument timeline becomes a per-provision currency strip in the Sources column, built only from engine-held instruments with real rupee figures, and its cursor is fixed at today until PLAN_13 §9 is amended (then limited to per-key coverage). C's 'How we checked' trail becomes a collapsible section built only from response fields, and C's glossary becomes an on-demand drawer. Drafts, OFAC and the feature tour are cut from the pilot build.
non_negotiables: Sample data regenerated from real engine output before any external showing. G.S.R. 880(E) and 700(E) are shown as held and corroborated, with rupee figures, the instrument and effective_from. No abstention may state a false reason. If a live abstention example is needed, use one that is actually unheld (S-177/S-203 rules).

No false passes. No '✓ Met' or 'Answered' that the engine would not return (s.173 while s.2(85) is undetermined; s.96 without the 15-month limb). Row states map 1:1 to obligations.py ROW_STATES, with one label table in src/lib shared by the site and the app.

Colour tokens enforced by lint. #9F743B is allowed only inside citation markup. #5B6472 plus dashed is allowed only for abstained/unknown (not the sample badge, not the 'What to do' box, not roadmap cards). 'Needs action' is ink-only (bold border plus '!'). ServiceError uses a solid rule and never shares the dashed abstain treatment.
Exactly one Brass Gold #C9A24B element per view, 10% or less of the screen. The gold nav bar and the gold cursor never appear together.

One brand lexicon across site, backend and app: Answered / Abstained in part / Abstained / Not held (PLAN_13 §27), plus the output classes Verified fact / Determined / Signal, not asserted. A SIGNAL (IBBI, any screening) never wears the verified/met visual.

IBM Plex Mono for every section, instrument, rupee figure and statutory date, applied by a tokenizer rather than hand-styling, including headlines and prose. Mono is not used for row numbers or labels.

Every figure prints 'section · instrument (or "as enacted") · in force from DD-Mon-YYYY' inside the figure block. Section text carries the engine's law_version line ('current consolidation, not a point-in-time version'), and no 'in force' claim is made about section text.

Voice in the judgment register: claim then basis, humility only in the abstention, no feature tour, no 'Was this useful?' inside the evidence card (replace it with 'This is blocking me' on abstained turns and rows), no 'every duty the Act gives'. Use the scope denominator ('the 15 duties Placedon checks today').

Brand assets: brand-kit/logo (white on ink), 3px radius token, no italics on legal content (the B slots become roman), 12px minimum type and 4.5:1 contrast on ink. A single date-format decision recorded (PLAN_13 open decision 3).
A two-tone focus ring that is visible on both ink and cream, and a 360px frame of the Ask result and Duties before sign-off.
A 'not legal advice; approver remains responsible' line beside any approve or export action, and a quiet 'Request a pilot' text link in the pre-launch sample shell (not a second accent).

debates.role: Legal accuracy & honesty auditor (Indian company law) - debate round
agree_with: Backend alignment engineer, critical #1 and #2: I re-checked the backend. The evidence state in checker/prescribed_thresholds.py comes from the registration records (the attestation gaps and is_attested() at lines ~140-190). It is not a constant. The engineer's live run returned CORROBORATED for both 700(E) and 880(E). So every mockup gives a false reason when it abstains. This confirms my own Round 1 critical #2, and it matters most, because an abstention that states a false reason breaks the honesty promise.

Backend engineer, critical #2 on s.96: I read checker/obligations.py _decide_agm (lines 298-360). With 2024 and 2025 AGMs on record and none yet in 2026, the missed-year check does not fire. Line 856 then turns any pass that has undecided limbs into UNDETERMINED. So '! Not met yet' four days before the deadline is not a state the engine produces. This also answers my own Round 1 open question and the Devil's advocate's open question. The deadline has to be a separate derived-deadline item, never a row state.

Backend engineer, major on C's in-force claims ('Checked each section is in force', 'Confirmed s.96(1) is in force'): the law_version flag point_in_time_verified is false, and ask_contract rejects citations that carry effective_from. This is the same finding as my C major.

Backend engineer and the Interaction critic on B's date travel: support it for figures and threshold-driven rows from 15-Sep-2022 onward only. Section text is today's consolidation only. PLAN_13 §9 must be amended before any build.

Trust/privacy reviewer, critical on the OFAC tick: ofac_sdn.py itself says an empty screen means 'not on the list as published on <date>, never not sanctioned', and matching is exact-name only. Using the Met/Checked chip for it is a legal misstatement. It also misses the UNSC and MHA/UAPA lists, which I raised.

Trust/privacy reviewer, critical on IBBI 'similar name': there is no fuzzy matcher, ibbi.py forbids re-labelling, and naming a counterparty next to the word 'insolvency' in a list title carries a defamation risk. I endorse matching on CIN or exact name only, with a human confirm step that is logged.

Trust/privacy reviewer and all three simulated customers: the draft notice certifies its own dispatch ('sent at least seven days ahead, as s.173(3) requires'). That is a false statement inside an operative document. Remove it.

Brand guardian, major on vocabulary: C labels the Ask quote row '✓ Met' next to a verbatim quote, and the met chip is reused for SIGNAL items. Classes must be separated. This is an honesty issue as well as a brand one.

Usability researcher, major: s.149(3) is mapped to 'Can't tell' when the engine returns APPLIES_UNDETERMINED. The distinction between a missing fact and a missing rule has legal meaning: one is the user's job, the other is ours. The Devil's advocate's three-way split of non-answers (we need from you / Placedon still verifying / signal) is the right product expression of it.

Product strategist and Devil's advocate: Drafts should be cut from the pilot. From my role: the notice as drafted is legally incomplete (no time, agenda, VC option, signatory or date of notice). Approve unlocks once the venue alone is filled, so the 'no blanks' gate is false comfort.

Simulated senior partner: A's s.96(1) quote cites the opening words while the answer depends on the first proviso. That is a real citation defect I missed in Round 1. The quote must contain the operative words. C gets this right.

challenge.target: Devil's advocate, critical #1 (cites prescribed_thresholds.py:108 SOURCE_880='UNRESOLVED' as proof the moat abstains)
challenge.argument: That line is misread. SOURCE_880 is the fallback India Code URL handle. The comment at line 103 says 'The India Code handle for 880(E) is UNRESOLVED'. It is not the evidence state. The state is derived from the registration record (lines 140-190, 'Not a hand-edited constant'), and the backend engineer's live run returned CORROBORATED with ₹10 cr/₹100 cr from 01-Dec-2025. The recommendation to hold the UI until a threshold is verified rests on a false premise. The instrument is already verified. What is actually stopping s.2(85) from resolving is the proviso facts (holding/subsidiary/s.8/special Act) and whatever exclusion is unverified, not 880(E).

challenge.target: Brand guardian, praising B's dashed 880(E) marker as 'correctly means abstention'
challenge.argument: It is correct styling on a false fact. 880(E) is CORROBORATED, so drawing it dashed and 'not yet checked' misstates what we hold. B also draws 700(E) solid while its text says it is awaiting review. The device is good. B's current content in it is dishonest both ways.

challenge.target: Accessibility specialist and Frontend feasibility lead, preferring C as the shell
challenge.argument: Reflow is a real requirement, but C's shell is the one that carries the most unsupported legal claims. Its mandatory 'We check' step renders checkmarks for verifications the engine does not perform ('in force as of today', 'no notification has changed this rule'). Its duties result says 'every duty we checked' over 7 of 15 rows. Its read-only 'Tell us' collects no facts, yet step 3 asserts CSR 'Doesn't apply' and s.173 'Met'. Any shell can be made to reflow. A shell whose central step is a narrated proof cannot be kept unless the trace is built only from response fields. If C's structure is used at all, the trace must be an optional expander fed by law_version, evidence_pack and not_confirmed, never a gated step.

challenge.target: Frontend feasibility lead and Backend engineer: B's as-of control as a 'cheap global searchParam'
challenge.argument: It is cheap technically but not legally. A global date implies every view is point-in-time. The engine can date thresholds only, and only from 15-Sep-2022. Section text, Watch and Drafts cannot be dated. The control must be scoped per view, with a visible 'section text is today's consolidation (ingested 18-Aug-2026)' line. It must be disabled, with a reason, below each key's coverage floor. Otherwise we rebuild B's worst bug inside A.

challenge.target: Interaction critic: keep the timeline but freeze the cursor at today
challenge.argument: Over-corrected. The engine can honestly answer the s.2(85) threshold on 14-Aug-2025 (it returns 700(E) ₹4 cr). That is the single most defensible point-in-time demo the product has, and the partner and GC personas both named it as the thing they would pay for. Limit the date control by coverage. Do not remove it.

challenge.target: Simulated customers and several members treating s.177 'Can't tell' for a Pvt Ltd as only a UI issue
challenge.argument: It is an engine decision (the _audit_committee path abstains pending Rule 6 review), so a UI relabel alone would be a UI inference, and inference is forbidden. The fix belongs in the backend. Review Rule 6 so the private-company case returns DOES_NOT_APPLY. Until then, the row may say 'Rule 6 not yet reviewed; the Act's own limb (listed public company) does not reach a private company' as reasoning text. It must not show a 'Doesn't apply' chip the engine did not return.

challenge.target: Usability researcher's recommendation to show typed Ask questions in a 'sample: engine not connected' answer card
challenge.argument: Any sample card, labelled or not, must not show '■ Answered' for 'When is our AGM due?'. The engine returns partial for that free text. The demo should show the honest partial result, which is the brand's actual behaviour.

debates.changed_my_mind: Yes, on three points. (1) In Round 1 I said the pre-deadline s.96 'Not met' might be how the engine behaves. Reading _decide_agm and the undecided-limbs rule at line 856 shows it returns UNDETERMINED, so the backend engineer is right, and the AGM date belongs in a separate deadline item. (2) The simulated partner showed that A's s.96(1) quote does not contain the operative proviso. I had credited A's quotes as matching the corpus word-for-word, and they do, but it is the wrong passage for the proposition. (3) The trust reviewer convinced me the OFAC and IBBI items are worse than an overclaim: they are live legal and reputational hazards (a false clearance, and a named company next to 'insolvency'). They should be cut from the pilot rather than relabelled. Nothing changed my view that B cannot lead, or that A has the fewest unsupported claims.
debates.vote: Hybrid: A as the shell (duties master-detail, Ask + Sources, law-change-only Watch). Add B's as-of date control, limited by coverage, and a per-provision instrument strip with real figures. Add C's glossary as an on-demand drawer and C's check trace as an optional expander built only from response fields. Cut Drafts, OFAC/IBBI and file upload from the pilot. Regenerate all sample data from live engine output.
non_negotiables: No row state, Ask state or chip may appear unless the engine can return it for the sample facts. The sample data must come from live POST /v1/compliance-pack, /v1/ask and /v1/document-check output.
