This means no s.173(1) 'Met' while s.2(85) is undetermined, no s.149(1) 'Met' with an undecided limb, no s.96 'Not met' pre-deadline, and no '■ Answered' for free-text 'When is our AGM due?'.

Every statement about instrument verification must match what the engine holds, shown the same way on every screen. 880(E) and 700(E) are CORROBORATED ('attested; Gazette copy matched automatically'). Live abstention examples must use instruments that really are unreviewed (S-177/S-188/S-203 rules). An abstention must state its true reason.

No '⟳ Law has changed' or '! Found an issue' verdict may rest on an unverified instrument. A raised threshold (700(E)→880(E)) must not be flagged as endangering small-company status unless the company's figures could flip the outcome.

Section text carries no in-force or point-in-time claim. Only figures[].effective_from may say 'In force from'. Every answer shows the currency line ('Text as ingested 18-Aug-2026; current consolidation, not a point-in-time version'). Delete C's 'Checked each section is in force' and 'No notification has changed this rule' ticks.

Any date control is limited by coverage: figures and threshold-driven rows only, from 15-Sep-2022 for s.2(85). It is disabled with a stated reason elsewhere, and no view may print 'as of X' over content that ignores X. PLAN_13 §9 must be amended in writing first.
Verbatim quotes must contain the operative words the answer relies on (the s.96(1) first proviso, not the opening words).

The AGM deadline item must name the missing previous-AGM date (15-month limb), 'unless extended by the RoC (s.96(1) proviso, GNL-1, not decided)', and the s.101 21-clear-day notice consequence. s.137(1)/s.92(4) rows must show the s.137(2)/s.92(4) outer dates (30 Oct / 29 Nov 2026) counted from the date the AGM should have been held. The backend's s.137(2) gap flagged by the partner persona must be confirmed and fixed.
Coverage honesty everywhere: 'the 15 duties Placedon checks today', all 15 rows reachable with summary counts, a 'what Placedon does not check' link, and never 'every duty the Act gives'.

Separate the three non-answer types visibly: a fact missing from the user (APPLIES_UNDETERMINED, with an inline input), a rule missing on our side (CANNOT_DETERMINE, with blocked_by named), and a SIGNAL (never the met or abstain chip). out_of_scope gets its own style.

Cut from the pilot: sanctions/OFAC and IBBI name-match items, file upload/OCR/signature forensics, and Drafts. If Drafts ever returns: no self-certifying compliance text in the notice body, all SS-1 elements present before Approve, a named approver and timestamp, and a persistent 'not legal advice; the approver remains responsible' line.
'Verified' is reserved for VERIFIED_FACT backed by a held source. A document's self-description is 'Identified as', and user-supplied facts carry a 'from your input' provenance tag.

agree_with: Backend alignment engineer, critical findings 1-3: the sample data has to be regenerated from real engine output. They ran compliance-pack live on the sample profile and got not_satisfied 0, undetermined 10, cannot_determine 3, satisfied 1, not_applicable 1. That means the 'AGM due in 4 days / 1 needs action' home story is not something the engine produces today. I re-checked corpus/sources/gsr880e_registration.json: classification VERIFIED_INSTRUMENT, status CORROBORATED, match 'identical'. This is the most decision-relevant finding in the dossier. Every mockup is demoing a product that does not exist.

Legal accuracy auditor, s.173 finding: 'Met' is impossible while s.2(85) is can't-tell, because obligations.py _decide_board refuses on the s.173(5) regime. Three meetings in September is also not four. All four simulated customers raised this independently, and every one of them named a false green tick as their dealbreaker. That makes it the top trust risk.

Legal auditor and all four customer personas on s.96(1): the 15-month limb, the s.101 21-day notice and the GNL-1 extension are missing. Customers want the notice deadline surfaced, not the meeting deadline. For a CS or GC this is the actual weekly value.
Usability researcher, critical finding on B: the date slot prints 'as of 14 Aug 2025' over Watch and Draft content from 2026. A date control has to apply to every view or visibly exclude it.

Usability researcher and backend engineer on vocabulary: freeze one label table keyed to obligations.ROW_STATES plus the three ask_contract STATES, used on the site and in the app. Keep APPLIES_UNDETERMINED visibly distinct from CANNOT_DETERMINE (s.149(3) is currently mis-mapped). The devil's advocate adds a split of non-answers into 'we need from you', 'Placedon is still verifying' and 'signal'. That split directly reduces churn, and I adopt it.

Trust/privacy reviewer on OFAC/IBBI: the SDN contract says 'not on the list as published on <date>', matching is exact-name only, there is no fuzzy matcher, and the feeds are LICENCE_UNVERIFIED so the engine refuses commercial serving. Watch must not show counterparty sanctions or insolvency items as live. This reinforces my Round 1 recommendation to cut them.

Trust/privacy reviewer on the Documents upload: it needs a data-handling disclosure (residency, retention, delete, processor). The GC and partner personas both named this as the first question from IT or the GC.

Accessibility specialist and design critic: require a 360px frame before the shell is chosen. UX_INTERACTION_SPEC §6.1 says the first demos happen on a phone, and PLAN_13 says the pane is the deliverable.
Design critic: design the ServiceError/transport-failure state now so it can never look like an abstention.
Frontend feasibility lead: step 0 for any direction is to fix types.ts/AGENTS.md so that /v1/ask and mca-strip exist in the client, and to build one StateChip with one label source.
Brand guardian: take gold-muted #9F743B off the 'needs action' chip and take Cool Grey off non-abstention elements. I agree because it protects the citation signature, which is part of the moat.

challenge.target: Devil's advocate, critical finding 1 (currency strip never answers; prescribed_thresholds.py:108 SOURCE_880='UNRESOLVED')
challenge.argument: This misreads the file. Line 108 is only the fallback source URL string. The state is computed dynamically, and it returns CORROBORATED at lines 201 and 298 when the registration artifacts check out. The registration JSON shows VERIFIED_INSTRUMENT / CORROBORATED, and the backend engineer's live run returned 880(E) at Rs 10 cr and 700(E) at Rs 4 cr for as_of 2025-08-14. So the moat can be demonstrated today, and the recommendation to 'hold the UI decision until a threshold is verified' is unnecessary. The problem is stale mockup copy, not a missing capability.

challenge.target: Legal accuracy auditor and simulated partner: claim that the backend does not implement the s.137(2) 'should have been held' backstop
challenge.argument: It does implement it. obligations.py _decide_aoc4 (lines ~429-469) handles the 'told there was none; the clock runs from when it should have been held' path, and the self-test at line 1208 checks for it. The gap is in the UI, which says 'isn't set yet'. The backend has no such gap. The final agreement should not spend backend effort on this.

challenge.target: Accessibility specialist and frontend lead: C as the shell
challenge.argument: C's reflow advantage is real, but the Round 1 evidence goes against using it as the shell. All four simulated customers rejected the forced 3-step flow for repeat use; the CS persona said '120 clicks I don't have'. PLAN_17's exit criterion is use twice a week. C's step 2 narrates stages that the engine does not return (contract.md D11). The single-column property can be had by requiring A's surfaces to collapse at 820px as PLAN_13 specifies. We do not need to adopt a wizard to get it.

challenge.target: Brand guardian: B as the frame
challenge.argument: The brand signature (dark shell, one gold cursor, timeline) can sit inside the Sources panel of each provision without making the editable sentence the navigation. B's sentence cannot take free text, has no client picker, and does not survive 360px. The customers ranked B last for daily use. Brand parity should be decided on the site shell, not by choosing B's interaction model.

challenge.target: My own Round 1 recommendation of an 'unrestricted date picker'
challenge.argument: The backend engineer and legal auditor are right. PLAN_13 §9 says as_of is today-only in v1, and section text is an 18-Aug-2026 consolidation with point_in_time_verified=false. An unrestricted picker would assert past statutory text we do not hold. The control has to be bounded by per-key coverage (s.2(85) from 15-Sep-2022), and every past view has to be labelled 'figures and duties as of X; section text is today's consolidation'. That also needs a written PLAN_13 amendment.

challenge.target: Usability researcher: keep A's 'New here' feature strip / C's permanent glossary
challenge.argument: For the named buyer (a CS with 40-80 clients) and the simulated GC and partner, both read as a brochure or as patronising. Keep the glossary as an on-demand drawer, and cut the feature grid to a one-line index. They are onboarding for the secondary founder segment and should not be the default.

debates.changed_my_mind: Yes, on two points. First, the date control. In Round 1 I asked for an unrestricted 'as of [any date]' picker on every view, and I now withdraw that. The engine can only date figures and row decisions within per-key coverage, and past section text is not held. I now want a bounded as-of control that states its coverage and labels section text as the current consolidation. Second, how much weight I gave the stale 880(E) copy. I had called verification 'a caveat I could not confirm'. The backend engineer's live run and the registration file settle it: the flagship ANSWERED s.2(85) state (Rs 10 cr, G.S.R. 880(E), from 01 Dec 2025) can be shown today. That makes regenerating the sample from the engine the gating task, ahead of any layout choice. The customer panel also strengthened my view that multi-entity support is the buyer-defining gap: the CS, GC and partner personas all independently called single-company a dealbreaker. What did not change is my view that Drafts and OFAC/IBBI should be cut from the pilot.
debates.vote: Hybrid "A-shell docket": A's structure (attention home, Duties master-detail, Ask + Sources, law-change Watch) with a portfolio/client-switcher layer on top. B's timeline goes per provision in the Sources panel, with a bounded as-of control. C's check trace becomes a collapsible 'How we got this' built only from response fields. C's glossary becomes an on-demand drawer. Drafts and counterparty Watch are cut from the pilot.
non_negotiables: Every sample state must be regenerated from live engine output: /v1/compliance-pack, /v1/ask, /v1/document-check and /v1/company/{cin}/events on the sample profile. No hand-written row state, answer state or verification claim. Instrument status copy must come from prescribed_thresholds/currency, not from memory.

No green 'Met' or '■ Answered' that the engine would not return. s.173 cannot be Met while s.2(85) is undetermined. s.96 cannot be Answered without the previous AGM date. A dependency rule should be enforced in the UI: no pass while any row it depends on is can't-tell.

The hero demo shows the moat actually answering: 'Are we a small company?' returns the Rs 10 cr figure with G.S.R. 880(E), in force from 01 Dec 2025, and evidence_state shown beside the number. There must also be one honest abstention on a provision that is really unheld (s.177 Rule 6, s.188 or s.203 rules), and its stated reason must be the engine's reason.

One status vocabulary, keyed to obligations.ROW_STATES and ask_contract STATES, shared by the site and the app. Missing-user-fact, Placedon-still-verifying and signal-not-fact must look different, and missing-fact rows get an inline input.

The as-of date control is bounded to engine coverage per key, applies to every visible view or visibly excludes it, and labels section text as the current consolidation. A written PLAN_13 §9 amendment is required before any past date ships.

Multi-entity from day one of the pilot: a client/entity switcher plus a portfolio home sorted by nearest hard deadline. The deadlines must include back-computed notice dates (s.101, s.173(3)) and the s.137(2)/s.92(4) backstop dates the engine already computes. The buyer (CS in BUSINESS_PLAN vs in-house in PLAN_17) must be settled by the founder before build, and the home screen is designed for that buyer.

Drafts and OFAC/IBBI counterparty Watch are removed from the pilot UI, or shown only as clearly labelled 'not available'. Watch v1 shows only law-change events, with output_class, both dates, and the _V0_SCOPE sentence verbatim.
Every duty view shows its scope: all 15 rows, the summary counts, and a 'what Placedon does not check' link. The copy never says 'every duty the Act gives'.

'This is blocking me' demand-signal control on every partial answer and every can't-tell row, logged with the provision ID. 'Copy with sources' and an export carry the section, the instrument, the in-force date, the as-of date and the law_version statement.
A 360px frame of the Ask partial state and the duties table, plus a designed ServiceError state that cannot be mistaken for an abstention, before the shell is signed off.

A data-handling disclosure (residency, retention, delete, processors) wherever client documents or facts are entered, and approvals that name the person and time. This is pending counsel on DPDP (PLAN_17 step 0.6).

agree_with: Backend alignment engineer, critical findings 1-3: the sample data contradicts the engine. 880(E) and 700(E) are CORROBORATED (I re-checked: corpus/sources/gsr880e_registration.json lines 26 and 31 say VERIFIED_INSTRUMENT and CORROBORATED). s.149(1) and s.173(1) can never render 'Met'. The flagship 'Answered: By 30 Sep 2026' comes back from /v1/ask as partial. This outranks every layout finding, because each mockup's visual hierarchy was designed around made-up states. The 'AGM due in 4 days' hero tile, the gold 'Not met' chip on s.96 and B's dashed 880(E) node are all visual emphasis attached to states the engine will not return.

Usability researcher, critical finding 2, and Accessibility, minor finding on glyphs: the chip vocabulary is overloaded. This is my own finding 3, and three separate reviewers reached it independently. The fix is to split it into three components (obligation row state, Ask turn state as a heading word, process tick as plain mono), not to write one legend.

Brand guardian, criticals 1-2: gold-muted #9F743B on the notmet chip and Cool Grey dashed borders on non-abstention elements (the sample badge, the 'What to do' box, the FEMA roadmap card). I raised the gold-muted point as minor. The brand guardian is right to treat it as critical, because it destroys the one colour that means 'citation'.

Accessibility specialist, critical findings 1-2: there is no 360px reflow, and the focus ring is 1.0:1 on the dark sidebar in A and C and on the cream sheet in B. Once reflow is taken seriously, B's 50px sentence and its absolutely positioned timeline are eliminated as a shell.

Legal auditor, s.137(2)/s.92(4) backstop deadlines and the s.96 fifteen-month limb: 'isn't set yet' hides the single most useful date. These are content-hierarchy failures as much as legal ones, because the row should lead with 'By 30 Oct 2026 at the latest'.
Trust reviewer, critical 1: the OFAC 'no match' uses the solid-ink met chip. Visually this is the worst misuse of the chip system, since the heaviest mark on the page carries the weakest claim.

Product strategist and Devil's advocate: the unit is wrong, because every mockup shows one company while the named buyer handles 40-80. All four simulated customers raised it unprompted (the CS: 'Where is the list of forty clients?'). I missed this in round 1, and it changes the home screen design.
Frontend feasibility lead, the StateChip finding: one label table in src/lib keyed on RowState and AskState. That is the engineering form of my vocabulary fix.

challenge.target: Devil's advocate, critical 1 ('backend checker/prescribed_thresholds.py:108 SOURCE_880 = UNRESOLVED', so the currency strip abstains everywhere)
challenge.argument: This misreads the file. I re-checked lines 101-107: SOURCE_880 is the India Code handle marker that shows only on an UNSERVABLE 880(E) row, and the comment says that once the registration record is attested, the served figure carries the real source. The registration JSON says CORROBORATED, and the backend engineer's live run returned ₹10 cr under 880(E). The moat is therefore demoable today. The problem is that the mockups were written from stale copy, so the right response is to regenerate the sample data, not to 'hold the UI decision'.

challenge.target: Brand guardian, preferred direction ('B as the frame' with a dark ink shell) and score B 7.5
challenge.argument: Brand coherence cannot outweigh the other evidence: B fails reflow (Accessibility), has no free-text Ask (every customer persona objected), recomputes past dates the engine cannot (PLAN_13 §9: as_of today only in v1), and hard-codes an s.2(85) timeline under unrelated verbs. The dark shell is also contested. PLAN_13 §27 notes that status hues fail contrast on ink, and the Word pane is light. Keep B's one-gold-cursor discipline and its timeline as brand devices inside a light working shell. A dark shell for the working app is not a requirement.

challenge.target: Accessibility specialist and Frontend feasibility lead, preferred direction C as the shell (because it reflows best and maps to URL-addressable steps)
challenge.argument: C's structural advantage is really its single column, not its wizard. Its step gating adds two clicks to a millisecond-fast deterministic result (UX_INTERACTION_SPEC §6.2 rejects staging), and all four customer personas except the week-one associate rejected it for repeat use. A's master-detail collapses to a single column at <820px just as well, with list, then detail route, then back (the feasibility lead's own /app/duties/[obligationId] proposal). Take C's reflow-friendly one-column result stack and its trail, and drop the gated steps.

challenge.target: Usability researcher, 'A's Overview … the only design that gets a first-time user to I know what's urgent in 60s' (the tiles as strengths_worth_keeping)
challenge.argument: The tiles are computed from states the engine does not produce: 'AGM due in 4 days' as notmet, and '3 can't tell' with the wrong mapping. The four identical tiles plus the numbered '01-05 Try it' feature grid are also the generic KPI and feature-card pattern. Keep an attention surface, but make it a ranked list of dated deadlines (derived from agm.py and the s.137(2)/s.92(4) backstops) with 'what we need from you' counts. Drop the tile grid and the feature tour.

challenge.target: Product strategist, 'Cut the permanent glossary' / Devil's advocate 'glossary is patronising'
challenge.argument: I agree it should not be a permanent 330px column. Cutting it entirely is overcorrecting. The week-one associate persona named it the most trust-building element, and in-house and founder users are a real secondary segment. Make it an on-demand drawer, with dotted-underline terms that open inline definitions and add AGM, CSR, OFAC and IBBI. It costs nothing for the CS and still helps the novice.

challenge.target: Legal auditor and several reviewers, s.96 'Not met yet' four days before the deadline
challenge.argument: This is a design problem as well as a legal one. There is no visual state for 'live, not yet breached, deadline approaching'. The engine returns APPLIES_UNDETERMINED here, so the '!' chip is wrong. A deadline should be rendered as a date-first row element ('Due 30 Sep 2026 · 4 days'), separate from the five row-state chips, so urgency does not require falsely claiming a breach.

debates.changed_my_mind: Yes, on two points. First, on the unit of design. In round 1 I judged each mockup's single-company screens on their own terms. The unanimous customer feedback and the strategist's evidence (BUSINESS_PLAN.md §3, 40-80 clients) convince me the home screen must be a portfolio or docket (clients × deadlines, with abstentions grouped by cause), and the single-company view becomes the drill-down. Second, on severity. I ranked the gold-muted chip minor, and after the brand guardian's argument I now treat it as critical. Also, the backend engineer's live runs showing 880(E) and 700(E) CORROBORATED mean B's dashed-node 'honesty' device is currently depicting a false abstention. The timeline must be driven by evidence_state, not by hand-drawn styling. My view that B's past-date recomputation should be dropped did not change. PLAN_13 §9 still says as_of is today only in v1. The backend engineer showed thresholds do honour as_of, so a figure-only date control can be offered as a Phase C amendment, but it cannot be a v1 shell.
debates.vote: Named hybrid 'A-shell docket': A's working screens (the duties master-detail with What we found / Still needed / The rule, and Watch with a causal chain drawn only from /affected) inside a light shell that collapses to one column. The home is a multi-client docket with a ranked deadline list, not KPI tiles. C's 'what we checked' is an expandable trail inside each result, built only from response fields, with the glossary as an on-demand drawer. B's instrument timeline appears per provision in the Sources column, driven by evidence_state, with ₹ figures on nodes and a table fallback, and the cursor fixed at today in v1. Drafts are cut from the pilot.
non_negotiables: Three separate state components, never sharing one chip style. (1) Obligation row chips: exactly the five ROW_STATES, one label table used everywhere, with APPLIES_UNDETERMINED and CANNOT_DETERMINE worded to name their different questions. (2) Ask turn state as the heading word (answered / partial / out_of_scope), with out_of_scope styled differently from abstain. (3) Process ticks as plain mono text. Deadlines are a date-first element, not a state chip.

A ServiceError / 'No result' card designed now, with a solid rule, no glyph and 'Send again'. It must share no dashed treatment with abstention, so PLAN_13 §7.11's 'dashed Ink-80 border' must be amended.

Every sample state regenerated from real engine output (compliance-pack, ask, document-check, events). No 'Met' or 'Answered' that the route cannot return, and no abstention for a false reason. 880(E)/700(E) are shown as CORROBORATED with the ₹ figure, instrument and effective_from.
Colour discipline: #9F743B only on citations; Cool Grey plus dashed only on abstain, out-of-scope and blank slots; one Brass Gold element per view. 'Needs action' is ink-only, using weight and glyph.

A 360px frame of the portfolio home, a partial Ask answer (with verbatim text and TextBasisLine) and the duties drill-down before sign-off. No fixed-px multi-column grids below 820px, and no overflow:hidden root.

A focus ring that is visible (≥3:1) on every surface, including dark chrome and the cream sheet, plus focus moved to the new heading and a live region announcing the state word on every result change.

A single evidence stack reused for every result: stamp, state heading, NOT CONFIRMED, CONFIRMED, figure (value · instrument · in force from), verbatim with text-basis line, sources. Headlines never repeat the figure.
Coverage denominator on every duties view ('N of the 15 duties Placedon checks'), with all 15 reachable and a link to what is not covered. Never 'every duty the Act gives'.
Any date control shown must either apply to every visible view or visibly say that the view ignores it. In v1 it stays fixed at today unless PLAN_13 §9 is amended in writing.

Provenance must be exposed in text or ARIA, not only through underline style. Watch items carry output_class (VERIFIED_FACT / DETERMINISTIC_CONSEQUENCE / SIGNAL), and a screening result never uses the met chip.

debates.role: Frontend engineering feasibility lead (Next.js 16 / React 19 / Tailwind v4, placedon-claude-legal-3300)
agree_with: Backend alignment engineer, critical findings 1-3: the sample data contradicts the engine. 880(E) is held and s.173(1)/s.149(1) 'Met' is impossible, and /v1/ask returns partial for the AGM question. I re-checked corpus/sources/gsr880e_registration.json: status CORROBORATED, classification VERIFIED_INSTRUMENT. For my build plan this means the mockups' renderVals() arrays cannot be used as fixtures, which retracts my Round 1 'strength'. Fixtures must be recorded from the real handlers.

Backend alignment engineer, 'engine returns things the UI never shows' (law_version, evidence_state, coverage.sentence, summary counts, all 15 rows): the typed client should parse these fields and the components should render them. This is cheap for the frontend and has high value.

Legal auditor and all three customer personas on s.173(1) 'Met' and the missing s.96(1) 15-month limb: these confirm my rule that the client does no legal inference. Every state, date and 'Met' comes from a response field or is not shown.

Interaction critic, ServiceError finding: EngineResult<T> in src/lib/engine/errors.ts already separates transport failure from abstention. The design must give ServiceError a solid-rule card with no chip, never a dashed one.

Usability researcher, Accessibility specialist, Interaction critic and Backend engineer on one status grammar: this matches my StateChip finding. Build one label table keyed on ROW_STATES (5), Ask STATES (3) and event output_class (3). Out_of_scope must not reuse the can't-tell style.

Accessibility specialist on focus management, aria-current/aria-pressed, the A form submitting on Enter (Main.dc.html:151-155) and the 360px reflow requirement: all of these are acceptance criteria I can test in Playwright.

Trust reviewer and Legal auditor on OFAC/IBBI: the feeds are LICENCE_UNVERIFIED and have no route, so they must not ship. Their point that 'similar name' matching does not exist in the backend confirms they are not buildable.
Product strategist and Devil's advocate that Drafts should be cut: it has no route, drafting.py implements only the AGM notice, and the business plan excludes drafting.

Strategist and C-critics (Usability, Interaction, Strategist, CS customer) that C's gated 3-step wizard is wrong for repeat users and that 'We check' must be an expandable trace built from response fields. This changes my vote (see changed_my_mind).

challenge.target: Devil's advocate, critical finding 1 (prescribed_thresholds.py:108 SOURCE_880 = 'UNRESOLVED' means the moat never resolves)
challenge.argument: That constant is a fallback. _source_880() (prescribed_thresholds.py ~line 323) returns served_source_url(registration()) or SOURCE_880, and the registration file on disk reads CORROBORATED / VERIFIED_INSTRUMENT. The backend engineer's live run returned the Rs 10 cr figure. One real ambiguity remains: served_source_url is None in the registration JSON, so the source_url the UI would show may be the fallback string. That is a backend fix to make before the demo, not grounds to 'hold the UI decision'. The gate should be a recorded golden response from the real checkout, not a debate about memory.

challenge.target: Accessibility specialist and Trust reviewer: 'C reflows to 320-400px without redesign, so C is the base'
challenge.argument: None of the mockup markup survives the port. All three use inline style strings with hex values and fixed px grids, and all three are rebuilt in Tailwind against src/lib/tokens.ts. Whether a layout reflows depends on the rebuild, not on which mockup it came from. A's master-detail collapses cleanly at narrow widths when the detail is an App Router segment (/app/duties/[obligationId]): below 820px it becomes a full-page route with back navigation, which is also what PLAN_13's one-column pane wants. The reflow argument therefore does not favour C's IA over A's.

challenge.target: Product strategist, Devil's advocate and GC/CS customers: 'multi-client portfolio is a prerequisite before choosing A/B/C'
challenge.argument: I agree it is the buyer's unit of work. It cannot be populated today, though. /v1/compliance-pack is stateless per request (facts in, pack out), there is no client or company store, and the events route ignores the CIN (api._V0_SCOPE). A portfolio needs persistence (PLAN_17 M3 gateway and M5 vault). The frontend answer is to make the entity a route parameter from day one (/app/c/[cin]/...), so a portfolio index slots in above it without a retrofit. The buyer question (CS vs in-house) must be settled by the founder. It should not block the Phase 1 build of the single-entity screens that every portfolio row drills into.

challenge.target: Brand identity guardian: 'B's dark ink shell as the frame'
challenge.argument: PLAN_13 §27 notes that the status hues fail contrast on ink. The accessibility review measured the dark-chrome focus rings at 1.0:1 and B's rgba timeline rule at 2.91:1. The Word pane deliverable is light paper. Dark belongs on the chrome only (sidebar and header), with every stateful surface on cream. That is A's arrangement, and it can still carry B's single gold 'you are here' cursor.

challenge.target: Senior-partner, GC and associate customer personas, and Usability: 'any-date as-of control applied globally to every view'
challenge.argument: It cannot be built truthfully as a global control. as_of is accepted by compliance-pack, ask, document-check and events. Section text is always the current consolidation (point_in_time_verified=false), threshold lookups raise ThresholdUnavailable before 15-Sep-2022, and PLAN_13 §9 restricts v1 to today. The feasible version is a searchParam ?asof= that the UI sends only to routes that accept it. Each response then carries its own law_version statement and per-figure effective_from, which the UI renders verbatim. Views whose data ignores the date (for example law-change Watch) hide the control instead of silently ignoring it. This needs a written PLAN_13 amendment first.

challenge.target: Legal auditor and CS customer: 'show AOC-4 by 30 Oct / MGT-7 by 29 Nov backstop deadlines' and the s.101 notice back-computation
challenge.argument: The law is correct, but the frontend must not compute it. The partner persona notes that _decide_aoc4 does not implement s.137(2), and no route exposes agm.py. If the UI does the date arithmetic, we have created a second, unaudited legal engine in TypeScript. That is a backend ticket: expose derived deadlines as figures with their working. Until then, the UI shows the engine's missing_facts text.

challenge.target: Usability researcher and Accessibility specialist open question on dc runtime onChange/disabled semantics
challenge.argument: This does not affect the decision. The mockup runtime is not the build target, and no support.js sits beside the files in mockups/project. In the real build, the Approve lock uses aria-disabled plus a handler guard, per the accessibility recommendation. We should stop spending council time on it.

debates.changed_my_mind: Yes, on the shell. In Round 1 I voted C as the shell because its task/step structure maps neatly onto URL-addressable routes. The debate showed that this neatness is partly an artefact of C's invented step 2. The Backend engineer and Legal auditor showed that 'We check' narrates stages the engine does not run (contract.md D11: no stages on the general path). The Usability, Strategist and Interaction reviews and three of four customer personas showed that the gated wizard costs repeat users on every visit and hides urgency. Once step 2 becomes a disclosure built from response fields, C collapses to form → result, and A's Duties master-detail maps one-to-one onto _row_json. A's IA is therefore also the cheapest to wire honestly. I also withdraw 'renderVals arrays are good fixtures': they encode states the engine cannot return, so fixtures must be recorded from real handlers. My views on B are unchanged.
debates.vote: Hybrid 'A-routed': A's information architecture (attention home computed only from engine summary counts, Duties master-detail showing all 15 rows, Ask + Sources, law-change Watch), rebuilt as App Router segments keyed on /app/c/[cin]/... with ?asof=; C's glossary as an on-demand drawer and its 'How we got this' trace as a disclosure built only from response fields; B's timeline only as a per-provision strip built from figures[].effective_from with a table fallback, and B's date slot only as a scoped ?asof= control pending the PLAN_13 amendment. Drafts, OFAC/IBBI, upload and B's sentence shell are cut from Phase 1.
non_negotiables: Step 0 before any screen: correct the stale types.ts header (it says 'Exactly six routes… /v1/ask DO NOT EXIST'; api.py serves eight) and AGENTS.md. Add askSchema (a zod discriminated union on answered|partial|out_of_scope per contract.md) and mcaStrip, implemented in both HttpEngineProvider and MockEngineProvider, and extend tests/contracts.mjs.

Every fixture and every demo string is recorded from the real engine handlers on the real checkout under the project's Python, committed as golden JSON and contract-tested. No hand-written sample states. The 880(E) CORROBORATED state and its served_source_url (currently None in the registration JSON) are confirmed in that run.

No legal inference in the client: row state, deadlines, dates, 'Met', in-force dates and stale verdicts are rendered only from response fields (state, missing_facts, blocked_by, figures[].effective_from, evidence_state, law_version). Anything the engine does not return (s.137(2) backstops, AGM deadline, notice back-computation) becomes a backend ticket, never TypeScript arithmetic.

One StateChip/label table in src/lib, keyed on ROW_STATES (5), Ask STATES (3) and output_class (3), is the only place labels live. Snapshot tests assert that out_of_scope, CANNOT_DETERMINE, APPLIES_UNDETERMINED and SIGNAL never share a style, and that nothing uses gold-muted except citations.

EngineResult transport errors render a ServiceError card (solid rule, no chip, question kept, 'Send again') that cannot be confused with abstention. Playwright covers one test per state, including the error state.

All view state is URL-addressable: entity CIN in the path, selected duty/turn/document as a segment, as_of as a searchParam sent only to routes that accept it. Views that ignore the date hide the control. Past views print the engine's law_version statement verbatim.

Features without a route (Drafts, file upload/OCR, OFAC/IBBI/counterparty Watch, portfolio) are either absent or shown as explicit 'not available yet' states. No mock data for them becomes a design contract.

Accessibility acceptance before merge: a 360px frame per screen, form submit on Enter, focus moved to each result article's h2, a polite live region announcing the state word, a two-tone focus ring at 3:1 or better on every surface, aria-current/aria-pressed/aria-selected, and a table fallback under any timeline.
All 15 duties shown, with the engine's summary counts and coverage/scope sentence in the header. No '9 of 15' hiding.

Engine client split into a client-safe shared module (types, label helpers) and server-only providers, enforced by the server-only package or an eslint rule. Ask via server action with useActionState and no streaming. A real test runner (vitest or node:test plus Playwright) is wired into package.json before M10 work starts.

agree_with: Backend alignment engineer, critical finding 1, and Legal auditor, critical finding 2: the 880(E) 'not yet checked against the Gazette' story is false. I re-checked corpus/sources/gsr880e_registration.json. It has classification VERIFIED_INSTRUMENT and status CORROBORATED. A false reason for abstaining is a trust defect, not a copy nit. The honest wording is the legal auditor's: 'attested by a named reviewer; Gazette copy matched automatically; original download provenance not recorded' (provenance_note, line 18).

Legal auditor critical 1, Backend critical 2, and all four simulated customers: s.173(1) 'Met' is a pass the engine would refuse to give. Every simulated customer independently called a false green tick their dealbreaker. That makes it the highest-weight trust finding in the dossier, above any layout choice.

Product strategist major finding (sanctions and IBBI) and Legal auditor major (OFAC-only sanctions): these support my own findings 1 and 2. OFAC 'no match' shown with the met chip is a false clearance. ofac_sdn.py line 58 says '"not on the list as published on <date>", never "not sanctioned"'.

Frontend feasibility critical 1 and Backend major findings on Watch and Drafts: none of these has a route. ofac_sdn and egazette are LICENCE_UNVERIFIED (ofac_sdn.py line 122), so the engine will refuse to serve them commercially. A design built on data that cannot be served misleads pilot users.

Usability researcher and Interaction critic on status-vocabulary overload: the same black chip currently means Met, Verified, Checked, Done and Answered. From a trust angle this is the mechanism that lets a SIGNAL pass as a VERIFIED_FACT, which I raised as my own major finding 6.
Interaction critic, critical finding on ServiceError: a transport failure must never look like an abstention (AGENTS.md). Design this state now.

Devil's advocate major finding on 'can't tell': split it into 'we need from you' and 'Placedon is still verifying'. The split also tells the user who owns the gap, and owning a gap is a form of accountability.

Legal auditor minor, and Senior partner and GC personas: add 'not legal advice / approver remains responsible' near Approve and exports. Add maker-checker approval with named people and timestamps. drafting.py:55 approve(self, reviewer, at) already requires a named reviewer, so an anonymous 'Approved and recorded' contradicts the engine.

Simulated senior partner and GC: data residency, retention, training use and access have to be on screen before any upload. PLAN_17 already specifies Azure Central India storage, per-tenant envelope encryption, crypto-shredding and Document Intelligence OCR in-region (PLAN_17_BETA_BUILD.md lines 124-132). The UI simply never says any of this.
Senior partner persona: pin the corpus version (fetched_at and sha256) on every output so an answer can be reproduced later. This is an auditability requirement, and I missed it in round 1.

challenge.target: Devil's advocate, critical finding 1 (backend SOURCE_880 = 'UNRESOLVED', so the differentiator never resolves)
challenge.argument: This misreads the file. prescribed_thresholds.py:103-108 says only that the India Code HANDLE for 880(E) is unresolved and that the placeholder is 'what an UNSERVABLE 880(E) row shows'. The registration record is VERIFIED_INSTRUMENT / CORROBORATED, and the backend engineer's live run served ₹10 cr. The engine can therefore show a resolved currency strip today. The right conclusion is to rebuild the samples from engine output, not to postpone the UI decision. The one real caveat is the null download provenance, and it belongs in the source panel as disclosed text, not as an abstention.

challenge.target: Accessibility specialist, and Frontend feasibility, choosing C as base mainly because it reflows
challenge.argument: Reflow matters, but it can be fixed in any shell. What cannot be fixed in C is its step-2 'We check' ticks, which are invented process claims ('Checked each section is in force'; contract.md D11 says no stages on the general path). A fabricated audit trail does more damage to trust than a layout that needs to collapse. If any of C is kept, step 2 must be built only from response fields.

challenge.target: Brand guardian, preferring B as the frame
challenge.argument: B's global date travel shows point-in-time statutory text that the engine explicitly cannot produce (PLAN_13 §9; point_in_time_verified=false). It also prints an as-of date over Watch and Draft content that ignores that date. For a product whose whole promise is dated provenance, a date label that is sometimes decorative is the single worst trust failure available. Brand distinctiveness does not outweigh that.

challenge.target: Product strategist and Devil's advocate: 'cut Drafts' as the only answer to the drafting problem
challenge.argument: I agree Drafts should leave the pilot. But the approval pattern will return for forensics reports and exports. The council should still bind the approval rules now: a named reviewer, IST timestamp, version or hash, the wording 'Approved for use by <name>', and no self-certifying statutory text in generated output. Otherwise the same defect comes back on the next surface.

challenge.target: Usability researcher and Devil's advocate: C's glossary treated as low value for professionals
challenge.argument: The glossary is a minor issue. The bigger gap nobody else raised is that the counterparty list and uploaded minutes contain director and third-party personal data (DPDP). PLAN_17 step 0.6 leaves that position with counsel. Whatever shell wins needs a disclosure point at intake, and C's 'Tell us' step, or a per-upload line in A, is where that goes. That is the actual reason I rated C's structure well, not the glossary.

challenge.target: My own round-1 vote (C shell)
challenge.argument: See changed_my_mind. The legal auditor, backend engineer and three of four personas persuaded me that A's master-detail duties panel is the better evidence surface. The trust layer I asked for can sit in A just as easily.

debates.changed_my_mind: Yes, on the shell. In round 1 I preferred C, because its step structure gave natural places to disclose data handling. The backend engineer showed C's 'We check' step is largely invented engine stages. The legal auditor and three of the four simulated customers (partner, GC, CS) showed that A's 'What we found / Still needed / The rule' panel is the surface they would trust and actually use. Data-handling disclosure can go at the upload control and in a Settings screen in A just as well. I also upgraded two points after reading the dossier and re-checking the files. First, the 880(E) 'unchecked' copy is a false abstention reason, not merely out of date: the registration file shows CORROBORATED. Second, output reproducibility needs to be a trust requirement: the corpus version and hash pinned on every answer and export. On two points I did not move: the sanctions and IBBI presentation and the missing upload disclosure remain critical.
debates.vote: Hybrid: A shell (Duties master-detail, Ask + Sources, law-change-only Watch), B's as-of control only for engine-dated figures, with no global date travel over section text, and C's check trace as an expandable 'How we got this' built only from response fields. Drafts and OFAC/IBBI are cut from the pilot or shown as 'not available'. A trust layer is added: upload disclosure, Settings for retention, consent and delete, named approval, and pinned corpus version.
non_negotiables: No status the engine would not return. All sample data must be regenerated from live /v1/compliance-pack, /v1/ask and /v1/document-check output. Specifically: no s.173 'Met' while s.2(85) is undetermined, and no 'Answered' AGM date that ignores the fifteen-month limb and the RoC extension.

No false abstention reasons. 880(E) is shown as attested and corroborated, with the missing download provenance disclosed in the source panel. Any instrument shown as unverified must be unverified in currency.instrument_status, and the same status must appear identically on every screen.

Sanctions: never use the met or verified chip. If shown at all, the wording is 'Not found on <list> as published on <publish date>; exact-name match only; not a sanctions clearance', and nothing is shown while the feed is LICENCE_UNVERIFIED. The pilot either drops the feed or shows 'Source not yet cleared for display'.

IBBI and counterparties: match on CIN or exact published name only, never 'similar name'. Include ATTRIBUTION_TEXT. Never place a counterparty name beside 'insolvency' in a list title until a named person confirms the match, and log who confirmed it.

Before any upload control ships: an on-screen statement of storage location (India), encryption, who can see the document (matter scope), retention period, that scans go to Azure Document Intelligence (Central India), no training or evaluation use by default, and a per-document 'Delete permanently' action. A Settings screen for retention, evaluation consent (off by default) and delete-all. The copy is subject to counsel's DPDP review (PLAN_17 step 0.6).

Approval always shows the named approver, an IST timestamp and a version or hash. The wording is 'Approved for use by <name>', never a bare 'Approved'. Maker-checker is available. Generated documents never self-certify future facts such as dispatch dates.

Every '✓' row carries a provenance tag (from your input / from MCA record / worked out from law / verified source). The backend output classes (VERIFIED_FACT / DETERMINISTIC_CONSEQUENCE / SIGNAL) are visible, and a SIGNAL never uses the verified style.

Every answer and export carries the as-of date, law_version statement, corpus fetched_at and hash, scope sentence ('15 duties Placedon checks; not a full compliance review'), 'not legal advice' line and the sample or live flag, so a copied or pasted result cannot circulate without its caveats.
A ServiceError state that looks nothing like an abstention.
A date control never labels content the date did not change. Past dates apply only to engine-dated figures, and section text is labelled 'current consolidation, not point-in-time'.

agree_with: Backend alignment engineer, critical #1 and #2: the engine holds G.S.R. 880(E) and 700(E) as CORROBORATED, and s.149(1)/s.173(1) can never be 'Met' for this company (a live compliance-pack run returned satisfied:1, undetermined:10, cannot_determine:3). This is the most decision-relevant finding in the dossier. All three mockups were drawn from memory rather than from engine output, so their scores reflect copy that is fiction, not layout.

Backend engineer, critical #3: /v1/ask returns `partial` for 'When is our AGM due?'. The flagship 'Answered: By 30 Sep 2026' cannot be produced today. Either an agm.py-backed figure route gets built, or no mockup may show that answer.

Legal accuracy auditor, critical #1 and the three customer personas: s.173(1) 'Met' while s.2(85) is 'Can't tell' is wrong in law and wrong against obligations.py _decide_board. All four practitioner voices named this as the trust-killer, so it has to be a gating fix, not a polish item.

Legal auditor and personas on s.96(1): an 'Answered' label that ignores the fifteen-month limb, the Registrar extension proviso and the s.101 21-clear-days notice consequence is dangerous advice four days out. The alert should have been the notice deadline three weeks earlier.

Legal auditor on s.137(2)/s.92(4) backstops: the engine already implements 'should have been held' (obligations.py _decide_aoc4 lines ~429-469), so the UI is throwing away the most useful date it has.
Usability researcher critical #1 and every persona: B's date control silently ignores Watch and Draft. In a product whose pitch is 'as of a date', that disqualifies B's shell.

Product strategist, critical #2, and all three customer personas: single-company scope is the real dealbreaker. The CS (40 clients), the GC (13 entities) and the partner (DD targets plus subsidiaries) each said independently that they stop evaluating without a portfolio view.

Trust/privacy reviewer, criticals #1 and #2: an OFAC 'no match' shown with the heaviest 'met' tick, and a 'similar name' IBBI insolvency match the backend deliberately cannot produce, are defamation and false-clearance risks. Feed licences are also LICENCE_UNVERIFIED, so the engine refuses to serve them.
Accessibility specialist, critical #1, and the frontend lead: no mockup has a 360px frame. This is cheap to require and it eliminates B's shell on its own.
Interaction critic, critical #1: the ServiceError state is undesigned, and PLAN_13's dashed ServiceError border collides with the dashed abstain grey. Fix it before build.
Brand guardian, critical #1: gold-muted #9F743B is spent on the 'not met' chip. Agree, and it is a one-line fix.

challenge.target: My own Round 1 critical #1 (the moat abstains everywhere because SOURCE_880='UNRESOLVED')
challenge.argument: I was wrong. Re-reading checker/prescribed_thresholds.py lines 101-107, SOURCE_880 is only the source string shown on an UNSERVABLE row. Serving is decided by attestation (lines 142, 201, 298), and the backend engineer's live run returned 880(E) CORROBORATED at ₹10 cr / ₹100 cr from 2025-12-01, with 700(E) CORROBORATED at ₹4 cr from 2022-09-15. The moat does not abstain; the mockups under-claim it. The conclusion flips: the hero demo can show the currency strip with real figures TODAY for 15-Sep-2022 onward. The only open question is the wording for an automated Gazette-copy match ('attested; Gazette copy matched' rather than 'checked against the Gazette').

challenge.target: Brand guardian, preferred direction (B as the frame, score 7.5)
challenge.argument: Brand fidelity is being weighted above the facts. B's frame fails 360px reflow (a 50px italic sentence and absolute-% timeline marks), has no free-text Ask, keeps no URL state, and its date control lies on two of five verbs. Every customer persona rejected it as a daily tool. A dark ink shell and one gold cursor can be applied to A's layout at almost no cost. The timeline is the brand asset; B's shell is not.

challenge.target: Accessibility specialist and frontend lead preferring C as the shell
challenge.argument: Reflow cost is real, but C's structure is a wizard, and three of the four practitioner voices called it slow or patronising. The only persona who preferred C was the week-one associate, who is explicitly not the buyer. C's step 2 'We check' trail is also fabricated: no route returns those stages (contract.md D11, and validate's rule that 'stages exist only on the document path'). A single-column reflow can be designed into A's duty table plus detail panel (stacked rows below 820px) without adopting C's step gating. Take C's glossary as an on-demand drawer; do not take its shell.

challenge.target: Backend engineer and legal auditor recommending s.177 / Rule 6 as the 'honest abstention' demo example
challenge.argument: This backfires. Three personas said a private company getting 'can't tell' on s.177 makes the tool look ignorant, because Rule 6 only prescribes public-company classes. An abstention demo must be one a practitioner respects. Better choices: s.149(3) missing director days (user-fixable), or an s.203 KMP Rules gap. Separately, prioritise a Rule 6 review so the private-company case returns 'Doesn't apply'.

challenge.target: Simulated senior partner, legal objection that _decide_aoc4 does not implement s.137(2)
challenge.argument: Factually wrong. checker/obligations.py _decide_aoc4 (lines ~429-469) explicitly handles 'the date it should have been held' when no AGM is on record. The gap is UI-only, which makes it cheaper to fix and makes the mockups' 'isn't set yet' copy less excusable.

challenge.target: Product strategist and devil's-advocate (me) cutting Drafts outright
challenge.argument: Partly overweighted. drafting.py does implement an AGM-notice template with slot provenance and named-reviewer approval, so the engine is not empty here. The honest version: cut the board-notice draft (no engine code, legally incomplete, self-certifying text) and keep at most the AGM notice behind a 'not yet available' label until a route exists. The provenance underline legend should survive and move onto answers.

challenge.target: Interaction critic: keep B's timeline but fix the cursor at today (read-only)
challenge.argument: Too timid, and it throws away the one thing both the GC and the partner said they would pay for. The engine honours as_of for thresholds and row decisions (live 2025-08-14 returns 700(E) ₹4 cr). The right rule is a per-key coverage floor: allow any date from 15-Sep-2022 for s.2(85) figures, refuse below the floor, and label section text as today's consolidation. That needs a written PLAN_13 §9 amendment. Do not ban the feature.

challenge.target: Usability researcher score A=7
challenge.argument: Too high while the sample data is wrong. A's comprehension win is partly built on false signal: an 'AGM due in 4 days' tile from a row state the engine does not produce, and 'Met' rows the engine refuses. Once the data is regenerated from the engine (10 of 15 undetermined), A's Overview tiles will look very different. Re-test comprehension after that, because a mostly-'Not known yet' sheet is the real churn risk (UX_INTERACTION_SPEC §9 falsifier).

debates.changed_my_mind: Yes, on two points. (1) My headline finding was that the currency-strip moat abstains in every state, based on SOURCE_880='UNRESOLVED'. That was wrong. The backend engineer's live run and my re-read of prescribed_thresholds.py show that 880(E) and 700(E) are served as CORROBORATED. That removes my reason to hold the UI decision, and it strengthens the case for putting a dated rupee figure on the hero screen now. (2) I preferred B (score 6) as the only differentiated idea. The debate convinced me that B's differentiation lives entirely in the timeline and the as-of control, not its shell. Its shell fails reflow, URL state, free-text Ask and cross-verb date honesty, and every buyer-side persona rejected it. I have not changed my mind on the single-company problem. It is still the biggest strategic gap, and the three independent personas confirmed it.
debates.vote: Hybrid "A-shell, engine-truth, portfolio-first": A's layout (duty table plus What we found / Still needed / The rule panel, Ask with Sources, law-change Watch), with a multi-entity portfolio home above it; B's timeline per provision, with an as-of date control limited to engine coverage floors; C's glossary as an on-demand drawer; and the 'How we got this' trail built only from response fields. Drafts, OFAC/IBBI and file upload are cut or shown as not yet available.
non_negotiables: Every sample value, row state and Ask state in the next mockup round is generated from real engine output (compliance-pack, ask, document-check, events) for the sample profile. No hand-written legal copy. A row the engine would not return may not be drawn.

No 'Met' or 'Answered' unless the engine returns APPLIES_SATISFIED or answered. s.173(1) and s.149(1) may never show Met for this company. The s.96 answer must name the fifteen-month limb and the Registrar-extension limb as not decided, and must surface the s.101 notice consequence.

One verification status per instrument, shown identically on every screen. 880(E) and 700(E) are shown as held, with a figure, instrument, effective_from and evidence_state. No 'law has changed' verdict ever rests on an unverified instrument.

The hero demo shows the s.2(85) currency strip with rupee figures (700(E) ₹4 cr, then 880(E) ₹10 cr) and a resolved answer where proviso facts allow, plus one abstention a practitioner respects (not s.177 for a private company).

The date control is honest: either it applies to every view, or each view that ignores it says so. Past dates are allowed only above the per-key coverage floor, with 'section text is today's consolidation' shown. This needs a written PLAN_13 §9 amendment before build.

A portfolio/multi-entity layer (clients or entities sorted by nearest hard deadline, with abstentions grouped by cause and split into 'we need from you' and 'Placedon still verifying') must be designed before the single-company screens are finalised, and the buyer (CS vs in-house) must be named in writing.
Show all 15 duties, with the denominator and an explicit 'not covered' list. Remove every 'every duty the Act gives' claim.
Remove the OFAC/IBBI and counterparty items, or show them as not yet available. Never use a met-style tick on any screening result. No fuzzy-name insolvency match next to a named company.
A 360px frame of the Ask partial answer and the duties table is required before sign-off, along with a designed ServiceError state that shares no dashed styling with abstention.
One status lexicon keyed to obligations.ROW_STATES and ask_contract STATES, owned in a single label table. out_of_scope gets its own style. Gold-muted is for citations only.
